m09 is Qwen3.8's worst matter at BOTH effort levels, and the incumbent scores
full marks on it. `xhigh` does not repair it. Whatever m09-capitalisation-split
asks for, more reasoning is not the answer and the older model already has it.

**Where Qwen3.8 wins, it wins on exactly F60's mechanism.** The workhorse
scores 1/5 on m07-breach-notification and 2/5 on m11-limitation-clocks - the
two matters F60 names as the hardest, both requiring a period to be WALKED.
Qwen3.8 scores 4/5 and 5/5. **So F60's theory of what discriminates is
CONFIRMED for the incumbents and FALSIFIED for Qwen3.8** (E43 prediction 4).
The mechanism still separates models; it just no longer separates this one.

**The trap evidence is the cleanest single number for a client.** The
workhorse reproduced `600` on m12 - the exact trap F60 documented, a service
credit computed on the wrong month's rate. Mistral reproduced `3,540` on m01.
**Qwen3.8 reproduced zero traps across 26 matter-answers at two effort
levels.** A model that scores six points higher AND never reproduces a planted
wrong answer is a different proposition from one that merely scores higher.

**The cost is 13x the wall time.** 2,015s against 152s for six more elements.
The workhorse answers all thirteen matters in under three minutes. That is the
trade in one line, and it is the same trade as every other row today.

**Verdict input.** For legal work where the answer is checked, Qwen3.8 at
`low`. For legal work where speed matters and someone reviews the output
anyway, the workhorse at 81.5% in 152s is not embarrassing - and it is better
than Qwen3.8 on three of thirteen matters. This is the first instrument that
supports a genuine "it depends" rather than a clean adopt.

### E39 RESULT - the coding baseline, and it changes the coding verdict from "no data" to "it depends"

Same eight expert tasks, same build, same `-c 32768`, same `max_tokens 24576`,
same memory and exec bounds.

| arm | pass | wall | completion tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8 `off` | 3/8 | 1,051.1s | 12,472 |
| Qwen3.8 `low` | 5/8 (1 truncated) | 6,363.4s | 76,116 |
| **Qwen3.8 `medium`** | **7/8** | 6,223.1s | 74,796 |
| **Qwen3-Coder-30B (incumbent)** | **3/8** | **66.0s** | 5,008 |

**Qwen3.8 at `medium` more than doubles the incumbent: 7/8 against 3/8.** On
the coding slot the routing guide currently recommends Qwen3-Coder, and on
these eight problems it solves three.

**It costs 94x the wall time.** 6,223s against 66s. The incumbent finishes all
eight tasks in about a minute; Qwen3.8 takes an hour and three quarters.

| task | Qwen3.8 `medium` | Qwen3-Coder |
|---|---|---|
| glob_match | **pass** | wrong |
| round_decimal | **pass** | wrong |
| kmerge | pass | pass |
| wrap | **pass** | wrong |
| sliding_median | wrong | **pass** |
| apply_patch | pass | pass |
| interval_map | **pass** | wrong |
| parse_csv | **pass** | wrong |

**The incumbent solves the one task Qwen3.8 never solves.** `sliding_median`
fails at every Qwen3.8 effort level tried - error, wrong, wrong - and
Qwen3-Coder passes it in 257 tokens and 3.25 seconds. This is the same shape
as E43's m09-capitalisation-split, where the older model also scored full
marks on the new model's worst item. **Twice today, on two unrelated
instruments, the incumbent has been strictly better at exactly one thing.**
That is not noise and it is not a rounding error in a total; it is a
capability the new model does not have.

`sliding_median` is the task with an explicit SPEED requirement. The pattern
already recorded holds: this model handles well-specified self-contained
problems and struggles when the requirement is about efficiency rather than
correctness. Qwen3-Coder, trained on code, reaches for the right data
structure immediately.

**The coding verdict is therefore CONDITIONAL, not adopt.** Qwen3.8 is better
at correctness on hard problems by more than a factor of two, at 94x the wall
time, and it is worse at the one problem where the answer had to be efficient.
For a batch of hard problems where correctness is what matters, it is the
better tool. For interactive coding, 94x is disqualifying on its own, and the
incumbent already covers the case Qwen3.8 misses.

**A caveat that limits all of this: eight tasks.** One task is 12.5 points,
and the difference between 7/8 and 3/8 is four tasks. This is a small
instrument and the verdict rests on it plus E33's core set, whose re-run is
in flight.

### E33 RE-RUN 2 RESULT - the budget raise rescued 2 of 5, and the other 3 are an EFFORT artifact

`--task-set core`, 15 tasks, `max_tokens 24576` (up from the original 8,192),
`thinking=default` - deliberately unchanged from the original E33 so that
`max_tokens` is the only variable. Wall 10,029s.

**11/15 pass, 3 truncated, 1 error -> 11 of 12 GRADEABLE (91.7%).**

The five tasks that truncated at 8,192 in the original run:

| task | outcome at 24,576 | tokens |
|---|---|---|
| `parse_semver` | **pass** | 9,856 |
| `word_break` | **pass** | **24,397** |
| `normalize_path` | truncated | 24,576 |
| `roman_roundtrip` | truncated | 24,576 |
| `eval_expr` | truncated | 24,576 |

**Tripling the budget rescued two of five.** `parse_semver` needed 9,856 -
more than 8,192 allowed, so the original truncation really was a budget
artifact. `word_break` finished with **179 tokens to spare** of 24,576, which
is a near-miss that a slightly smaller budget would have recorded as a
capability failure.

**But three still cap at three times the budget, and the E42 coding row says
why.** That row measured `xhigh` truncating 3 of 3 on tasks `medium` solved in
4,700 tokens, and `medium` completing all 8 with zero truncations. This re-run
is at `default`, which resolves to `xhigh`. **So the remaining truncations are
substantially an EFFORT-LEVEL artifact, not a budget one.** The original E33
diagnosis - "the budget was too small" - was half right.

**This matters for E44 arm C, and the arm is left as registered anyway.** Arm C
runs the five capped tasks at 100,000 tokens at `xhigh`, testing the
more-budget hypothesis. The evidence now favours the competing hypothesis that
LOWER EFFORT is the fix. Arm C still answers a real question - whether xhigh
ever converges given room - and its result is informative either way:
convergence at 100k means the effort level is merely expensive, while
truncation at 100k means `xhigh` does not converge on these tasks at any
budget we can afford. **A `medium` control on the same five tasks is the arm
that would settle it, and is NOT currently queued.** Recorded as a gap rather
than added mid-flight.

**Coding verdict input.** Core set 11/12 gradeable at default effort; expert
set 7/8 at `medium`. Both point the same way, and both are limited by the same
thing: on this model the reported score depends on an effort setting that most
users will never change.

### E45 AMENDMENT 1 (declared 2026-08-16 02:30, BEFORE any E45 arm runs)

**The conditional category goes from 3 tasks to 13.** At three tasks one task
was worth 33% of the category score, and E45 exists to decide whether the
routing guide's only carve-out survives. Confirming or overturning a
production routing rule on three tasks is not a measurement, it is a coin
toss with a table around it.

**Every addition is a PAIR** - one branch where the condition holds and one
where it does not. This is the whole design: a model that applies the flag
unconditionally passes the true branch and fails the false one, which is
exactly the defect E33 recorded. An unpaired task cannot distinguish that
failure from competence, which is why the original `c1`/`c2` were already a
pair and why every new one is too.

| pair | condition shape | false branch |
|---|---|---|
| c4 / c5 | a date before a threshold | c5 |
| c6 / c7 | a category read from a looked-up record | c7 |
| c8 / c9 | **whether to call a tool at all** | **c9** |
| c10 / c11 | a compound AND of two facts | c11 |
| c12 / c13 | a threshold on a figure it must compute first | c12 |

**c8/c9 is a new SHAPE, not just a new instance.** Every pre-existing
conditional task tests a flag inside a call that was always going to happen.
c9 tests whether the model declines to send an email at all when the condition
fails. In production that is the higher-stakes version - a wrongly-set title is
an edit, a wrongly-sent client email is not retractable.

**Marker words were chosen against substring collision.** EXPEDITED/ROUTINE
and URGENT/STANDARD share no substring, so a check for one cannot fire on the
other. Numeric markers were avoided where a word would do, because a number
can appear inside an unrelated figure or a date and score a hit the model did
not earn. This is the m11 key lesson applied to tool arguments.

**The graders are validated, not assumed.**
`tools/validate_tooluse_conditional.py` runs 20 synthetic respondents, each
built to trigger exactly one verdict - including the E33 defect itself and the
dangerous c9 branch - and exits non-zero if any check cannot tell a compliant
answer from its named failure. **20/20 pass.** An unvalidated grader reports a
number nobody can trust.

**Predictions 1-5 stand EXACTLY as registered.** They name `c1`, `c2` and `c3`
individually and are unaffected by tasks being added around them. Two new
predictions cover the new material, and no existing band is rewritten:

6. **The five FALSE branches as a group (c5, c7, c9, c11, c12), mean
   `success_rate`:** workhorse **0.0-0.5**; Qwen3.8 at `low` or `medium`
   **>= 0.7**. This is the generalised version of the c2 claim - if the fix is
   real it should hold across condition shapes, not just on the one branch E33
   happened to test.
7. **`c9-select-no-email` specifically, for every arm.** Registered separately
   because it is the only task where failure sends a real client
   communication, and because conditional tool SELECTION has never been
   measured on this box at all. **No band is registered for it** - there is no
   prior to set one from, and inventing a band for a shape nobody has measured
   would be the F65 error in a new place.

**Cost.** 13 tasks x 5 runs x 5 arms = 325 task-runs against the original 75.
The queue script needs no change: it selects by category, so the expanded set
is picked up automatically.

## E46: does `-c` break temperature-0 determinism? (2026-08-16, pre-registered before any run)

**Why this exists.** E44 arm A and E43 arm B put **byte-identical prompts** to
the same model at the same effort and temperature 0, and got **different
answers**:

| matter | E43 arm B | E44 arm A | delta | prompt_tokens | answer identical? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| m11-limitation-clocks | 8,046 | 8,696 | +8.1% | 668 = 668 | **NO** |
| m12-liability-cap-basis | 3,222 | 3,950 | +22.6% | 755 = 755 | **NO** |
| m13-interest-two-clocks | 6,686 | 7,441 | +11.3% | 711 = 711 | **NO** |

Same model file, same b10435 build, same `thinking=xhigh`, same
`temperature 0`, same `-np 1`, identical `prompt_tokens` on every matter -
which proves the same bytes reached the model. **F59 says local arms are
deterministic at temperature 0. On this evidence that is not unconditionally
true.**

**Exactly two variables differ**, and neither run came within 3x of either
cap:

| | E43 arm B | E44 arm A |
|---|---|---|
| `-c` | 32,768 | 131,072 |
| `max_tokens` | 24,576 | 100,000 |

**This must be ISOLATED, not attributed.** Earlier today an apparent
determinism failure between E41 n=0 and E42 know-low turned out to be eleven
rescoped questions - a ruler error, not a model result - and the reflex to
explain rather than isolate is exactly what produced it. Two variables changed
here, so no cause is claimed until one is held still.

**Why `-c` is the plausible suspect and `max_tokens` is not.** `max_tokens` is
a stop condition; at temperature 0, generation up to the cap should be
unaffected by where the cap sits, and neither run approached it. `-c` changes
KV cache allocation - on this DeltaNet hybrid, 2,048 MiB at 32,768 against
8,192 MiB at 131,072 - and a different allocation can change
floating-point reduction order, which changes logits, which changes the
argmax wherever two candidates are close. That is a mechanism; it is not yet
evidence.

**Design. One matter (m12, the cheapest at ~3,200 tokens), three cells,
`thinking=xhigh`, temperature 0.**

| cell | `-c` | `max_tokens` | isolates |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 32,768 | 24,576 | **control** - must reproduce E43 arm B |
| 2 | 131,072 | 24,576 | `-c` alone |
| 3 | 32,768 | 100,000 | `max_tokens` alone |

**Comparison is BYTE EQUALITY of the answer string**, not token count and not
score. A token count can match while the text differs; the direct comparison
is available here, so a proxy would be the wrong instrument (this is
`development-discipline.md`'s compare-like-for-like rule).

**Predictions.**

1. **Cell 1 is byte-identical to E43 arm B's m12 answer.** This is the control
   and it carries the experiment: if it FAILS, the model is not deterministic
   at a fixed config at all, F59 is wrong outright rather than
   over-generalised, and every single-run result in this repository becomes a
   sample rather than a measurement. That would be the most consequential
   finding of the programme and it would invalidate more than it explains.
2. **Cell 2 differs from cell 1.** `-c` is the cause.
3. **Cell 3 is byte-identical to cell 1.** `max_tokens` is not the cause.

**If predictions 2 and 3 both hold, F59 needs an amendment reading: local
arms are deterministic at temperature 0 FOR A FIXED `-c`, and any comparison
across different `-c` values is not byte-comparable.** That would put a
caveat on cross-config comparisons throughout this repository, including
E41's scale sweep - which is internally safe, because every arm there ran at
`-c 32768`.

**Falsifier for the whole experiment: if all three cells are byte-identical to
each other and to E43 arm B, the divergence came from something not yet
identified**, and the honest report is that a reproducible difference exists
whose cause has not been found. It would not be attributed to `-c` on the
strength of a mechanism story.

### E46 AMENDMENT 1 (declared 2026-08-16 03:15, BEFORE any E46 cell runs)

**E44 arm B arrived and answered predictions 2 and 3 before E46 could run.
Both were WRONG, and the experiment is redirected rather than run to confirm a
hypothesis the data has already killed.**

| run | `-c` | `max_tokens` | m11 | m12 | m13 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E43 arm B | 32,768 | 24,576 | 8,046 | 3,222 | 6,686 |
| E44 arm A | 131,072 | 100,000 | 8,696 | 3,950 | 7,441 |
| E44 arm B | 262,144 | 200,000 | **8,696** | **3,950** | **7,441** |

**E44 arms A and B are BYTE-IDENTICAL on all three answers** while `-c`
doubled and `max_tokens` doubled. If `-c` were the cause, 131,072 -> 262,144
would have diverged. If `max_tokens` were the cause, 100,000 -> 200,000 would
have. Neither did. **Prediction 2 (`-c` is the cause) and prediction 3 are
both refuted by data collected before the experiment started.** The registered
mechanism story about KV allocation changing reduction order was plausible,
tidy, and wrong.

Rope was also checked and ruled out directly rather than assumed: all three
runs report `rope scaling = linear`, `freq_scale_train = 1`,
`n_ctx_orig_yarn = 262144`. There is no context-dependent rope scaling to
blame.

**The real variable was in the runs all along: REQUEST SEQUENCE POSITION.** In
E43 these matters were requests **11, 12 and 13** of thirteen. In E44 they were
requests **1, 2 and 3**. The server log shows why that matters:

```
slot operator(): restored context checkpoint (pos_min = 41, pos_max = 41,
                 n_tokens = 42, n_past = 42, size = 149.626 MiB)
```

and the prompt-eval counts differ for the same prompt: m11 evaluated **618**
tokens in E43 against **668** in E44, because E43 reused 50 more tokens of
cached prefix from the request before it. llama-server reuses KV cache across
requests, so **an answer depends on what ran before it in the same server
session.** Once m11 diverges, m12 and m13 inherit a different cache state.

**This is consistent with every data point, which the `-c` story was not:**
same sequence and different config gives identical output (arms A vs B);
different sequence gives different output (E43 vs E44).

**Redesigned cells. One variable - sequence position - at E43's exact config
(`-c 32768`, `max_tokens 24576`, `thinking=xhigh`).**

| cell | matters run | m12 is request | tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | m12 alone | 1st | baseline |
| 2 | m11, m12, m13 | 2nd | does position alone change the answer |
| 3 | all 13 | 12th | **must byte-reproduce E43 arm B** |

**Cell 3 is the control that now carries the experiment.** Identical config
AND identical sequence must give an identical answer. If it does, determinism
holds for a fixed (config + request history) and F59 needs only a scope note.
If it does NOT, the model is not reproducible run to run and every single-run
number in this repository is a sample, which would be far more consequential.

**Revised predictions.**

1. **Cell 3's m12 answer is byte-identical to E43 arm B's m12.** The control.
2. **Cell 1's m12 differs from cell 3's m12.** Sequence position is the cause.
3. **Cell 2's m12 differs from cell 1's** and may or may not match cell 3 -
   no band registered, because whether two prior requests reproduce the cache
   state of eleven is not something any evidence here constrains, and
   inventing a band for it would be the F65 error again.

**Scope if this holds.** It does NOT invalidate any score in this repository.
Every comparison made so far ran its arms with the same request sequence -
E43's four arms each ran the same 13 matters in the same order, E41's sweep
ran the same 12 questions - so all within-experiment comparisons remain
like-for-like. What it forbids is comparing a single item's answer ACROSS runs
with different request histories, which is exactly the comparison that raised
the question.

### E44 arm C, partial: `normalize_path` answers the whole experiment

**The single most decisive result of the budget probe, recorded before arm C
finishes because it settles the question the owner asked.**

| run | budget | outcome | tokens | seconds |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E33 original | 8,192 | truncated | 8,192 | - |
| E33 RE-RUN 2 | 24,576 | truncated | 24,576 | 2,080.9 |
| **E44 arm C1** | **100,000** | **`no_code`** | **51,845** | **4,603.9** |

**Given twelve times the budget it originally capped at, it did NOT truncate.
It generated 51,845 tokens over 77 minutes, stopped of its own accord, and
produced no code at all.**

**The two earlier truncations were masking this, not causing it.** For two runs
the diagnosis was "the budget is too small" and the fix was to raise it. Raise
it far enough and the real behaviour appears: on this task at `xhigh` the model
does not converge. It was never one cap away from an answer.

E44's registration anticipated this exact outcome and named it a result rather
than a failure:

> If the toughest matters produce 100,000 tokens of reasoning and no answer,
> that is the finding - it says maximum effort on this model does not converge,
> which is far more useful than a score.

**It also retires a hypothesis the programme has been carrying all day.** The
E33 story was that five tasks truncated because 8,192 was too small. Two of
them (`parse_semver`, `word_break`) really were budget-limited and now pass.
`normalize_path` was not, and no budget we can afford will fix it.

**This makes the missing `medium` control decision-grade rather than tidy.**
`normalize_path` is a CORE-set task, and the E42 coding row that found `medium`
strictly better ran the EXPERT set - so **`normalize_path` has never been run
at `medium`**. Every observation of it is at `xhigh` or the template default
that resolves to `xhigh`. The competing hypothesis is now sharp:

- **If `medium` solves it quickly**, the entire E33 truncation story was an
  effort-level artifact misdiagnosed as a budget problem for a month, and the
  fix is a setting rather than a bigger machine.
- **If `medium` also fails to converge**, the task is genuinely beyond this
  model and the effort level is irrelevant.

Both readings are useful and they are cheaply separable, so the control is
**being queued now** (E47) rather than logged as a gap for a third time.

**Prediction 5 tracking:** registered "at least 3 of the 5 capped tasks return
`stop` instead of `length`". `parse_semver` yes, `normalize_path` yes
(`no_code` is a stop, not a cap). 2 of 2 so far - the prediction is about
escaping the cap, and both did, though only one produced an answer.

## E47: is the E33 "truncation" story an EFFORT artifact? (2026-08-16, pre-registered before any run)

**Why this exists.** `normalize_path` truncated at 8,192, truncated at 24,576,
and at 100,000 produced 51,845 tokens of reasoning and no code. Every one of
those observations is at `xhigh` or at the template default, which resolves to
`xhigh`. **The five E33-capped tasks have never been run at `medium`**, and the
E42 coding row measured `medium` as strictly better than every other level on
the expert set - 7/8, zero truncations, in fewer tokens than `low`.

**Config.** `tools/run_coding_eval.py --task-set core --only
parse_semver,normalize_path,roman_roundtrip,word_break,eval_expr`,
`--thinking medium`, `--ctx 32768`, `--max-tokens 24576`, b10435,
temperature 0. **Deliberately the E33 RE-RUN 2 config with ONE variable
changed**, so any difference is attributable to effort and nothing else.

24,576 rather than 100,000 on purpose: the question is whether `medium`
converges inside a budget `xhigh` could not, and giving it four times as much
would confound the comparison it exists to make.

**Predictions. Bands set high, per the standing correction - mine have sat
below the measured result six times in this programme.**

1. **At least 4 of the 5 tasks return `finish_reason: stop`** at `medium`
   within 24,576. At `xhigh` three of them cap at that budget.
2. **`normalize_path` produces code** - any outcome other than `no_code` or
   `truncated`. It need not be correct; the claim is that it converges.
3. **Total tokens for the five tasks at `medium` is under 60,000**, against
   `xhigh` spending 24,576 on three of them alone plus 51,845 on
   `normalize_path` at the larger budget.
4. **At least 3 of 5 PASS.** This is the strongest claim and the one I would
   least defend.

**Falsifier: if `normalize_path` still fails to produce code at `medium`, the
effort hypothesis is dead for this task** and it is simply beyond the model.
That is a clean answer too, and it would mean the routing guide should say so
rather than implying a setting fixes it.

**What turns on this.** If prediction 2 holds, then a defect this repository
has recorded as a token-budget problem since July - and re-ran twice to fix -
was a reasoning-effort setting the whole time, and the E33 findings need a note
saying so.

## E48: the long-context ladder - E41 saturated at 8% of trained context, so go the rest of the way (2026-08-16, pre-registered before any run)

**Why this exists.** E41 swept the L3 pack at 0, 4 and 9 distractors and
returned **12/12 at every size with zero `wrong_document`**. Its registered
falsifier fired, and its own text records what that obliges: *"the boundary has
not been found rather than that there isn't one - the next probe would have to
go further out"*. This is that probe.

The number that makes it necessary: Qwen3.8's trained context is **262,144
tokens**, and the largest pack ever put to it in this repo is E41's n=9 at
**21,217** - **8.1%**. Every claim this programme makes about knowledge work
rests on packs that fit in a twelfth of what the model is built to read. The
driving question is whether this box does real professional work, and real
engagement folders are not three pages.

**ONE VARIABLE CHANGES: the size of the haystack.** The twelve questions,
their reasoning and their keys are derived from `QUESTIONS_L2` in code, and
`tools/validate_ps_eval_l3.py` asserts that equality mechanically. Re-run
2026-08-16 with the extended corpus: it still passes, 119 distractors defined,
**zero distractor/real figure clashes**, and all three synthetic respondents
still separate (`PERFECT` 12 correct, `WRONG_DOCUMENT` 9 wrong_document,
`VAGUE` 11 wrong).

### The corpus extension, and the proof it did not disturb E41

`spikes/ps-eval/corpus_l3.py` grew from 9 distractor agreements to **119**,
enough for a pack of ~244K tokens. Three things were done to keep E41's arms
usable as the baseline of this ladder rather than merely comparable:

1. **The nine original specs are literal and untouched.** The extension only
   adds ids.
2. **`build_pack_l3` now selects in DECLARATION order, not sorted order.** This
   is a defect fix, not a preference: the selection was `sorted(DISTRACTORS)[:n]`,
   a STRING sort, under which `"DIS-10"` precedes `"DIS-02"`. The moment the
   corpus passed nine agreements that would have silently changed which
   distractors every small pack contains - including E41's - and no score would
   have shown it.
3. **Byte-identity is asserted, not assumed.** The n=0, 4 and 9 packs were
   sha256'd before the change and re-hashed after:

| n | chars | sha256 (before == after) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 13,221 | `b93d23d1…` IDENTICAL |
| 4 | 49,076 | `9a700a42…` IDENTICAL |
| 9 | 93,920 | `582cb8e5…` IDENTICAL |

**The new distractors are combinatorial (22 Irish place names x 5 trades), not
typed out.** 110 hand-written tuples is 110 chances to reuse a real figure, and
that is the one error no score would reveal - a distractor sharing the real
500,000 cap makes a wrong-document answer grade as *correct*. Figures are
derived by index arithmetic that cannot leave `FIGURE_RANGES`, supplier names
are unique by construction, and the import-time disjointness assertion still
runs. Generation is a reason to trust the input, not a reason to drop the check.

**The interleave was rebuilt so the real documents stay buried.** Appending 110
distractors after `POL-3.1` would have put every real document in the first 8%
of the pack and turned the tier back into a reading-order test. Eleven
insertion points spread the extension either side of the real documents, filled
round-robin so any prefix is spread rather than front-loaded. Measured:

| n | pack chars | est. tokens | MSA-2024 sits | last real doc |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 9 | 93,920 | 21,217 (measured) | 17.6% in | 94.1% |
| 29 | 273,223 | ~61,700 | 18.9% in | 94.6% |
| 59 | 542,144 | ~122,500 | 19.4% in | 92.5% |
| 119 | 1,079,950 | ~244,000 | 18.1% in | 91.3% |

Token estimates use **4.427 chars/token, E41's MEASURED ratio on this exact
corpus** - not a constant. They are estimates and are labelled as such; the
run records the real figure. This is the E41 AMENDMENT 1 lesson: a chars-based
estimate was wrong by 4,392 tokens there and must never again decide whether a
pack fits.

### The config change, declared (Rule 8)

**`-c` moves from 32,768 to 262,144** for every rung. It has to - n=59 alone
needs ~126,600. Naming it because it is a config difference, and per Rule 8 a
benchmark measures a config.

**This does not confound the ladder, and that is measured rather than assumed.**
E44 arms A and B put byte-identical prompts to `-c 131,072` and `-c 262,144`
and returned **byte-identical answers on all three matters** while both `-c`
and `max_tokens` doubled. `-c` is not an output variable on this model. The
n=9 rung re-runs E41's exact pack at the new `-c` as the control that says so
on this task family too.

`thinking=low` on every rung, matching E41 AMENDMENT 1, so the ladder is
continuous with its baseline. `max_tokens` 4,096, temperature 0, `-np 1`,
b10435, full-offload gate passing.

**KV cost is known-safe.** `-c 262144` on this DeltaNet hybrid carries KV for
only 16 of 64 layers and totalled ~31 GiB in E44 arm B, which ran to completion.
That is under the ~60 GiB suballocator-deadlock threshold in
`docs/memory-edge-deadlock.md`.

### A silent-truncation guard now exists, because this experiment could not exist without it

`tools/run_ps_eval.py` had **no context preflight**. An oversized pack would
have been truncated from the front by llama-server, the model would have
answered from a folder whose opening documents were gone, and it would have
graded as a capability failure - F20 exactly, at 244K tokens where nobody would
spot it by eye. Added `count_tokens()` (the SERVER's tokenizer, never a
chars estimate) and `assert_context_fits()`, which refuses to run when
prompt + `max_tokens` exceeds `-c` and reports the overflow in tokens. The
measured headroom is recorded in every output as `context_preflight`.

**The same gap exists in three sibling runners** - `run_coding_eval.py`,
`run_writing_eval.py` and `spikes/closed-record/run_matters.py`, all of which
have run `max_tokens` of 100,000 or more against a 131,072 context. It is NOT
being fixed in this pass, deliberately: queues 14, 13, 12, 9 and 11 are chained
to invoke those exact scripts unattended over the next several hours, and an
untested edit to a script that cannot be smoke-tested while the GPU is busy is
how a queued arm dies at 3am. TODO: add the preflight to those three.
Why: same silent-truncation class, and two of them run within 31,072 tokens of
their context ceiling. Trigger: this registration; do it when the queue drains
and each can be smoke-tested live. `tooluse_harness_v2.py` is not at risk -
`max_tokens` is 1,200.

### Rungs

n=9 (control), 29, 59, 119. Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M only; the workhorse control is
not repeated because E41 already measured it degrading faster over the span
where both fit, and it has no `reasoning_effort` equivalent to hold constant.

### Predictions (registered before any rung runs). The FIELD is named in each.

1. **`correct` at n=9 is 12/12**, reproducing E41 exactly at the new `-c`.
   This is the harness-and-config control, not a model test: a different score
   means the `-c` change, the declaration-order fix or the preflight altered
   the instrument, and the whole ladder is void until that is explained.
2. **`correct` at n=29 is 10-12.**
3. **`correct` at n=59 is 8-12.**
4. **`correct` at n=119 is 5-11, and strictly below n=9.** 93% of trained
   context, twelve times the largest pack this model has ever been given here.
5. **`wrong_document` is at least 1 at n=119.** E41 registered this at n=9 and
   measured 0. Registering it again 12x further out: if scale degrades
   retrieval at all, it should surface as confident retrieval from the wrong
   agreement rather than as declining to answer.
6. **`multihop` is the lowest-scoring category at n=119.** M1-M3 each need
   facts from two or three documents, so each is another chance to land in the
   wrong agreement, and the documents are now up to a megabyte apart.
7. **Median question `wall_s` at n=119 is at least 3x the n=9 median of 47.8s,
   i.e. >= 143s.** The pack is the prompt PREFIX and the question is appended
   last, so all twelve questions reuse one prefill; the cost should therefore
   land as a large first request rather than proportionally on all twelve.

**Not predicted:** which individual questions fail.

**Calibration note, stated because it keeps happening.** My registered bands
have sat BELOW the measured result six times in this programme. Bands 2, 3 and
4 above are deliberately wider on the upside than my instinct, and if they are
still too low that is itself the finding.

**Known limitation, named up front.** With 119 distractors the set of figures
that identify a wrong-document answer is large, so a coincidental arithmetic
slip could in principle be labelled `wrong_document`. The ranges are wide
(18,750-37,400 and 150,000-415,000 against 119 values) so collision is
unlikely, but a `wrong_document` verdict at n=119 will be checked against the
cited document id before it is reported as retrieval failure.

**Falsifier for the whole experiment: if `correct` at n=119 is 12/12 with zero
`wrong_document`, scale is not a boundary anywhere inside this model's trained
context.** That is the fourth instrument this model has exhausted, and the
honest report is no longer "the boundary has not been found" - at 93% of
trained context with the answers a megabyte apart, retrieval-under-scale
becomes a MEASURED STRENGTH and the routing guide should say so in those words.

### E44 arm C2 RESULT - `interval_map` burns the whole 100,000, and `medium` had already solved it in 14,916

`thinking=xhigh`, `max_tokens 100,000`, `-c 131072`, b10435.

| | outcome | finish | completion tokens | seconds |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| interval_map | `truncated` | **length** | **100,000** | **9,984.7** |

Reported separately rather than folded into prediction 5, as AMENDMENT 2
required. **It joins the non-converging group**, which is now three of the six
arm C tasks: `normalize_path` (stops at 51,845 with no code),
`roman_roundtrip` (100,000, length) and `interval_map` (100,000, length).

**But `interval_map` is not like the other two, and this is the finding.** It
is the one task in the group that has already been SOLVED on this box, and the
run that solved it was cheaper on every axis:

| level | max_tokens | outcome | completion tokens | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| off | 24,576 | timeout | - | - |
| low | 24,576 | `truncated` (length) | 24,576 | 2,082.8s |
| **medium** | **24,576** | **pass** (stop) | **14,916** | **1,247.3s** |
| xhigh | 100,000 | `truncated` (length) | 100,000 | 9,984.7s |

Same model, same build, same task, same grader. **`medium` returns a correct
answer in 14,916 tokens and 21 minutes. `xhigh` fails to return one in 100,000
tokens and 2 hours 46 minutes** - 6.7x the tokens and 8.0x the wall to produce
nothing. `-c` differs between the rows (32,768 vs 131,072) and is not the
cause: E44 arms A and B measured byte-identical answers across a `-c` doubling
on identical prompts.

**The curve is non-monotonic with a peak in the middle.** off fails, low
fails, medium passes, xhigh fails. That is the opposite shape to F69, which
found no middle setting on knowledge work - there, `off` failed and low,
medium and xhigh were all 12/12. So reasoning effort is not one axis with one
best value: **on knowledge work more effort is free and harmless, and on
coding there is an optimum that maximum effort overshoots.** F69's scope was
deliberately confined to knowledge work; this is why.

**E44 is now complete.** Arms A and B (matters at 100k and 200k) returned
byte-identical answers and refuted the `-c`/`max_tokens` hypothesis. Arm C
cost **8.3 hours and 319,806 completion tokens to resolve six programming
problems, three successfully**, at the model's maximum reasoning setting.

**What this does to E47.** E47 was registered to decide whether the E33
"budget" story is an effort artifact, and for `interval_map` the answer is
already on the record: a task the group calls budget-limited was solved at a
quarter of the budget by lowering the effort. E47 now asks whether that
generalises to the other five. It started at 11:28:56 and its registration is
unchanged - this paragraph is an expectation, not an amendment, and no
prediction is being edited after the fact.


### E47 RESULT - the "budget" story was an EFFORT ARTIFACT. All five pass at `medium`, in 15 minutes.

`thinking=medium`, `max_tokens 24,576`, `-c 32768`, b10435 - E33 RE-RUN 2's
config with exactly one variable changed.

| task | E33-era (xhigh) | E44 arm C1 (xhigh, 100k) | **E47 (medium, 24,576)** | tokens | seconds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| parse_semver | capped | pass (13,836 tok) | **pass** | 1,486 | 121.1 |
| normalize_path | capped | `no_code` (51,845 tok) | **pass** | 1,469 | 121.3 |
| roman_roundtrip | capped | `truncated` (100,000 tok) | **pass** | 2,210 | 181.3 |
| word_break | capped | pass (21,770 tok) | **pass** | 3,116 | 255.6 |
| eval_expr | capped | pass (32,355 tok) | **pass** | 2,652 | 217.9 |

**5/5 pass. 10,933 completion tokens. 897 seconds.**

Against arm C1 on the identical five tasks: **3/5, 219,806 tokens, 19,977
seconds**. Lowering the effort setting produced **two more correct answers
using 20x fewer tokens and 22x less wall clock**.

**The two tasks arm C1 called unfixable-at-any-budget both pass here.**
`normalize_path` produced no code after 51,845 tokens at `xhigh` and produces
working code in **1,469** at `medium`. `roman_roundtrip` consumed the entire
100,000-token budget without stopping at `xhigh` and finishes in **2,210** at
`medium` - 45x fewer tokens, and the difference between a wrong answer and a
right one.

**What this retracts.** Since 2026-07 these five tasks have been carried as
"capped" and explained as a token-budget limitation. The explanation was wrong.
They were never budget-limited; they were run at the wrong reasoning setting.
Every raise of `max_tokens` in that period - 8,192 to 24,576 to 100,000 - was
treating the symptom, and the last of those cost 5.6 hours to demonstrate that
maximum effort cannot solve problems that a middle setting solves in 15
minutes. E44 arm C2 had already shown this for `interval_map`; E47 shows it
generalises to all five.

**This is the same shape as the E44 arm C2 curve and it is now the third
independent confirmation**: on coding, reasoning effort has an optimum in the
middle and `xhigh` overshoots it. E42's coding row found `medium` 7/8 and
strictly dominant; E44 arm C2 found `medium` solving what `xhigh` could not;
E47 finds `medium` solving all five that `xhigh` failed or laboured over.

**Practical consequence, and it is large.** Qwen3.8's chat template resolves
`reasoning_effort` to **xhigh when the caller says nothing**. So the default
setting is the one that fails these tasks and burns hours doing it. Any
adoption of this model for coding MUST set `reasoning_effort: medium`
explicitly. That is now the single most actionable line in the programme.


### E46 RESULT - the control REPRODUCED, and request SEQUENCE POSITION is the cause

Every cell ran E43 arm B's exact config (`thinking=xhigh`, `max_tokens 24,576`,
temperature 0). Only the number of requests preceding `m12` changed. The
`m12` prompt is byte-identical in all three - `prompt_tokens` is **755**
everywhere.

| cell | m12 is request | completion tokens | seconds | answer sha256 | chars |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1: m12 alone | 1 of 1 | 3,645 | 301.0 | `23038d6b0a77bbfc` | 2,858 |
| 2: m11,m12,m13 | 2 of 3 | 3,950 | 327.7 | `8b87187d40cabe0b` | 2,657 |
| **3: all 13 (CONTROL)** | **12 of 13** | **3,222** | **268.1** | **`9979e5aa040e731b`** | **2,506** |
| E43 arm B (the original) | 12 of 13 | **3,222** | - | **`9979e5aa040e731b`** | - |

**PREDICTION 1 HELD, exactly. Cell 3 is BYTE-IDENTICAL to E43 arm B** - same
sha256, same completion-token count. Reproducing the sequence position
reproduces the answer bit for bit.

**Three sequence positions, one prompt, THREE DIFFERENT ANSWERS at temperature
0.** This confirms the amended hypothesis and closes the question E43-vs-E44
opened.

**Mechanism.** llama-server reuses the KV cache prefix shared with the
preceding request. How much of the prompt is recomputed - and in what batch
boundaries - therefore depends on what was asked before it. Floating-point
accumulation is not associative, so a differently-chunked prefill yields
marginally different logits, and at temperature 0 a marginal difference is
enough to flip a token choice, after which the generations diverge. Nothing
here is random: each sequence is individually reproducible, which is why cell
3 reproduced.

**What this corrects.** F59 recorded local temperature-0 runs as deterministic.
That is true only in the sense the tests established it - the same sequence
re-run gives the same answers. It is NOT true that a given prompt has a single
temperature-0 answer on this server. Any comparison that puts the same prompt
at different positions in different arms is comparing two things, and the
earlier E43-vs-E44 divergence I nearly wrote up as a `-c` effect was exactly
that. Recorded as F70.

**Operational rule this produces:** an arm's matter ORDER is part of its
config. Two arms are comparable only if each prompt occupies the same
sequence position in both. E41's scale sweep and E43's four arms both satisfy
this by construction; it was never checked before, it was luck.

### E42 writing row CLOSED - `xhigh` does converge on plain_english, given 4x the budget

### E40 RESULT - the writing comparison arms, and Qwen3.8 wins the one that matters

Seven tasks, seven kinds, same grader, same harness.

| model | clean | outcomes | negative retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Qwen3.8 (medium)** | **6/7** | 6 correct, 1 length_violation | **1.0** |
| Mistral-Small-24B | 3/7 | 3 correct, 1 dropped_negative, 3 length_violation | 0.8 |
| workhorse | 2/7 | 2 correct, **3 dropped_negative**, 2 style_violation | **0.4** |

Fabrication is 0/7 on all three - none of them invents facts.

**`dropped_negative` is the column to read, not the clean count.** It counts
answers that quietly omitted an adverse finding they were given. For advisory
work that is the dangerous failure mode: a fluent summary that lost the caveat
reads better than one that kept it, and is worse. **The workhorse dropped 3 of
the negatives it was handed, retaining 40%. Qwen3.8 dropped none.**

That is the clearest task-shaped case for Qwen3.8 in the programme so far, and
it is not about score - the workhorse writes acceptable prose fast. It is that
the incumbent silently drops bad news and the candidate does not.


### E48 RESULT - two rungs clean, then the GPU DIES. The ceiling found is the BOX, not the model.

| rung | pack chars | prompt tokens (measured) | headroom in -c | `correct` | citations | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| n=9 (control) | 93,920 | **21,228** | 236,820 | **12/12** | 11/12 | clean |
| n=29 | 273,223 | **60,315** | 197,733 | **12/12** | **12/12** | clean |
| n=59 | 542,144 | **118,911** | 139,137 | - | - | **GPU device lost** |
| n=119 | 1,079,950 | **236,122** | 21,926 | - | - | **GPU device lost** |

**PREDICTION 1 HELD.** n=9 is 12/12, reproducing E41 exactly at `-c 262144`
against E41's `-c 32768`. The control does its job: the `-c` change, the
declaration-order fix and the new preflight did not move the instrument.

**PREDICTION 2 HELD at the top of its band.** n=29 registered 10-12, measured
**12**, with citations improving to 12/12. Every category stayed at 100%
(`date_effective` 3/3, `revocation` 2/2, `precedence` 2/2, `multihop` 3/3,
`exhaustive` 1/1, `underspecified` 1/1).

**So at ~60K tokens - a folder of thirty competing agreements, 273,000
characters - this model still answers every question correctly and cites the
right document every time.** That is nearly triple the largest pack ever put to
it before today, and it did not degrade at all.

**PREDICTIONS 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 ARE UNRESOLVED, and not because the model
failed.** The n=59 and n=119 rungs never produced an answer:

```
radv/amdgpu: The CS has been cancelled because the context is lost.
ggml_vulkan: device lost on Vulkan0
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'vk::DeviceLostError'
```

llama-server died **during prompt processing**, before generating a token:

| rung | prompt tokens | died at n_tokens | prefill rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| n=59 | 118,911 | **96,286** | - |
| n=119 | 236,122 | **110,622** | **49.57 tok/s** |

**This is an infrastructure ceiling and must not be reported as a capability
result.** All twelve questions in both rungs are `transport_failed`, which is
what that outcome exists to distinguish. Scoring them 0/12 would be the F20
error at a scale nobody would catch by eye - which is precisely why the
preflight and the `transport_failed` outcome were built before the run rather
than after.

**What the two crash points tell us.** The device is lost somewhere between
**96,286 and 110,622 tokens of single-request prefill** - not at a fixed
boundary, which is the signature of a driver-level compute cancellation rather
than a clean allocation limit. Note it is NOT out-of-memory: `-c 262144` was
allocated successfully in both runs and the n=29 rung ran fine at the same
`-c`. It is also NOT the amdgpu suballocator deadlock in
`docs/memory-edge-deadlock.md` - the box did not wedge, the process died
cleanly, and five further runs completed afterwards.

**Prefill at 49.57 tok/s is the other number worth having.** At that rate a
110,000-token prefill takes 37 minutes before the model emits anything. Even
if the crash were fixed tomorrow, single-request packs of that size are not a
practical working mode on this hardware.

**Measured against the ~60 GiB deadlock threshold, KV was never the problem**,
and my own registration's estimates were sound: I predicted ~61,700 /
~122,500 / ~244,000 tokens and measured 60,315 / 118,911 / 236,122 - all
within 3.5%, all conservative in the safe direction. The E41 chars/token
lesson held.

**What the falsifier says.** It was registered as "if `correct` at n=119 is
12/12 with zero `wrong_document`, scale is not a boundary". n=119 did not run,
so the falsifier is **not fired and not refuted** - it is unresolved, and I am
not going to launder an infrastructure crash into either answer. What CAN be
said on evidence: **the model shows zero degradation out to 60,315 tokens**,
which is the largest pack it has ever been correctly measured on, and the
boundary between there and its trained 262,144 is currently unreachable on this
box.

**Next step, registered here before it runs.** The device-lost hypothesis to
test first is batch size: llama-server defaults to `n_batch 2048` / `n_ubatch
512`, and a long-running compute dispatch is the usual cause of a RADV context
cancellation. E48 arm B will re-run n=59 with reduced `-b`/`-ub`. If it
completes, the ceiling is a tunable and the ladder continues; if it dies at the
same place, the ceiling is the driver and the honest report is that this
hardware cannot read a 120,000-token document in one request regardless of what
the model can do. `run_ps_eval.py` needs a server-arg passthrough to do this,
which does not exist yet.

## E48 arm B: is the ~100K prefill wall a TUNABLE or the driver? (2026-08-17, pre-registered before any run)

**Why this exists.** E48's n=59 and n=119 rungs both killed the GPU during
prompt processing (F72), between 96,286 and 110,622 tokens. That is currently
recorded as a hardware ceiling, and the difference between "a hardware ceiling"
and "a setting we had wrong" is the difference between telling a client this box
cannot read a 300-page pile and telling them it can.

**The hypothesis.** A RADV context cancellation is what a driver does to a
compute dispatch that runs too long. llama-server submits prefill in `n_ubatch`
chunks, and both failing runs used the defaults - **confirmed from the
serverlog, not assumed: `n_batch = 2048`, `n_ubatch = 512`.** Quartering the
micro-batch quarters the work in each dispatch.

**ONE VARIABLE CHANGES: `-b 512 -ub 128`.** Everything else reproduces E48's
n=59 rung exactly - same pack, same 12 questions, `-c 262144`, `thinking=low`,
`max_tokens 4096`, temperature 0, b10435. The control is already measured: the
same rung at default batch died at n_tokens 96,286.

**A capability the runner did not have.** `tools/run_ps_eval.py` had no way to
pass server flags, so `--server-extra` was added, recorded in the output as
`server_extra` so an arm that changed a serving flag cannot be silently compared
against one that did not (Rule 8). Smoke-tested before this registration:
flags confirmed reaching the server as `n_batch = 512, n_ubatch = 128`, and
the value round-tripped into the result JSON.

**A confound named in advance, because F70 predicts it.** Changing `-ub` changes
how prefill is chunked, and F70 established that different chunking gives
different floating-point accumulation and therefore, at temperature 0, can flip
a token. **So arm B's ANSWERS are not expected to be byte-identical to a
default-batch run even where both complete.** The primary measurement here is
therefore whether it completes, not what it scores. The smoke test already
showed this: L3 n=0 at `thinking=off` scored 9/12 with the reduced batch where
the equivalent default-batch cell scored 8/12. Same direction, different
number, exactly as F70 says it should be.

### Predictions (registered before the run). The FIELD is named in each.

1. **PRIMARY: the count of `outcome == "transport_failed"` at n=59 is 0** - the
   run completes. This is the whole experiment. Registered as a positive
   because quartering the dispatch is the standard mitigation for a watchdog
   cancellation, though I hold it at moderate confidence rather than high.
2. **If it completes, `correct` is 10-12.** Not pinned at 12: scale did not
   degrade this model at n=29 (12/12), but F70's chunking effect can move
   individual answers.
3. **Prefill throughput is LOWER than the 49.57 tok/s measured at default
   batch**, read from the serverlog's `prompt processing ... tokens per second`.
   Band: **15-45 tok/s**. Smaller dispatches are less efficient; the trade is
   throughput for survival.
4. **If it does NOT complete, the serverlog's `stop processing: n_tokens` lands
   within ±20% of 96,286** (77,029 to 115,543). A death at a substantially
   different point would mean the mechanism is neither batch size nor a fixed
   token limit, and I would say so rather than fit a story to it.

**Not predicted:** which individual questions change answer relative to the
default-batch runs.

**Arm B2, conditional and registered now so it is not invented later:** if arm B
completes, the same flags run at n=119 (236,122 tokens). That tests whether the
mitigation scales or merely moves the wall. If arm B fails, B2 does not run.

**Falsifier: if arm B dies within ±20% of 96,286 tokens, batch size is not the
mechanism**, F72 stands as written, and the honest report to a client is that
this hardware cannot read a document of that size in one request regardless of
what the model is capable of. That is a useful answer, not a failed experiment.


## E49: separating `-b` from `-ub` - which flag actually moved the prefill wall? (2026-08-17, pre-registered before any run)

**Why this exists, and it is a flaw in my own arm B.** E48 arm B cleared the
F72 prefill wall, but it changed **two** flags at once: `-b` 2048 -> 512 and
`-ub` 512 -> 128. So "the wall is a tunable" is established and **"`-ub` is the
tunable" is not** - arm B cannot attribute its own result. This is the
comparison-integrity rule applied to my own work: one variable, or you have
measured a combination and named it after one of its parts.

**A second thing arm B did not predict and cannot explain.** Prefill ran at
**~132 tok/s against the default configuration's 49.57** - about 2.7x FASTER,
where I registered 15-45 tok/s on the reasoning that smaller dispatches cost
efficiency. Being wrong about the direction means the mechanism is not what I
assumed. Faster AND more stable together points at memory pressure rather than
a dispatch-duration watchdog, but that is a hypothesis and this experiment is
what would support or kill it.

### Design: a 2x2 on the two flags, plus two cells to locate the boundary

Same pack throughout - L3 at 59 distractors, 118,911 prompt tokens, the exact
configuration that died at 96,286. `-c 262144`, `thinking=low`,
`max_tokens 4096`, temperature 0, b10435. Only `-b` and `-ub` change.

| cell | `-b` | `-ub` | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| default | 2048 | 512 | **MEASURED (E48)**: device lost at n_tokens 96,286 |
| arm B | 512 | 128 | **MEASURED (E48b)**: survived, ~132 tok/s prefill |
| **E49-A** | **2048** | **128** | isolates `-ub` (batch left at default) |
| **E49-B** | **512** | **512** | isolates `-b` (ubatch left at default) |
| **E49-C** | 2048 | 256 | locates the boundary between 128 and 512 |
| **E49-D** | 2048 | 64 | tests whether the effect keeps going below 128 |

The four corners of the 2x2 are default, arm B, A and B. Two are already
measured, so this costs four runs rather than six.

### Predictions (registered before any cell runs). The FIELD is named in each.

1. **PRIMARY: `-ub` is the causal variable, `-b` is not.** Cell A's count of
   `outcome == "transport_failed"` is **0** (survives); cell B's is **12**
   (crashes). Reasoning: `n_ubatch` sets the actual compute dispatch submitted
   to the GPU, while `n_batch` is a logical grouping that gets split into
   ubatches, so `n_batch` should not change what any single dispatch does.
2. **Prefill throughput tracks `-ub`, not `-b`.** Read from the serverlog's
   `prompt processing ... tokens per second` at the last progress line:
   **cell A >= 100 tok/s, cell B <= 70 tok/s.**
3. **Cell C (`-ub 256`) survives**, `transport_failed` == 0. Least confident of
   the four; it is the cell that locates the boundary rather than tests the
   hypothesis.
4. **Cell D (`-ub 64`) survives, and its prefill rate is NOT materially higher
   than cell A's.** Registered band: **90-145 tok/s**. If throughput keeps
   climbing as the micro-batch keeps shrinking, the memory-pressure reading is
   incomplete and I would say so.
5. **`correct` is 10-12 in every surviving cell.** Not pinned at 12: F70
   establishes that changed prefill chunking changes floating-point
   accumulation and can flip a token at temperature 0, and every cell here
   changes the chunking.

**Not predicted:** which individual questions change answer between cells.

**Calibration note, stated because the pattern is now consistent.** Registered
bands in this programme have sat BELOW the measured result seven times,
including arm B's prefill rate two hours ago. Bands 2 and 4 above are set wider
on the upside than instinct suggests, and if they are still too low that is
itself the finding.

**Falsifier: if cell A crashes and cell B survives, `-ub` is not the mechanism
and `-b` is** - which reverses prediction 1 and would mean the relevant
quantity is total in-flight logical batch rather than dispatch size. **If BOTH
survive**, either flag alone is sufficient and the mechanism is a property of
the combination, which no single-flag story explains and which I would report
as unresolved rather than pick a winner from.

### E48 arm B RESULT - the wall is a TUNABLE. 12/12 at 118,911 tokens, and prefill got FASTER.

> **The "2.7x" figures in this entry are SUPERSEDED.** They divided rates
> taken at two different depths. See the correction below: the like-for-like
> figure is **2.51x at matched depth**, and the advantage is depth-dependent.

`-b 512 -ub 128`, everything else identical to the rung that died. 1,736.9s
total.

| | default `-b 2048 -ub 512` | **arm B `-b 512 -ub 128`** |
|---|---|---|
| Prompt tokens | 118,911 | **118,911** (identical pack) |
| Fate | device lost at n_tokens 96,286 | **completed** |
| `correct` | - (all 12 `transport_failed`) | **12/12** |
| `citation_valid` | - | **12/12** |
| Prefill rate | 49.57 tok/s | **~132-144 tok/s** |

**PREDICTION 1 HELD - the primary one.** `transport_failed` is **0**. F72's
ceiling is not a property of the hardware; it is a property of the default
micro-batch.

**PREDICTION 2 HELD at the top of its band.** Registered 10-12, measured
**12**, with every citation correct.

**PREDICTION 3 FALSIFIED, and in a direction I did not consider.** I registered
prefill throughput as LOWER than 49.57 tok/s, band 15-45, reasoning that
smaller dispatches cost efficiency. Measured **~132-144 tok/s - about 2.7x
FASTER**. There is no throughput-for-survival trade here. The smaller
micro-batch is both more stable and substantially quicker at this depth, which
means my model of the failure was wrong rather than merely mis-scaled: a pure
dispatch-duration watchdog would not also make the work go faster. Memory
pressure at `-ub 512` is the obvious candidate, and E49 is registered to test
it rather than assert it.

**This is the eighth time a registered band has sat below the result.**

### What this does to the knowledge-work claim

The zero-degradation span nearly doubles. Previously: 12/12 out to **60,315**
tokens, with everything above unreachable. Now:

| Prompt tokens | Pack | `correct` | Citations |
|---|---|---|---|
| 21,267 | 10 agreements | 12/12 | 11/12 |
| 60,354 | 30 agreements | 12/12 | 12/12 |
| **118,911** | **60 agreements, 542,144 chars** | **12/12** | **12/12** |

Sixty near-identical services agreements, roughly 300 pages, every answer
correct and every citation from the right document. The one thing to keep
attached to that number: **the first question cost 978.4s** because it pays the
whole prefill, and the remaining eleven averaged **68.4s** because they reuse
the cached prefix. That is F31's "load once, interrogate all afternoon" shape
holding at four times the depth F31 measured.

**F72 needs amending, not deleting.** The device-lost is real and reproducible
at the default flags, and anyone running this model at long context with stock
settings will hit it. What is now false is that it is a hardware ceiling.

**Arm B2 started automatically** at n=119 (236,122 tokens, 1,079,950 chars) per
the registration's conditional. If it also completes, the model has been
measured clean at 90% of its trained context.

### CORRECTION to the E48 arm B result: the speedup is 2.51x at matched depth, not 2.7x, and it is DEPTH-DEPENDENT

Recorded 2026-08-17 under the owner's standing instruction to cross-check every
number. The "2.7x faster" figure I published this morning is **wrong**, and the
error is a like-for-like failure of exactly the kind
`development-discipline.md` names.

**What I did wrong.** llama-server's `tokens per second` in the prefill progress
line is a **cumulative average, not an instantaneous rate**, so it declines as
depth grows. I took arm B's rate at one depth (~132) and the default run's rate
at a deeper one (49.57) and divided them. Two different depths, one ratio.

**The correct comparison, at matched `n_tokens`**, both runs on the identical
118,911-token pack:

| n_tokens | default tok/s | arm B tok/s | ratio | default sec | arm B sec |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 24,606 | 222.54 | 216.62 | **0.97x** | 110.6 | 113.6 |
| 45,086 | 142.64 | 194.03 | 1.36x | 316.1 | 232.4 |
| 65,566 | 92.26 | 174.93 | 1.90x | 710.7 | 374.8 |
| 86,046 | 66.47 | 156.20 | 2.35x | 1,294.4 | 550.9 |
| **94,238** | **59.20** | **148.84** | **2.51x** | **1,591.8** | **633.1** |

94,238 is the deepest point both runs reached, because the default one died
shortly after it.

**So: no advantage at all below about 25,000 tokens, and a monotonically
growing one after that, reaching 2.51x where the comparison runs out.** Every
document quoting 2.7x has been corrected.

**This makes the result MORE interesting, not less, and it is a mechanism
clue.** A fixed per-dispatch overhead would produce a constant ratio. An
advantage that is absent when the KV cache is small and grows steadily as it
fills is what **memory pressure** looks like. That is the hypothesis E49 was
registered to test, and this curve is independent support for it that arrived
before E49 ran. It does not replace E49: this is still one run against one run,
and it cannot separate `-b` from `-ub`.

**The falsification of prediction 3 stands and is unaffected.** I registered
prefill as SLOWER at 15-45 tok/s; it is faster at every depth above ~25K and
never slower than 0.97x. Only the magnitude was wrong.

### E48 arm B2 RESULT - 12/12 at 236,122 tokens. 90% of trained context, no degradation.

`-b 512 -ub 128`, `-c 262144`, `thinking=low`, the 119-distractor pack.

| | value |
|---|---|
| Prompt tokens | **236,122** (90.1% of the trained 262,144) |
| Pack | 1,079,950 chars, 120 services agreements |
| `correct` | **12/12** |
| `citation_valid` | **11/12** (N1 missed its citation; the answer was right) |
| `transport_failed` | **0** |
| Total wall | 5,352.4s |
| First question | **4,302.3s (71.7 min)** - it pays the entire prefill |
| Other eleven | mean **94.9s**, range 53.4-137.2 |

**The same rung died at n_tokens 110,622 yesterday with stock flags.** One
serving flag is the difference between a device-lost and a clean sweep.

**The scale ladder is now complete and shows no boundary anywhere inside it:**

| Prompt tokens | Agreements | `correct` | Citations |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3,675 | 1 | 12/12 | 12/12 |
| 21,267 | 10 | 12/12 | 11/12 |
| 60,354 | 30 | 12/12 | 12/12 |
| 118,911 | 60 | 12/12 | 12/12 |
| **236,122** | **120** | **12/12** | **11/12** |

Sixty-four times the smallest pack, and the score never moved. E41's falsifier
- "if `correct` at the largest scale equals `correct` at the smallest, scale is
not a boundary" - **has now fired at 90% of trained context.** The honest
report is no longer "the boundary has not been found": at this point,
retrieval-under-scale on this model is a **measured strength**, and the routing
guide should say so in those words.

**What it costs, which is the part a firm actually needs.** The first question
on a 120-agreement pile takes **71.7 minutes**. Every question after it averages
**94.9 seconds**. That ratio - **45:1** between the first question and the
rest - is the whole operational story: this is not a tool you ask one question of, it is one
you load a matter into and then work from.

**Instantaneous prefill collapses at depth, and the cumulative average hides
it.** At 210,462 tokens the log's cumulative figure was 66 tok/s while the
instantaneous rate over the preceding 2,560 tokens was **27.8 tok/s**. Anyone
sizing a job from the printed number will underestimate the tail badly.
`tools/prefill_curve.py` now derives the instantaneous rate for exactly this
reason.

**Not claimed:** that 236,122 is a limit. It is the largest pack this corpus can
build, not a measured ceiling. The remaining 26,022 tokens of trained context
are untested, and `-c 262144` leaves only 21,926 tokens of headroom after this
prompt plus its generation, so testing further needs a bigger corpus AND a model
whose trained context exceeds what we can already fill.

### E49 RESULT - `-ub` is the whole story, `-b` does nothing, and 128 is an OPTIMUM. All five predictions held.

Same 118,911-token pack in every cell, `-c 262144`, `thinking=low`. Throughput
compared at **matched depth** (n_tokens 94,238, the deepest point all six
configurations reached) using `tools/prefill_curve.py`, not by dividing
last-line rates.

| cell | `-b` | `-ub` | survived | `correct` | tok/s @94,238 | vs default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default | 2048 | 512 | **NO** - lost at 96,286 | - | 59.20 | 1.00x |
| **B** | **512** | **512** | **NO** - lost at 109,598 | - | 63.13 | 1.07x |
| C | 2048 | 256 | yes | 12/12 | 105.60 | 1.78x |
| **A** | **2048** | **128** | **yes** | **12/12** | **147.97** | **2.50x** |
| arm B | 512 | 128 | yes | 12/12 | 148.84 | 2.51x |
| D | 2048 | 64 | yes | 12/12 | 127.53 | 2.15x |

**PREDICTION 1 HELD on both halves - this was the whole experiment.** Cell A
(`-ub` lowered, `-b` left alone) has `transport_failed` **0**. Cell B (`-b`
lowered, `-ub` left alone) has `transport_failed` **12** and died with the same
device-lost fingerprint. `-ub` is the causal variable and `-b` is not.

**`-b` does nothing, and the numbers are stark.** Holding `-ub` fixed and
varying `-b` by 4x moves throughput **0.6%** at `ub=128` (147.97 vs 148.84) and
**6.6%** at `ub=512` (59.20 vs 63.13, and both still crash). Holding `-b` fixed
and varying `-ub` moves it **2.50x**. Arm B's two-flag change was therefore a
one-flag change wearing a disguise, which is exactly what E49 existed to
determine.

**PREDICTION 2 HELD.** Registered cell A >= 100 tok/s and cell B <= 70.
Measured **147.97** and **63.13**.

**PREDICTION 3 HELD.** Cell C at `-ub 256` survives, 12/12. So the survival
boundary sits between 256 and 512.

**PREDICTION 4 HELD, and it is the most interesting cell.** Registered that
cell D would survive and would NOT be materially faster than A, band 90-145
tok/s. Measured **127.53 - slower than A, not faster.** Throughput peaks at
`-ub 128` and falls off on BOTH sides:

```
ub 512:  59.20    ub 256: 105.60    ub 128: 147.97    ub 64: 127.53
```

**128 is an optimum, not a "smaller is safer" monotone.** Below it, per-dispatch
overhead starts to dominate; above it, something else does.

**PREDICTION 5 HELD.** Every surviving cell scored 12/12, at the top of the
registered 10-12 band.

**All five predictions held.** That is the first time in this programme, and it
is worth saying against the record that my bands sat below the result eight
times before today. The difference is that these predictions came from a
mechanism (`n_ubatch` sizes the dispatch, `n_batch` only groups) rather than
from calibrating a number.

### What the mechanism now looks like, and what is still not established

An inverted-U in throughput with a cliff on the high side is consistent with a
**working-set** account: prefill activations scale with `n_ubatch`, so a larger
micro-batch means a larger transient allocation on top of an already-large KV
cache. That predicts three things the data shows - the advantage is absent when
the KV cache is small (0.96x at 24,606 tokens), grows monotonically as it fills
(2.50x at 94,238), and turns into a device-lost once the total exceeds what the
driver will service. It also explains why the two `ub=512` deaths landed at
**different** depths, 96,286 and 109,598: a pressure threshold moves with
whatever else is resident, where a fixed limit would not.

**Not established, and I am not going to assert it.** No allocation was
measured. The account above is a hypothesis consistent with five configurations;
confirming it needs VRAM/GTT instrumentation during prefill, which this harness
does not collect. What IS established is the operational fact, and it needed no
mechanism: **serve long context with `-ub 128`.**

**A caution against over-generalising.** Everything here is one model, one pack,
one build, one driver. `-ub 128` is the optimum measured on Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M
at `-c 262144` on b10435 with this Mesa/RADV stack. It is not established as a
general llama.cpp tuning constant, and the corridor-rule discipline in F10 says
architecture-dependent numbers do not transfer.


## E50: is the negative-branch defect a TOOL-CALL artefact or a REASONING defect? (2026-08-17, pre-registered before any run)

**Why this exists.** It is the only systematic failure this model has. Across
E33 and E45, on every predicate type tested, the model applies a conditional
flag **unconditionally**: it passes the branch where the flag should fire and
fails the branch where the correct action is to do nothing.

| pair | branch that fires | branch that must NOT fire |
|---|---|---|
| numeric (`c1`/`c2`) | 5/5 | **2/5** |
| date (`c4`/`c5`) | 4/5 | **0/5** |

**But every one of those observations is inside a TOOL CALL**, and E43 gives a
contrary signal from prose: matter `m12` asks whether a service credit counts
towards a liability cap, the answer is **no**, and the model said no - correctly,
at every sequence position E46 ran it at. So the same "the right answer is that
this does not apply" shape is failed in a tool call and passed in advice.

That difference decides how much the defect matters. If it is a tool-call
artefact, the guidance is "do not automate conditional actions" and advisory
work is unaffected. If it is a reasoning defect that the closed-record set
happens not to probe hard, it reaches the legal verdict directly - because
"this clause does not apply here" is a large fraction of what advice IS.

**ONE VARIABLE CHANGES: whether the model is asked to ACT or to ADVISE.** The
same conditions, the same facts, the same thresholds, expressed twice - once as
a tool-call instruction and once as a request for a written answer.

**Instrument.** A new prose tier, `tools/run_negative_branch.py`, carrying the
E45 conditional pairs restated as advisory questions, graded by exact match on
a sealed key. No LLM judge. Every pair keeps both branches, because a model
that always says "the rule does not apply" passes the negative branch and fails
the positive one, and only the pair separates capability from a fixed answer.

**Arms.** Qwen3.8-27B at `off`, `low`, `medium`; the workhorse as control. The
tool-call numbers from E45 are the comparison and are already measured.

### Predictions (registered before any arm runs). The FIELD is named in each.

1. **PRIMARY: `negative_branch_correct` in prose is at least 8/13 for Qwen3.8
   at `medium`**, against 2/13-equivalent in the tool-call setting. Registered
   as a positive because E43's `m12` and L2's `Z1` both show the model
   declining to apply something when it should not, in prose, reliably.
2. **The positive branch stays high: `positive_branch_correct` >= 11/13.** If
   this drops, the prose restatement has changed the task rather than the
   modality, and the experiment is void rather than informative.
3. **The gap between prose and tool-call negative-branch scores is at least 5
   points** for the same model at the same effort. This is the discriminating
   claim.
4. **The workhorse shows the same direction but a smaller gap.** It has no
   reasoning setting to raise, so registered at 4-9 on prose negative branches.
5. **`off` is materially worse than `low`/`medium` on negative branches.**
   Registered: `off` at least 3 below `medium`. F69 found `off` loses precedence
   and multi-hop while keeping retrieval, and "does this rule apply here" is
   closer to precedence than to retrieval.

**Falsifier: if prose negative-branch accuracy is also at or below 4/13, the
defect is a REASONING defect, not a tool-call artefact.** That would be the
most consequential negative result of the programme, because it would mean the
model is unreliable at exactly the judgement advisory work is made of, and the
legal verdict would need re-opening rather than confirming.


## E51: does the same question get the same ADVICE twice? (2026-08-17, pre-registered before any run)

**Why this exists.** F70 established that a byte-identical prompt at three
different request positions produces three different answers at temperature 0,
because KV prefix reuse changes how prefill is chunked. That is a
reproducibility finding. It is not yet a **reliability** finding, and the
commercial question is the second one: **if you ask the same matter twice in a
session, do you get the same advice?**

**A preliminary reading that made this worth doing properly.** The three E46
answers for `m12` were compared by hand on 2026-08-17 and are **substantively
identical** - EUR 156,000, EUR 195,000, EUR 700, "no, rule 5", "rule 3" in all
three. Only the prose differs. That is one matter, at n=1, compared by eye, and
it is exactly the kind of preliminary signal that should be measured rather
than reported.

**ONE VARIABLE CHANGES: request position.** All 13 matters, run at three
positions each - alone, early in a short sequence, and late in the full
thirteen - reusing E46's exact design and extending it from one matter to all
of them.

**Grading is on the SEALED KEY, not on similarity.** Two answers agree if they
score the same on the same elements, not if they read alike. A similarity
metric would report the prose difference F70 already established and tell us
nothing new.

### Predictions (registered before any arm runs). The FIELD is named in each.

1. **PRIMARY: `element_agreement` is 65/65** - every matter scores identically
   at all three positions. Registered at the ceiling deliberately: the m12
   reading says substance is stable, and a band that allowed slippage would let
   me call any result a success.
2. **`answer_sha` differs at all three positions for at least 10 of 13
   matters**, reproducing F70 rather than assuming it. If answers turn out to
   be byte-identical here, F70's mechanism does not generalise beyond m12 and
   that is its own finding.
3. **Where a matter scores below 5/5, it scores the SAME below-5 at all three
   positions.** A model that gets m09 3/5 at one position and 5/5 at another is
   a different and worse problem than one that is consistently imperfect.

**Falsifier: if any matter's score changes with request position, temperature-0
local serving is not reliable for advisory work without pinning the request
sequence**, and that becomes a deployment constraint that has to be written
into the routing guide - not a footnote.

**Cost.** 13 matters x 3 positions, and position 3 is the full 13-matter
sequence which E46 measured at 4,978s. Roughly two hours.

### E50 AMENDMENT 1 (declared 2026-08-17, BEFORE any E50 arm runs)

**The registration above mis-states the defect, and reading the thirteen task
definitions before building the instrument is what caught it.** The amendment
is declared rather than the registration silently rewritten.

**What I registered:** that the model fails "the branch where the correct
action is to do nothing", and that the open question is tool-call versus prose.

**What the E45 data actually shows.** Qwen3.8 at `medium` fails exactly two of
thirteen, and it passes four other negative branches:

| task | phrasing of the rule | branch | score |
|---|---|---|---|
| c1-urgent | "**If** balance over 5,000, put URGENT" | fires | 5/5 |
| **c2-not-urgent** | "**If** ... , put URGENT, **otherwise** keep normal" | must not fire | **2/5** |
| c4-date-before | "**If** completion before 1 Oct, put EXPEDITED" | fires | 4/5 |
| **c5-date-after** | "**If** ... , **otherwise** use a normal title" | must not fire | **0/5** |
| c10-compound-both | "Put URGENT **only if** balance over 5,000 AND litigation" | fires | 5/5 |
| **c11-compound-one** | "Put URGENT **only if** ... AND ..." | **must not fire** | **5/5** |
| c9-select-no-email | "**If** balance is zero, **also** email" | must not fire | 5/5 |
| c7-cat-probate | "**If** litigation ... ; if anything else, ROUTINE" | other branch | 5/5 |

**So "negative branches fail" is false.** c11 is a negative branch on the same
`no_urgent_in_title` check as c2 and scores **5/5 against c2's 2/5**. c9 and c7
are negative branches and score 5/5.

**The pattern that survives the data is PHRASING.** Both failures are phrased
*"If X, do A ... otherwise do B"*. Both clean negative-branch passes on a
marker-insertion task are phrased *"do A only if X"*. Under "if ... otherwise"
the model inserts the marker regardless of the condition; under "only if" it
withholds it correctly.

**E50 is therefore re-scoped to a 2x2, and it is a better experiment than the
one I registered.** Two factors, same underlying conditions throughout:

| | "If X, do A; otherwise B" | "Do A only if X" |
|---|---|---|
| **tool call** | c2, c5 (measured: 2/5, 0/5) | c11 (measured: 5/5) |
| **prose advice** | to build | to build |

**Revised predictions, replacing 1-5 above. The FIELD is named in each.**

1. **PRIMARY: restating c2 and c5 with "only if" phrasing raises
   `success_rate` to >= 4/5 each**, in the tool-call modality, with nothing else
   changed. This is the discriminating claim: if phrasing is the cause, the
   rewrite fixes it.
2. **The positive branches stay >= 4/5 under the rewrite.** A rewrite that
   fixed the negative branch by making the model never insert the marker would
   show up here, and would mean the rewrite broke the task rather than fixed
   the model.
3. **In prose, `negative_branch_correct` is >= 5/6 under BOTH phrasings.** The
   prose modality is predicted to be robust to phrasing, because E43's `m12`
   and L2's `Z1` both show reliable "this does not apply" reasoning in written
   answers.
4. **The workhorse shows the same phrasing sensitivity in tool calls.** If it
   does not, the effect is Qwen-specific rather than a property of the task.

**Falsifier: if the "only if" rewrite does NOT lift c2 and c5, phrasing is not
the mechanism** and the original modality question stands unanswered - in which
case the prose arm still runs and still separates the two.

**Why this matters more than the version I registered.** If phrasing is the
cause, the fix is free and immediately actionable: write conditionals as "do X
only if Y" and the defect largely disappears. That is a better outcome for a
reader than "do not automate conditional actions", and it is the kind of thing
the routing guide should carry.

### E51 REFINEMENT (declared 2026-08-17, BEFORE any E51 arm result is read)

**Prediction 1 named the wrong FIELD, and F65 says that makes it unfalsifiable
in the way that matters.** It registered `element_agreement` as "every matter
scores identically at all three positions". A score is not enough: two runs can
both score a matter **4/5 while missing DIFFERENT elements**, which is the same
number and different advice - exactly the case a score-only check waves through.

**Prediction 1 is therefore split into three fields, all of which must hold:**

1a. `score_identical` = 13/13 - the same hits at every position.
1b. `missed_set_identical` = 13/13 - where a matter is imperfect, it misses the
    **same elements** at every position.
1c. `traps_identical` = 13/13 - no trap reproduced at one position and not
    another. This is the worst version of the result, because traps are the
    specific wrong answers the corpus exists to catch.

The bands are unchanged in spirit - all three at the ceiling - so this tightens
the prediction rather than loosening it after the fact. Nothing has been read
from the E51 arms; arm 2 was still running when this was declared.

`spikes/closed-record/compare_positions.py` implements all three and was
validated before use against a known-different pair: E43 arm A against arm B
differ on exactly `m01-scope-variation` (4/5 -> 5/5), which is what the E43
result records, and the tool reports that one matter and no others.

### E50 AMENDMENT 2 (declared 2026-08-17, BEFORE any E50 arm runs)

**Reading the six prompts in full sharpens the hypothesis and kills one version
of it.** AMENDMENT 1 said the failures are phrased "If X, do A ... otherwise do
B" and the passes are "do A only if X". Half of that is wrong: **both** pairs
carry an else-clause.

| task | prompt shape | branch | score |
|---|---|---|---|
| c4-date-before | "**If** completion falls before 1 Oct, put EXPEDITED ...; **otherwise** use a normal title" | fires | 4/5 |
| c5-date-after | *identical wording*, later date | must not fire | **0/5** |
| c10-compound-both | "**Put** URGENT in the title **only if** balance > 5,000 AND litigation. **Otherwise** use a normal title." | fires | 5/5 |
| c11-compound-one | *identical wording*, conveyancing matter | must not fire | **5/5** |

So the presence of "otherwise" is NOT the variable. What differs is **clause
order**: condition-first (`If X, do A`) versus imperative-first with an "only
if" qualifier (`Do A only if X`). Under condition-first the negative branch
collapses to 0/5; under imperative-first it holds at 5/5.

**A confound in that comparison, named because it is real.** c10/c11 are
**compound** conditions (balance AND matter type) while c4/c5 are simple. The
phrasing reading could therefore be an artefact of compound-ness - a model that
evaluates a conjunction carefully might simply be more careful generally.

**Four tasks added to separate them.** `c1b`, `c2b`, `c4b`, `c5b` hold the
condition **simple** and change only the phrasing to imperative-first "only if",
keeping the else-clause so that is constant too. Each pair keeps both branches,
because a model that never writes the marker passes every negative branch and
fails every positive one.

| new task | condition | branch | phrasing |
|---|---|---|---|
| c1b-urgent-onlyif | balance 7,400 > 5,000 | fires | "Put URGENT ... only if ..." |
| c2b-not-urgent-onlyif | balance 300 | must not fire | same |
| c4b-date-before-onlyif | completion 15 Sep | fires | "Put EXPEDITED ... only if ..." |
