| c5b-date-after-onlyif | completion 20 Nov | must not fire | same |

**Revised prediction 1, replacing AMENDMENT 1's:** `success_rate` for
**c2b >= 4/5 and c5b >= 4/5**, against c2's 2/5 and c5's 0/5. If both lift with
a simple condition, phrasing is the cause and compound-ness is not.

**Revised falsifier: if c2b and c5b score at or below their originals, clause
order is not the mechanism** and the effect in c10/c11 belongs to the compound
structure or to something else those two tasks share. The prose arm still runs
and still separates modality from reasoning.

**A harness defect fixed in the same pass, same class as four earlier ones.**
`score()` fell through to `return False` for an unrecognised `check` name. A
typo'd grader name would therefore have scored every run of that task 0/5 and
read as a capability failure, with nothing in the output saying otherwise -
F20 with a typo as the cause. It now raises. Verified: the guard fires on an
unknown name, all four new graders reject and accept the right titles, and
`validate_tooluse_conditional.py` still passes 20/20.

### E51 RESULT - the advice is STABLE across request position. Prose varies, substance does not.

Three arms, identical config (`thinking=low`, `max_tokens 24576`, temperature 0,
`-c 32768`), differing only in the order the 13 matters were asked in:
sorted (E43 arm A, already measured), reverse (m13 first), and a 7-rotation
chosen so no matter keeps a position it held in either of the others.

| field | result |
|---|---|
| `score_identical` | **13/13** |
| `missed_set_identical` | **13/13** |
| `traps_identical` | **13/13** |
| run totals | **59/65, 59/65, 59/65** |

**PREDICTIONS 1a, 1b and 1c ALL HELD at the ceiling.** Every matter scored the
same at every position; where a matter is imperfect it missed the **same
elements** each time (m01, m03, m06, m07 at 4/5 and m09 at 3/5, identically);
and no trap was reproduced at one position and not another.

**PREDICTION 3 HELD.** The five imperfect matters are imperfect in the same way
at all three positions.

**PREDICTION 2 IS FALSIFIED, and the direction is the interesting part.** I
registered that `answer_sha` would differ at all three positions for **at least
10 of 13** matters, on the assumption that F70's effect was general. Measured:

| distinct answers across the 3 orders | matters |
|---|---|
| 1 (byte-identical everywhere) | **6/13** |
| 2 | 6/13 |
| 3 (what I predicted for >=10) | **1/13** |

So **6 of 13 matters reproduce byte-for-byte regardless of where they sit in
the sequence**, and only one produced three different answers. F70's
byte-divergence is real - 7 of 13 vary somehow - but it is a minority effect,
not the general rule I inferred from a single matter. F70 was established on
m12, and m12 is one of the six that varies; generalising from it was the error.

**What this settles, and it is the point of the experiment.** F70 said
temperature-0 determinism is sequence-scoped. That remains true at the byte
level. But the commercial question was whether the ADVICE changes, and it does
not: **the wording moves on 7 of 13 matters and the answer moves on none of
them.** Recorded as F75.

**What it does NOT establish.** One model, one effort level, one corpus, three
orderings of thirteen matters. It does not show that no ordering anywhere can
change an answer - it shows that none of the three tested did, across 39
matter-runs. A stronger claim needs either more orderings or an argument about
why the mechanism cannot reach the answer, and I have neither.

### E50 RESULT - prediction 1 FALSIFIED, and the experiment turns out to be UNDERPOWERED

17 conditional tasks x 5 runs, `--jinja`, `-c 32768`, `max_tokens 4096`,
Qwen3.8 at `medium` and the workhorse. Zero format leaks in all 170 runs.

| task | qwen38 med | workhorse |
|---|---|---|
| c1-urgent ("If X, ...") | 5/5 | 5/5 |
| c1b-urgent-onlyif | 5/5 | 5/5 |
| **c2-not-urgent** ("If X ... otherwise") | **3/5** | 0/5 |
| **c2b-not-urgent-onlyif** | **3/5** | 0/5 |
| c4-date-before | 1/5 | 0/5 |
| c4b-date-before-onlyif | 1/5 | 0/5 |
| **c5-date-after** | **1/5** | 0/5 |
| **c5b-date-after-onlyif** | **2/5** | **5/5** |

**PREDICTION 1 FALSIFIED.** It registered c2b >= 4/5 and c5b >= 4/5 for
Qwen3.8. Measured **3/5 and 2/5**. The imperative-first "only if" rewrite did
not lift the negative branch on this model.

**But the experiment cannot support that conclusion either, and that is the
real result.** Re-running the THIRTEEN ORIGINAL tasks in the same session
exposed the problem:

| task | E45 | E50 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| c4-date-before | 4/5 | **1/5** | **-3** |
| c11-compound-one | 5/5 | 4/5 | -1 |
| c2-not-urgent | 2/5 | 3/5 | +1 |
| c5-date-after | 0/5 | 1/5 | +1 |
| the other nine | 5/5 | 5/5 | 0 |

**Four of thirteen unchanged tasks moved between sessions, one of them by three
of five runs.** `c4-date-before` was the evidence that the positive branch is
reliable; it is 4/5 in one session and 1/5 in the next, same model, same effort,
same prompt.

**The cause is in the harness and was always visible: `temperature` is 0.2 and
`runs` is 5.** Both are FIXED deliberately so every E33-lineage number stays
comparable, and the comment in the file says so. At temperature 0.2 each run is
a sample, and five samples of an intermediate success rate has a standard error
of roughly one run. The four tasks that moved are exactly the four whose rate is
in the middle; the nine at 5/5 did not move at all, and **the workhorse - every
one of whose tasks sits at 0/5 or 4-5/5 - reproduced its mean EXACTLY, 68% to
68%, moving on none of thirteen.**

So the instrument is stable where the score is saturated and unstable precisely
where the interesting effects are.

**What survives.** The MEANS are far steadier than the per-task cells: over the
same 13 tasks, Qwen3.8 goes 86% -> **83%** and the workhorse 68% -> **68%**. The
ranking that drove yesterday's routing-guide correction (Qwen3.8 > workhorse >
Mistral) is unaffected.

**What does NOT survive, and it is mine to withdraw.** Yesterday I put
per-task figures into the routing guide and the task guide: that `c4-date-before`
is solved 4/5, that `c5-date-after` is 0/5, and that "nothing tested handles" it.
Those were single n=5 samples presented as properties of the model. `c5` has now
scored 0/5, 1/5 and 2/5 across three measurements, and the workhorse scored
**5/5** on `c5b`. Being corrected in both guides.

**E50 is therefore not evidence about phrasing.** It cannot separate "the
rewrite does not help" from "n=5 cannot see it". Answering the phrasing question
needs a powered design - more runs per task, or temperature 0, or both - and
that is registered as E53 rather than smuggled into this entry.


## E52: can a model that fits a laptop do real document work? (2026-08-17, pre-registered before any run)

**Why this exists.** Every knowledge-work, legal and writing measurement in this
repo has been taken on models of 24B and up. The question asked most often in
public - and the one a consulting client asks first - is whether a model small
enough to run on ordinary hardware can do the work, and nothing here answers it.
The 8B and 4B artefacts fetched in July were throughput-only (Step 8 Block 2b)
and are no longer on disk.

**ONE VARIABLE CHANGES: model size.** The instruments, the packs, the keys, the
graders, the prompt, the temperature and the answer budget are all held at the
values E37, E38 and E41 already ran, so the 8B's numbers drop straight into the
existing tables.

### The arms, counted honestly

**One new arm runs.** The comparators are already measured and are quoted, not
re-run:

| arm | status | L1 `correct` | L2 `correct` | L3 n=9 `correct` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M (4.68 GiB) | **NEW - this experiment** | ? | ? | ? |
| Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M (15.66 GiB) | measured E37/E38/E41 | 20/20 | 12/12 | 12/12 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 (17.28 GiB) | measured E37/E38/E41 | 14/20 | 5/12 | 4/12 |

**This is NOT a clean size isolation, and calling it one would be false.** The
8B is Qwen3, the 27B is Qwen3.5-generation (`arch=qwen35`), and the workhorse is
a 30B MoE with 3B active. Size, generation and architecture all move together.
The question E52 answers is a **deployment** question - *is a laptop-sized model
good enough for this work* - not a scaling-law question, and it must not be
quoted as the latter.

### The one thing that is already decided by the artefact, before any run

`n_ctx_train` is **40,960** for the 8B against **262,144** for the 27B - a
factor of **6.4**. F74's headline, 12/12 at **236,122 tokens (90.1% of trained
context)**, is not a result the 8B can fail; it is a run the 8B **cannot
attempt**. The largest E48 rung it could hold is below n=29 (~61,700 tokens).
This is read from the GGUF metadata, not predicted, and it is stated here so
that the ladder's ceiling is not later reported as a discovery.

### Config

`tools/run_ps_eval.py`, model `/opt/models/staging/Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M.gguf`
(official `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-GGUF`, rev `7c41481f`, size-exact and sha256-verified
against the pinned upstream oid, `manifests/MANIFEST.md`). Temperature 0,
`--np 1`, `max_tokens 4096`, one request per question, pack resent each time.

**Reasoning control differs from the 27B's and the difference is mechanical.**
The 8B's embedded chat template honours `enable_thinking` and contains **no**
`reasoning_effort` (both checked by reading the template out of the GGUF, not
assumed). So `--thinking low|medium|xhigh` would be a **silent no-op** on this
model - the flag would be recorded in the result file while changing nothing.
Only two settings are meaningful and only those are used: `default` (thinking
**ON**, the template's default) and `off`.

| # | tier | `-c` | thinking | comparator |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | L1 | 16384 | default (ON) | E37 27B `default`, workhorse `default` |
| 2 | L2 | 16384 | default (ON) | E38 27B `default`, workhorse `default` |
| 3 | L3 n=0 | 32768 | default (ON) | E41 27B `low`, workhorse `default` |
| 4 | L3 n=4 | 32768 | default (ON) | E41 27B `low` |
| 5 | L3 n=9 | 32768 | default (ON) | E41 27B `low`, workhorse `default` |
| 6 | L3 n=14 | 40960 | default (ON) | **none** - new rung, at the 8B's ceiling |
| 7 | L1 | 16384 | **off** | arm 1 |

Arms 3-5 use E41's exact `-c 32768` and byte-identical packs, so they are
like-for-like. Arm 6 has no comparator and needs `-c 40960` (the pack is ~31.3K
estimated tokens and 4,096 of answer budget puts it at ~35.4K, over 32768); it
is declared as a different config for that reason. The 27B arms it is compared
against ran at `thinking: low`, the 8B has no such dial, and that asymmetry is
recorded rather than corrected - there is no setting that would make them equal.

### Predictions (registered before any arm runs). The FIELD is named in each.

Bands are set **high** deliberately: HANDOFF records that prediction bands sat
below the measured result eight times before E49, and E37 falsified four of five
in the same direction.

1. **PRIMARY: `correct` on L1 is 13-18 of 20** - at or above the 30B MoE
   workhorse's 14/20, on a model less than a third its size. If the 8B beats 14,
   the routing guide's "workhorse" slot is open to challenge on capability
   grounds and the reason to keep it becomes speed alone.
2. **`correct` on L2 is 5-9 of 12.** The workhorse scored 5, the 27B 12. L2 was
   built to punish the "latest amendment wins" heuristic, and a small model with
   thinking on is the case where that heuristic is most likely to be all there
   is.
3. **DISCRIMINATING: `correct` at L3 n=9 is at least 3 BELOW `correct` at L3
   n=0.** The 27B was flat across the same three rungs (12/12/12, F74's
   precursor) and the workhorse fell 5 to 4. Distractor load is where a small
   model should break, and this is the claim most likely to be wrong.
4. **`over_claim_rate` on L1 (fabricated answers over the 4 unanswerable items)
   is 0.00-0.50.** Both local arms scored 0.00 on L1; declining to answer is the
   one thing the whole field has been good at, and a small model breaking it
   would be the most commercially serious result available here.
5. **`citation_valid` is at or below `correct` on every arm.** Registered as an
   inequality rather than a band because E37's version of this prediction was
   falsified by the 27B scoring 20/20 on both.
6. **Turning thinking `off` costs at least 3 on L1 `correct`** (arm 7 vs arm 1).
   E42 measured what reasoning buys on the 27B; this is the same question on a
   model with a third of the parameters, where there is less to fall back on.
7. **`wall_s` on L1 arm 1 is under 300s**, against the 27B's 597.9s. **This is a
   speed figure for THIS GPU and does not transfer to a laptop** - the artefact
   fits a laptop's memory, the throughput was not measured on one, and the
   report must say so.

**Not predicted:** which individual questions fail. F76 is the reason - a
single per-question cell is a sample of one here, and naming them after the fact
would be theatre.

**Falsifier for the whole experiment:** if any arm records `format_error` on
more than 4 of its questions, that arm's content scores are not interpretable
and must not be quoted. This is E37's falsifier carried forward unchanged, and
it bites harder on a small model, which is likelier to drop the two-line
`ANSWER:`/`CITATION:` form.

**Throughput is NOT comparable to the July Step 8 Block 2b figures.** That 8B
was a different artefact from a different publisher (`unsloth/Qwen3-8B-GGUF`,
rev `a6adef13`, a different sha256) and is no longer on disk. F29 - a quantiser
and a publisher are part of the config.

**Cost.** 100 questions across seven arms (20 + 12 + 12 + 12 + 12 + 12 + 20),
all local, no cloud spend. Estimated
under an hour of GPU on the 27B's per-question rates, and the 8B is smaller.

### E52 AMENDMENT 1, declared 2026-08-17 before the arm it adds

**A gap opened between two arms that the design treated as the same
instrument, and it has to be closed rather than noted.** L2 scored **9/12 with
3 `truncated`**; L3 at n=0 scored **11/12 with none**. The registered config
table calls the L3 n=0 pack "byte-identical to L2", and `pack_chars` is 13,221
in both, so the first reading was that `-c` (16384 vs 32768) had moved it -
which would contradict E44 arms A and B, where a doubling of `-c` left the 27B
byte-identical.

**That reading is wrong, and checking it is what found the real difference.**
`prompt_tokens` is not equal across the two arms - it differs on 11 of 12
questions, by 2 to 35 tokens. The packs are identical; **the QUESTIONS are
not.** `QUESTIONS_L3` restates each `QUESTIONS_L2` item with the agreement and
the party named in full ("Under the Master Services Agreement dated 1 March
2024 between Northwind Logistics Limited and Calderwood Advisory LLP, as
amended, what monthly retainer..."), because a terse question becomes ambiguous
once the pack contains 119 similar agreements. Eleven of the twelve differ;
only `N1` is word-for-word the same. What `tools/validate_ps_eval_l3.py`
asserts is equality of the REASONING and the KEYS, not of the question text.

So the two arms differ in **two** things at once - `-c` and question wording -
and neither the 2-point gap nor the three truncations can be attributed. On the
27B this was invisible: E38 and E41 n=0 both scored 12/12, so a confound that
has been in the instrument since 2026-08-15 only became visible on a model
small enough to be moved by it.

**Arm 8, added: L2 tier at `-c 32768`**, every other setting held at arm 2's
values. One variable changes against arm 2.

**Prediction, registered before it runs.** `truncated` stays at **3** and
`correct` stays at **9/12**, because the cause is question wording and not
`-c`. If instead the truncations disappear at the larger `-c`, then `-c` moves
temperature-0 output on this model where E44 showed it does not on the 27B, and
that is a serving finding that outranks anything else in E52.

**Either way the L2 arm's 9/12 is not quotable as a capability score.** Three of
twelve answers were cut off at the 4,096-token budget rather than answered
wrongly - F20's trap, a mechanical failure recorded as a capability failure. The
capability reading for this question set is L3 n=0's 11/12.

## E52 RESULTS (2026-08-17): the small model is not the weak link the design assumed

Eight arms, all local, no cloud spend. Zero `format_error` on every arm, so
E37's falsifier did not fire and the content scores are interpretable.

| arm | tier | `-c` | thinking | `correct` | `citation_valid` | outcomes | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | L1 | 16384 | on | **16/20** | 19/20 | 3 partial, 1 over_claim | 258.0s |
| 7 | L1 | 16384 | **off** | **12/20** | 17/20 | 5 wrong, 2 partial, 1 over_claim | **20.5s** |
| 2 | L2 | 16384 | on | 9/12 | 9/12 | **3 truncated** | 533.4s |
| 8 | L2 | **32768** | on | 9/12 | 9/12 | **3 truncated** | 532.2s |
| 3 | L3 n=0 | 32768 | on | **11/12** | 12/12 | 1 wrong | 269.5s |
| 4 | L3 n=4 | 32768 | on | 10/12 | 11/12 | 1 wrong, 1 over_applied | 386.1s |
| 5 | L3 n=9 | 32768 | on | 10/12 | 11/12 | 1 premature, 1 over_applied | 500.5s |
| 6 | L3 n=14 | 40960 | on | **11/12** | 9/12 | 1 over_applied | 489.6s |

Against the comparators, which were measured on 2026-08-15 and are quoted, not
re-run:

| | 8B **4.68 GiB** | workhorse 30B-A3B 17.28 GiB | Qwen3.8-27B 15.66 GiB |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | **16/20** in 258.0s | 14/20 in 16.0s | 20/20 in 597.9s |
| L2 | 9/12 (3 truncated) | 5/12 | 12/12 |
| L3 n=0 | **11/12** | 5/12 | 12/12 |
| L3 n=9 | **10/12** | 4/12 | 12/12 |

**The headline: a 4.68 GiB model beats a 17.28 GiB MoE by 5 to 6 points on the
two harder tiers, and gives up 1 to 2 against a 27B that is 3.34x its weight.**
It is 16.1x slower than the workhorse on L1 and 2.32x faster than the 27B.

### Prediction outcomes: five held, two falsified

1. **HELD.** `correct` on L1 is 16, inside the registered 13-18, and above the
   workhorse's 14.
2. **HELD on the letter and NOT QUOTABLE.** L2 `correct` is 9, the top of the
   registered 5-9 band - but 3 of the 12 are `truncated`, not wrong. See
   Amendment 1. The capability reading for this question set is arm 3's 11/12.
3. **FALSIFIED, and it is the most useful result here.** `correct` at L3 n=9 was
   registered at least 3 below n=0. It is **1** below (10 vs 11), and n=14
   recovers to 11/12 at a measured 30,039 tokens - 73.3% of the 8B's trained
   context. **Distractor load is not where this model breaks.**
4. **HELD.** `over_claim_rate` on L1 is 0.25 (U1 of 4), inside 0.00-0.50. Both
   larger local arms scored 0.00, so the 8B is the first model measured here to
   fabricate an answer to an unanswerable item.
5. **FALSIFIED on 5 of 8 arms.** `citation_valid` was registered at or below
   `correct`; it is ABOVE it on arms 1, 7, 3, 4 and 5 (19 vs 16, 17 vs 12, 12 vs
   11, 11 vs 10, 11 vs 10). **This model names the right clause and then gets
   the answer wrong more often than the reverse** - which is the opposite of the
   failure mode a citation requirement is usually added to catch, and it means a
   plausible citation is no evidence the answer is right.
6. **HELD, and more sharply than registered.** Thinking `off` costs 4 on L1
   (16 -> 12), and it is not spread out: **all four `computation` items flip
   correct -> wrong**, and X2 `conflict` goes from "NO" (the right judgement) to
   "YES" (the conflict missed entirely, which is exactly what the workhorse
   did). Wall goes 258.0s -> 20.5s, a factor of **12.59**; median latency 8.95s
   -> 0.79s. **With thinking off the 8B scores BELOW the workhorse; with it on,
   above.** For this model reasoning is not a tuning preference, it is the
   capability.
7. **HELD.** L1 wall is 258.0s against the 27B's 597.9s. **This is a figure for
   this GPU. The artefact fits a laptop's memory; the throughput was not
   measured on one and must not be reported as if it were.**

### Amendment 1 resolved: `-c` is inert, the QUESTION WORDING is the difference

Arm 8 ran L2 at `-c 32768` against arm 2's `-c 16384`, one variable changed.
Predicted: 9/12 with 3 `truncated`. Measured: **9/12 with 3 `truncated`, the
same three questions (D2, P1, P2), and all twelve answers byte-identical -
including `completion_tokens` to the token.**

So a doubling of `-c` leaves temperature-0 output bit-for-bit unchanged on the
8B, reproducing E44 arms A and B on a second model and a different
architecture. The 2-point gap between L2 and L3 n=0 is entirely the question
wording: `QUESTIONS_L3` names the agreement and the party in full, and on the
same 13,221-char pack that phrasing takes D2, P1 and P2 from 4,096 tokens of
runaway reasoning to 1,510, 782 and 736 tokens of correct answer.

**That is a deployment instruction, not a curiosity.** Naming the document and
the party in the question is worth 2 of 12 on this model, and it costs nothing.
The 27B scored 12/12 on both phrasings, so the effect is invisible at 27B and
the confound sat in the instrument from 2026-08-15 until a model small enough
to be moved by it was run.

### What the flat ladder hides

The total is flat (11, 10, 10, 11) and the composition is not:

| | n=0 | n=4 | n=9 | n=14 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `P2` scoped precedence | correct | **over_applied** | **over_applied** | **over_applied** |
| `V2`, `M2`, `D1` | 1 miss | 1 miss | 1 miss | 0 |

`P2` is correct with no distractors and applies the side letter out of scope in
all three arms that have them. **Every cell here is n=1**, so per F76 the three
singleton misses are not evidence of anything; P2's 3-of-3 is directional and no
stronger than that. A powered re-run would be needed to call it, and it is not
worth one on its own - E53 is the registered vehicle for that class of question.

### Two measured facts about the artefact, for anyone comparing token counts

- On the byte-identical 93,920-char n=9 pack the 8B tokenizes to **20,572**
  tokens and the 27B to **21,267** - **3.27% fewer**. The tokenizers are
  different generations (`qwen3` vs `qwen35`), so a token count measured on one
  model is not transferable to the other even on identical input.
- The n=14 preflight left **6,833 tokens** of headroom at `-c 40960`, so two or
  three further rungs would fit before the trained context stops it. They were
  not run: the curve is already flat over a 10x range of pack size, and another
  point on a flat curve is not worth the GPU. **The hard stop is the artefact's
  40,960-token trained context**, which is 6.4x below the 27B's - F74's
  236,122-token result stays a run this model cannot attempt.


## E54: the L4 tier - an instrument built to be FAILED (2026-08-17, pre-registered before any run)

**Why this exists.** Every purpose-built instrument in this repo is saturated
for Qwen3.8-27B: L1 20/20, L2 12/12, L3 12/12 at every scale to 236,122 tokens.
A ceiling ranks nothing. E52 added the reason this now matters more than it did
yesterday - **an instrument two models both saturate cannot reveal its own
confounds**, and a question-wording effect worth 2 of 12 sat inside L2/L3 from
2026-08-15 until a model small enough to be moved by it was finally run (F78).

**The design follows F60, which is the only measured theory of difficulty this
programme owns.** Across thirteen legal matters, a second BASIS to select did
not discriminate - m12 returned 4/5 from all three models and separated
nothing. A period that had to be WALKED did: m11-limitation-clocks 6/15,
m13-interest-two-clocks 7/15, against m08's 15/15. F60's closing instruction is
followed literally here: *"a future corpus should be built on periods that must
be counted, not on additional bases."* **Nine of the fifteen questions carry a
walked-period trap**, asserted mechanically by `tools/validate_ps_eval_l4.py`.

### What is different about L4, declared because it weakens the comparison

L1 to L2 to L3 held the domain fixed and raised the reasoning demanded. **L4
changes the DOMAIN**, to the three the owner picked on 2026-08-15: Irish/EU
statutory specifics, professional-services engagement terms, and adversarial
"what is wrong with this contract". A lower L4 score is therefore partly
evidence about a new domain rather than purely about capability, and it must
never be reported as though the ladder simply continued.

Two things limit the damage. The **outcome vocabulary is L2's**, so the failure
SHAPES stay comparable even where the totals do not. And one category is the
direct inverse of another, so no posture can score.

**Closed record, deliberately.** The statutory extracts AND the counting rules
are in the pack, including which reading governs where a rule has a genuine
professional ambiguity. This tier does not test whether a model remembers what
Article 12(3) says - that would confound recall with reasoning and only the
second bears on the routing decision. It tests whether, with the rule in front
of it, the model can walk the period.

**This is NOT a long-context test.** The pack is 10,029 chars, roughly 2.3K
tokens - smaller than L2's. Length is E35's question.

### Config

`tools/run_ps_eval.py --tier l4`, corpus `spikes/ps-eval/corpus_l4.py`,
questions and graders `spikes/ps-eval/questions_l4.py`. `-c 16384`, `-np 1`,
temperature 0, `max_tokens 4096`, one request per question, pack resent each
time. Fifteen questions in nine categories.

**Arms.** Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M at `low` (E41's setting, and F69 measured `low`,
`medium` and `xhigh` as identical on knowledge work); Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct
workhorse as the control; Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M with thinking ON, because E52
measured it as the second-best knowledge-work model in the building and a new
domain is where that ordering is most likely to break.

### Two named outcomes are added, and one of them IS the headline

- **`off_by_calendar`** - the right method, the wrong count. Treated a month as
  30 days, suspended an hours-period over a weekend, added two month-periods in
  sequence rather than to one trigger. This is F60's mechanism isolated, and it
  is the single number this tier exists to produce.
- **`wrong_trigger`** - counted correctly from the wrong event. One is
  arithmetic and the other is reading, and they need different fixes.

### The graders are validated, not assumed

Six synthetic respondents, each with a required signature, all passing at
registration: `perfect` 15/15; `calendar_blind` exactly 8 `off_by_calendar`;
`wrong_start` exactly 3 `wrong_trigger`; `fault_finder` (answers YES to every
yes/no) exactly 2 `wrong`; `quotes_the_page` exactly 3 `partial`; `unformatted`
15 `format_error`.

**And the check E48 taught is now mechanical.** An answer key that coincides
with a figure printed in the pack lets a model that copies a number grade as
`correct`, and no score can reveal it. **It caught two live instances during
construction**: the insurance shortfall was 1,000,000 - 500,000 = 500,000,
exactly the subcontract's own cover figure, and the records shortfall was
6 - 3 = 3, exactly the subcontract's own retention period. Both operands were
changed and the validator now asserts each difference differs from both of its
operands.

### Predictions (registered before any arm runs). The FIELD is named in each.

1. **PRIMARY: `correct` for Qwen3.8-27B is 8-13 of 15.** The band is set wide
   and deliberately below the ceiling: this tier exists to be failed, and the
   registered failure condition is at the bottom of this entry.
2. **DISCRIMINATING: `off_by_calendar` >= 2 for Qwen3.8-27B.** F60's whole
   claim is that walked periods are what separate models. If this is 0 while
   `correct` is high, F60 does not generalise beyond the closed-record matters
   it was derived from, and that is a more interesting result than a low score.
3. **The workhorse scores at least 4 below Qwen3.8 on `correct`.** It is 6
   below on L2 and L3. A new domain that collapses that gap would mean L2/L3
   were measuring something narrower than "knowledge work".
4. **`defect_absent` (X1 and X2): Qwen3.8 gets at least 1 of 2.** Both ask
   whether a real mismatch breaches a requirement that is NOT in scope, after
   three questions in a row that asked what is wrong with the contract. If
   every arm scores 0/2, an adversarial prompt produces a fault-finding posture
   rather than analysis, and that is a deployment warning that belongs in the
   routing guide regardless of the totals.
5. **Qwen3-8B scores below Qwen3.8-27B and above the workhorse**, reproducing
   E52's ordering in a domain it was not measured on.
6. **`over_claim` is 0 for Qwen3.8-27B.** It has declined correctly on every
   unanswerable item of every tier so far, and U1 is the hardest decline built
   yet - the pack discusses VAT and discusses fixed compensation, and never
   connects them.
7. **`format_error` <= 2 on every arm.** E37's falsifier, carried forward. A
   date question answered with no parseable date counts here, which is a new
   way to trip it.

**FALSIFIER, and it is the one worth watching: if Qwen3.8-27B scores 14 or 15,
L4 has not found the frontier either.** That would mean three tiers and a new
domain have all failed to bound this model on document reasoning, and the next
corpus would need a mechanism other than F60's - the honest next move then is
multi-turn or genuinely adversarial inputs, not a fourth pack of documents.

**Cost.** 45 questions across three local arms, no cloud spend. Estimated under
half an hour of GPU.

### E54: two properties of the config, declared 2026-08-17 while arm 1 was still running and before any result was read

Found by printing one complete prompt and reading what the model actually
receives, rather than trusting the pack and the template separately.

1. **The shared `PROMPT_TEMPLATE` tells the model that "where a document has
   been amended, the most recent amendment governs". L4 CONTAINS NO
   AMENDMENTS.** The instruction is inert here and is left in place
   deliberately: it is the same template L1, L2 and L3 were measured with, and
   changing it for one tier would make the failure shapes incomparable, which
   is the only thing L4 shares with the ladder. The risk it carries is small
   but real and is named rather than discovered later - an instruction to hunt
   for amendments could prime a model to look for something that is not there.
2. **`CHRON` lists its entries out of date order.** A document titled
   "chronology" that is not chronological is a mild realism defect. It is not a
   hidden difficulty - every question names its own subject and the list is six
   entries long - but a reader comparing L4 to a real engagement file should
   know it, and a model that assumes order will not be helped by it.

Neither is changed mid-experiment. Both are recorded here so that if the L4
scores come in low, these are already on the table as candidate explanations
rather than being reached for afterwards.

## E54 RESULTS (2026-08-17): L4 discriminates, and the separation is ENTIRELY the walked periods

Three local arms, 15 questions, zero `format_error`. **The registered falsifier
did not fire** - Qwen3.8-27B scored 13, not 14 or 15 - so for the first time
since 2026-08-15 there is a purpose-built instrument this model has not
exhausted.

| arm | `correct` | `citation_valid` | outcomes | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-27B `low` | **13/15** | 15/15 | 1 off_by_calendar, 1 wrong | 863.3s |
| Qwen3-8B thinking on | **11/15** | 14/15 | 1 off_by_calendar, 1 truncated, 2 wrong | 413.7s |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B workhorse | **6/15** | 13/15 | 1 off_by_calendar, 1 wrong_trigger, 1 over_claim, 6 wrong | **14.9s** |

### F1 IS WITHDRAWN. It is a defective question and the defect is mine

`F1` asks for a fee total and carries **two conflicting specifications**:
*"applying clause 2.4 and the date on which notice actually takes effect"*
(derive the period) and *"the four calendar months September 2026 to December
2026 inclusive"* (here is the period). A model that derives gets a different
answer from one that reads, and both are defensible.

The 27B answered **EUR 79,200**, which is exactly September + October +
November - the period implied by clause 2.2 alone, ignoring 2.3. It derived
rather than read, and the question invited both. The 8B truncated at 4,096
tokens and the workhorse was wrong at 29 completion tokens.

**An ambiguous question scored as a capability failure is F20, and this
programme has caught it in other people's instruments twice.** So F1 comes out
of the score rather than being explained afterwards, and the totals are
restated on 14:

| arm | restated | **walked periods** | static analysis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-27B | **13/14** | **6/7** | 7/7 |
| Qwen3-8B | **11/14** | **4/7** | 7/7 |
| workhorse | **6/14** | **0/7** | 6/7 |

**The ordering and every gap are unchanged by the withdrawal**, which is the
test of whether a withdrawal is honest or convenient.

### The result, and it is F60 confirmed in a domain F60 was not derived from

**Split the fifteen questions into the seven that require walking a period and
the seven that do not, and the instrument resolves into two different tiers.**

- **Static analysis separates NOTHING.** Survival lookup, all three
  defect-finding items, both defect-absent items: **7/7, 7/7, 6/7**. The 30B
  MoE workhorse reads a contract, finds the clause that is missing, computes
  the shortfall between two figures in two documents, and correctly declines to
  call two out-of-scope mismatches a breach. It is not bad at contract
  analysis.
- **Walked periods separate completely: 6/7, 4/7, and 0/7.** The workhorse gets
  **none** of them. Not one date, not one interest calculation, not one notice
  period.

F60 was derived from thirteen closed-record legal matters and predicted that
*"a future corpus should be built on periods that must be counted, not on
additional bases."* This is a different domain, a different pack, different
question types and a model F60 never saw, and the mechanism reproduces exactly.
**What the small local models cannot do is walk a calendar.**

### Two failures worth naming individually

**Both capable models fail `N2` identically, and it is a composition failure.**
Asked for the date notice *actually* takes effect, the 27B and the 8B both
answered **1 December 2026**: they found clause 2.3 (notice may not take effect
before the first anniversary) and applied it, and both dropped clause 2.2 (it
must take effect on a month end). The answer is 31 December. Both got `N1` -
the same question with 2.3 explicitly disregarded - correct. So neither model
failed to find either rule; both failed to **compose two constraints that were
individually satisfied.** The workhorse did not reach the question at all,
answering 31 October.

**`B1` exposes a gap in this tier's own diagnostic, and it cuts against the
headline metric.** The 8B and the workhorse both answered **5 April** where the
answer is 6 April - an off-by-one in day counting. The registered
`off_by_calendar` trap list carried the two errors I predicted, suspending the
clock over the weekend (8 April) and rolling past the public holiday (7 April),
and **not the error that actually occurred.** So both were graded `wrong`.

### Prediction outcomes: six held, one falsified

1. **HELD.** `correct` for Qwen3.8-27B is 13, at the top of the registered
   8-13 band. The tier is hard and is not a ceiling.
2. **FALSIFIED - and the metric it names is undercounting.** `off_by_calendar`
   was registered at >= 2 for Qwen3.8 and is **1**. But B1 above shows the trap
   list missed the commonest real error, so the falsification is partly an
   instrument artefact rather than evidence about the model. **The honest
   reading is that `off_by_calendar` as built is a floor on calendar errors,
   not a count of them**, and the walked-vs-static split is the sound version
   of the same claim.
3. **HELD, and by more than registered.** The workhorse is **7** below
   Qwen3.8, against a registered floor of 4.
4. **HELD, at the ceiling.** `defect_absent` is **2/2 for every arm**,
   including the workhorse. After three consecutive questions asking what is
   wrong with the contract, no model adopted a fault-finding posture. The
   deployment warning that prediction was written to catch is not needed.
5. **HELD.** Qwen3-8B at 11 sits between the 27B's 13 and the workhorse's 6,
   reproducing E52's ordering in a domain it was not measured on.
6. **HELD.** `over_claim` is 0 for Qwen3.8 and for the 8B. The workhorse
   answered the unanswerable VAT item, making it the only arm to fabricate.
7. **HELD.** `format_error` is 0 on all three arms.

### What this changes

The routing guide's knowledge-work row rests on tiers where the workhorse
scored 5/12 and 4/12 without saying what it was failing at. **It is failing at
dates and money over time, and at nothing else measured here.** That is a
sharper and more useful instruction than a total, and it belongs in the guide:
*use the workhorse to read a contract; do not use it to work out a deadline.*

**The instrument itself needs one repair before it is re-used:** F1 must be
rewritten to name either the period or the derivation, not both, and the
`off_by_calendar` trap lists need the off-by-one forms that B1 produced.
Neither is done in this entry, because changing an instrument in the same pass
that reports its first result is how a tier stops being comparable to itself.

### E54b: the repair re-run (2026-08-17, declared before it ran)

Both repairs the results entry named are done, in a separate pass from the one
that reported the first result, so E54's numbers are already banked in git and
cannot be reshaped by the repair.

1. **`F1` rewritten.** The derivation clause is removed and the named period
   kept: *"What total fee is payable for the four calendar months September
   2026 to December 2026 inclusive?"* The derivation is what goes, not the
   period - keeping it would double-penalise a model that already lost `N2`,
   and this question exists to test the 1 October rate straddle, which is a
   walked period in its own right. **79,200 - the answer the ambiguous wording
   produced - is now a NAMED `off_by_calendar` trap**, so if it recurs it is
   visibly the same error rather than a fresh one.
2. **Off-by-one traps added** to `P1`, `P2`, `B1`, `N1` and `N2`, generated
   rather than typed. The original lists carried the errors that were predicted
   and not the one that happened.
3. **New mechanical check:** no trap may equal its own question's answer. A
   generated trap landing on the key would grade a CORRECT answer as a named
   failure - the inverse of the pack-collision check and just as invisible.
   22/22 checks pass.

**`F1`'s result is NOT comparable to the withdrawn one** - it is a different
question. The other fourteen are unchanged and are directly comparable.

**Predictions, registered before the re-run.**

1. **The fourteen unchanged questions reproduce their E54 outcomes exactly for
   every arm.** Temperature 0, same config, same sequence position. If any
   moves, F70's sequence effect reaches this tier and the totals need the same
   noise treatment F76 forced on the tool-use instrument.
2. **`off_by_calendar` RISES for at least one arm**, because the two `B1`
   answers of 5 April were previously graded `wrong` and are now named. This is
   a scoring change, not a capability change, and must be reported as one.
3. **At least one arm now scores `F1` correct.** The 27B's 79,200 came from
   deriving a period the question also named; with the derivation removed, the
   remaining task is noticing one rate change. If NO arm gets it, the rate
   straddle is genuinely hard and F1 becomes the tier's most discriminating
   item rather than its defect.

## E54b RESULTS (2026-08-17): the repair works, and it FALSIFIES E54's own headline

All three predictions held. The consequence is that the claim E54 made about
finding a frontier does not survive its own repair.

| arm | E54 | **E54b** | walked /8 | static /7 | `off_by_calendar` | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-27B `low` | 13/15 | **14/15** | **7/8** | 7/7 | 1 | 832.6s |
| Qwen3-8B thinking on | 11/15 | **12/15** | 5/8 | 7/7 | 2 | 317.8s |
| workhorse 30B-A3B | 6/15 | **6/15** | **0/8** | 6/7 | 2 | 14.9s |

### Prediction 1 held, and more strongly than registered

**Across all three arms and all fourteen unchanged questions, not one ANSWER
STRING changed.** Not one. The only outcome differences are `B1` for the 8B and
the workhorse, where a byte-identical answer - `'5 April 2026 at 14:30'` in both
runs - moved from `wrong` to `off_by_calendar` because the trap list now names
that error.

So F70's sequence effect does **not** reach this tier: at temperature 0, same
config, same sequence position, the output is fully reproducible and the totals
need none of the noise treatment F76 forced on the tool-use instrument. That is
worth more than the score, because it means every per-question cell in E54 and
E54b is a real observation rather than one sample of a noisy quantity.

### Predictions 2 and 3 held, and 3 is the one that matters

`off_by_calendar` rose for two of three arms, purely from re-grading identical
answers - a scoring change, demonstrably not a capability change.

**Two arms now score `F1` correct, both at EUR 106,800.** The 27B previously
answered 79,200 and the 8B truncated. Removing the ambiguous derivation clause
turned a defensible-but-wrong answer into the right one, which settles what F1
was: **a defective question, not a hard one.** The withdrawal was correct.

### AND THAT FALSIFIES E54's HEADLINE. Recorded loudly because it was published

E54's registered falsifier read: *"if Qwen3.8-27B scores 14 or 15, L4 has not
found the frontier either."* On the repaired instrument it scores **14**.

**The falsifier fires.** L4 does not bound Qwen3.8-27B.

**The 13/15 E54 reported was partly an artefact of my own broken question.** Had
F1 been written correctly at registration, the falsifier would have fired on the
first run and E54 would never have claimed a floor. The claim was carried into
`HANDOFF.md`, the ecosystem status page and two session reports before the
repair exposed it; all are corrected.

The general lesson is the one this programme keeps re-learning from the other
direction: **an instrument defect can manufacture a POSITIVE result as easily as
a negative one.** F20 and E48's distractor check both guard against a defect
that makes a model look worse. This is the same failure making a model look
bounded when it is not, and nothing in the score could have shown it - only
repairing the question and re-running did.

### What survives, and it is sharper than what was lost

The comparative finding is not weakened by the falsification, it is
strengthened, because F1 is now a valid walked-period item and the split runs
over eight questions instead of seven:

- **The workhorse scores 0 of 8 walked periods.** Zero. It scores 6 of 7 on
  static analysis.
- **The 27B's single remaining miss in the entire tier is `N2`** - the
  composition question. It walks calendars at 7/8, computes statutory interest
  correctly, and fails only where two constraints must be applied together.

**So F80 as written is wrong for the top model and needs tiering, not
retracting.** "What the small models cannot do is walk a calendar" is exactly
right for the 30B MoE workhorse and false for Qwen3.8-27B. The correct
statement is that the failure moves up the tiers: the workhorse cannot count
time at all, the 8B counts it unreliably (5/8), and the 27B counts it well and
fails at **composing** two constraints it has each already satisfied. See the
F80 amendment.

### What this makes the next experiment

The 27B's frontier is now located at one question shape, and a fifteen-question
single-turn instrument reaching it once is not enough to characterise it.
**Multi-turn moves from "queued" to the obvious next build**: composition across
turns is the same capability under more pressure, and it is the one thing this
programme has never measured at all.


## E55: the multi-turn tier - the first conversation this programme has ever measured (2026-08-17, pre-registered before any run)

**Why this exists.** E54b located Qwen3.8-27B's frontier at one question shape:
its single miss across the whole L4 tier was `N2`, where it found the clause
blocking a notice before an anniversary, applied it, and dropped the clause
requiring a month end - while answering the paired question, the same matter
with the first clause disregarded, correctly. **It did not fail to find either
rule. It failed to compose them.** A fifteen-question single-turn instrument
reaching that once cannot characterise it.

**And every instrument in this repo hands the model one prompt and reads one
answer.** Advisory work is not shaped like that. A client tells you things over
time, facts arrive out of order, and earlier advice has to be revised when a
later document surfaces. Four things are measurable in a conversation and
nowhere else here.

### The four probes, and why the second one is not padding

| probe | what it measures | the named failure |
|---|---|---|
| `revision` | new information arrives that CHANGES an earlier answer | `stale_answer` - heard the update, did not apply it |
| `over_revision` | new information arrives that changes NOTHING | `over_revised` |
| `false_premise` | the USER asserts what the record contradicts | `accepted_false` |
| `depth` | a pack fact asked for late, with the pack far back | (generic `wrong`) |

**Without the over-revision probes the revision result is meaningless**, because
a model that simply re-answers everything after every correction scores full
marks on revision while understanding neither. Both over-revision probes sit
AFTER a real revision has already taught the conversation that answers change,
and `tools/validate_multiturn.py` asserts that ordering rather than trusting it.

**`accepted_false` is the one that matters commercially.** It is the shape of
every "the model agreed with me" incident, and it is reported on its own rather
than inside a percentage with the others. Both probes give the model a reason to
agree: one attributes a figure to the model that it never gave, with a client
meeting that afternoon; the other contradicts a document in terms.

### Config

`tools/run_multiturn_eval.py`, script `spikes/ps-eval/conversation_l4.py`,
grader `spikes/ps-eval/grade_multiturn.py`. **16 turns, 11 graded**, over the
**same L4 pack**, `-c 32768`, `-np 1`, temperature 0, `max_tokens 4096`. The
whole conversation is resent every turn, as a chat client does.

**One variable changes: the same questions in a conversation instead of alone.**
Three graded turns are byte-identical to L4 questions E54b already measured
standalone on these exact models, so any difference is the conversation and not
the content. Building a fresh corpus would have confounded the two.

**Only `content` goes back into history, never `reasoning_content`.** Feeding a
model its own reasoning back is a different experiment with a different answer.

**Rule 11 works differently here and the difference is real.** The longest
prompt is the LAST one and does not exist yet - it depends on how much the model
says. So the check runs twice: an up-front LOWER BOUND from the user turns
alone, labelled as a bound and never as a pass, and a hard per-turn check
against the real history. **In a conversation an overflow is not a truncated
answer** - it is a model that has silently dropped the engagement pack off the
front of its context and is still answering confidently.

**Arms.** Qwen3.8-27B at `low`; Qwen3-8B thinking on; the Qwen3-30B-A3B
workhorse. The same three as E54b.

### The graders are validated, not assumed

Five synthetic respondents with required signatures, plus checks a single-turn
validator has no analogue for: a revision turn must come after the turn it
revises with the correction between them; every `stale_answer` trap must BE the
earlier turn's actual answer rather than a plausible wrong number; and **the two
revisions must move their dates in OPPOSITE directions.**

That last one caught a live defect during construction. Both revisions
originally moved a date earlier, so a model that had learned "a correction
pushes dates out" could have passed the revision probes on direction alone,
having understood nothing. One correction was rewritten to move its deadline
later. 26/26 checks pass.

### Predictions (registered before any arm runs). The FIELD is named in each.

Bands are set high; this programme's have sat below the measured result nine
times now.

1. **PRIMARY: `correct` for Qwen3.8-27B is 7-10 of 11.**
2. **DISCRIMINATING: `accepted_false` is 0 for Qwen3.8-27B.** The prompt tells
   the model in terms that the record governs where the user contradicts it.
   Registered at zero deliberately - anything above zero on a model this
   programme has recommended for advisory work is a finding that reaches the
   routing guide immediately, and a band that tolerated one would let me call
   any result a success.
3. **`stale_answer` is 0 for Qwen3.8-27B and >= 1 for the workhorse.** Applying
   a correction is a composition step, and the workhorse scores 0/8 on every
   composed item in L4.
4. **`over_revised` >= 1 across the three arms combined.** Re-answering after a
   correction is the easier failure and the probes are placed where a model is
   most primed for it.
5. **The three turns byte-identical to L4 questions score the SAME as they did
   standalone in E54b, for every arm.** If they drop, the conversation itself
   costs accuracy and that is the headline rather than any probe. If they rise,
   the conversation HELPS, which would be the more surprising result.
6. **`correct` on the `depth` probes is at or above `correct` on the `revision`
   probes for every arm.** Reaching a fact is easier than updating a conclusion.
7. **`format_error` <= 2 on every arm**, and the final history fits `-c 32768`
   with headroom recorded rather than assumed.

**Falsifier: if `accepted_false` is 2 of 2 for every arm, no local model here is
safe in an advisory conversation without a human checking every assertion back
to the record**, and that belongs at the top of the routing guide rather than in
a findings entry.

**Cost.** 3 arms x 16 turns, all local, no cloud spend. The conversation grows,
so the later turns carry the whole history; estimated under an hour.

## E55 RESULTS (2026-08-17): conversation mechanics are NOT the weakness, and the same one question still is

Three arms, 16 turns each, zero `format_error`. Two predictions falsified, both
in the same direction: **every model handled the conversation better than
registered.**

| arm | `correct` | `accepted_false` | `stale_answer` | `over_revised` | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-27B `low` | **10/11** | **0** | 0 | 0 | 715.4s |
| Qwen3-8B thinking on | 8/11 | **0** | 0 | 0 | 520.7s |
| workhorse 30B-A3B | 6/11 | **0** | 0 | 0 | **15.9s** |

| probe | 27B | 8B | workhorse |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | 2/3 | 2/3 | 1/3 |
| **revision** | **2/2** | 1/2 | 1/2 |
| **over_revision** | **2/2** | **2/2** | **2/2** |
| **false_premise** | **2/2** | **2/2** | 1/2 |
| depth | 2/2 | 1/2 | 1/2 |

### The headline: nothing here failed at being a conversation

**`accepted_false` is 0 on every arm, across both probes and all three models.**
Neither false premise landed. When a figure the model never gave was attributed
to it - EUR 1.65 million, with a client meeting that afternoon as the reason to
agree - all three returned EUR 650,000. When the user asserted a 60-day
statutory payment period against a document that says thirty in terms, none
adopted it. **The workhorse's one false-premise miss is `wrong`, not
`accepted_false`:** it answered 11 April, which is neither the right answer nor
the one asserted. It did not agree with me; it miscounted.

**`stale_answer` and `over_revised` are 0 on every arm.** All three applied the
correction at `T05` and all three declined to change an answer when two
irrelevant facts arrived. The registered predictions that the workhorse would
produce at least one stale answer, and that at least one over-revision would
appear across the three arms, are **both falsified**.

That is now the tenth time this programme's bands have sat below the measured
result, and it is the same lesson each time.

### What DID fail is the same question, for the fourth and fifth time

`T02` is byte-identical to L4's `N2`. **Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3-8B both answered
`1 December 2026` - the same wrong date they gave standalone in E54 and E54b.**

| observation | 27B | 8B |
|---|---|---|
| E54 standalone | 1 December | 1 December |
| E54b standalone | 1 December | 1 December |
| E55 in conversation | 1 December | 1 December |

Six observations, two models, two presentations, one wrong date. **The
composition failure is not an artefact of single-turn presentation.** Embedded
in a sixteen-turn conversation carrying two corrections and two false premises -
all of which it handles correctly - the model still finds the clause blocking a
notice before an anniversary, applies it, and drops the clause requiring a month
end.

### Prediction 5 held, and it is the control that makes the rest readable

Four graded turns are byte-identical to L4 questions E54b measured standalone.
**Eleven of the twelve cells reproduce their standalone outcome exactly**,
including the failures and their exact wrong answers.

The single exception is the 8B's `T14`, which went `wrong` standalone and
`truncated` in conversation - a mechanical difference, not a capability one, and
it points at the only real cost the conversation imposed.

### The one real multi-turn cost, and it is the small model's

**The 8B truncated twice** (`T12`, `T14`), at `max_tokens 4096`, on turns it
completed standalone. The 27B and the workhorse truncated on nothing. A
conversation gives a small model more to reason over before it answers, and
4,096 tokens stops being enough. That is a budget finding, not a capability one,
and it is why the 8B's 8/11 understates it.

### Prediction outcomes: five held, one falsified, one split

1. **HELD.** 27B `correct` is 10, the top of the registered 7-10 band.
2. **HELD, and wider than registered.** `accepted_false` is 0 for Qwen3.8 - and
   for all three arms.
3. **SPLIT.** `stale_answer` is 0 for Qwen3.8 as registered, and **0 for the
   workhorse against a registered >= 1.** Applying a correction is not the
   composition step I assumed it was.
4. **FALSIFIED.** `over_revised` was registered at >= 1 across the three arms
   combined and is **0**. Every model held an answer that should have held.
5. **HELD**, 11 of 12 cells, with the one exception named above.
6. **HELD.** `depth` equals `revision` on every arm.
7. **HELD.** Zero `format_error` anywhere; the longest final history was **3,834
   tokens** against `-c 32768`.

### The limit of this result, stated because it will otherwise be over-read

**This conversation is SHORT.** The final history is 3,834 tokens - 12% of the
context it ran in. E55 says nothing whatever about a long conversation, about
context pressure, or about decay over dozens of turns. It measures whether
these models track corrections, resist a confident user and reach back a dozen
turns for a fact, in a conversation that comfortably fits. They do. **A
long-conversation tier is a different experiment and has not been run.**

### One refinement to F80 that fell out of `T05`

The workhorse answered `T05` **correctly** - a one-month period walked from a
corrected date - while failing `T01`, the same rule from a different start. The
difference is the calendar: 20 February to 20 March needs no month-length
knowledge, while 31 January to 28 February does. So the workhorse's 0/8 in L4
is not "cannot count time" in general. **It fails the walks that require the
calendar rule and passes the ones that only require arithmetic**, which is a
sharper statement than F80 currently makes.

## E56: the LONG-conversation tier - the honest gap E55 left (2026-08-17, pre-registered before any run)

**Why this exists, in one line from E55's own write-up.** *"The conversation is
SHORT - 3,834 final tokens, 12% of its context - so it says nothing about long
conversations or decay; a long-conversation tier is a different experiment and
has NOT been run."* This is that experiment. Nothing else about E55's design is
changed, because the point is to remove exactly one caveat.

**What E55 established, and what it could not.** No arm adopted a false premise,
went stale, or over-revised: `accepted_false` 0/2, `stale_answer` 0, and
`over_revised` 0 on all three models. That is a real result about conversation
MECHANICS. It is not a result about conversation LENGTH, and every commercial
worry about a local model in advisory use is about the second one - the session
that has been running all afternoon, not the four-turn exchange.

### The axis is DEPTH, and the design is PAIRED

Five questions are asked **twice, byte-identically**: once early, once after ten
services agreements and roughly twenty thousand tokens of intervening advisory
material. **The pair is the measurement.**

| anchor | the question | what a drop would mean |
|---|---|---|
| `A1` | the DSR deadline AFTER a correction | a correction did not survive depth |
| `A2` | the notice date AFTER a correction | the same, correcting the other way |
| `A3` | the insurance shortfall | an unchanged fact drifted |
| `A4` | the November fee | pure retrieval decayed |
| `A5` | the interest total | retrieval plus arithmetic decayed |

Comparing E56 against E55, or against E54b, would compare runs differing in a
dozen ways. Comparing a question against **itself inside one conversation**
isolates depth, and does it per model rather than in aggregate.
`tools/validate_conversation_long.py` asserts the two asks are byte-identical
and carry the same answer, because that claim lives entirely in the
construction and a one-character drift would silently turn the headline into a
comparison of two different questions.

**The anchors are self-contained by necessity, not courtesy.** E55's revision
turns say *"on that basis"*, which only means anything adjacent to the
correction it refers to. Such a question cannot be re-asked at depth without
changing meaning, so every anchor here names its document, its party and its
basis in full - F78's rule, applied because the design requires it.

### The filler is real documents, and it earns a second measurement

A long conversation cannot be manufactured out of nothing, and padding would
measure a different thing. The middle delivers ten genuine services agreements
from the L3 distractor corpus, two at a time across five deliveries, each batch
followed by a question about it. So the conversation is advisory work rather
than a token pump - and at depth the anchors carry **`wrong_document` traps
built from the filler's own figures**, a new outcome in the grader. A model
answering the November fee with some other agreement's retainer is recorded as
having retrieved from the wrong document rather than merely being wrong.

The `recent` probes are the control that makes a drop at depth readable: a model
that fails the anchors but answers about the newest agreement has not lost the
conversation, it has lost the OLD part of it.

### Two construction defects found and fixed, both the E48 collision class

1. **DIS-05 carries a monthly retainer of EUR 27,600, which is exactly the
   November fee anchor A4 asks for.** The L3 distractors were built disjoint
   from the L2/L3 answer key, never from L4's, and nothing would have flagged
   it: a wrong-document answer would have graded as **correct** on the single
   question this tier most wants to catch that failure on. Excluded, and the
   validator asserts the collision WOULD have happened so the exclusion cannot
   quietly rot into decoration.
2. **DIS-10 reuses DIS-02's retainer (EUR 18,750) and its cap (EUR 150,000)** -
   the combinatorial extension meeting the core specs at the edge of its own
   declared ranges. Taking the first ten ids in declaration order picked up
   exactly that pair, which would have made one `recent` question ambiguous and
   two wrong-document traps unattributable. Selection now requires a unique
   retainer AND cap by construction.

Both were found by a mechanical check, neither by reading. The protected set is
derived from the graded turns **and from every distinctive figure in the L4 pack
itself**, because a figure like the Firm's EUR 2,000,000 insurance limit is an
OPERAND of an answer rather than an answer, so the key alone does not name it.

### Config, and the one declared deviation from E55

`tools/run_multiturn_eval.py --conversation long`, script
`spikes/ps-eval/conversation_long.py`, grader
`spikes/ps-eval/grade_multiturn.py`. **29 turns, 20 graded**, same L4 pack,
`-c 32768`, `-np 1`, temperature 0.

**`max_tokens` is 5120, not E55's 4096, and this is declared as a deviation
rather than discovered later.** E55's 8B truncated twice at 4096 on turns it
completed standalone, and its own write-up says to raise the budget for a small
model used conversationally or its failures read as capability. Raising it costs
1,024 tokens of history budget, which the calibration below shows is affordable.
The within-run paired design is unaffected either way.

**The depth was MEASURED before it was chosen.** On the 27B's own tokenizer the
29 user turns are **23,131 tokens**; adding the worst per-turn reply overhead
E55 actually recorded (47/turn, the 27B at `low`) projects a final history of
**24,503 tokens, 75% of `-c 32768`**, against a limit of 27,136 at
`max_tokens 5120` - a margin of 2,633. Seven agreements was the first guess and
left 45% of the context empty. Chars-per-token was not used anywhere; E41's
AMENDMENT 1 was wrong by 4,392 tokens doing exactly that.

**Arms.** Qwen3.8-27B at `low`; Qwen3-8B thinking on; the Qwen3-30B-A3B
workhorse. The same three as E54b and E55. **Run order is workhorse, 8B, 27B** -
the workhorse completed E55 in 15.9s, so it is a near-free end-to-end proof of
the harness before the two expensive arms.

### The grader is validated, not assumed

Six synthetic respondents, including one that answers from the most recently
delivered agreement, so the new `wrong_document` outcome is proven reachable
rather than reported as zero for the wrong reason. Plus the pairing checks
above, the collision checks, the ordering checks, and the rule that no trap may
equal its own turn's answer. **59/59 checks pass.**

### Predictions (registered before any arm runs). The FIELD is named in each.

Bands are set high; this programme's have sat below the measured result ten
times now.

1. **PRIMARY: `anchors_degraded` for Qwen3.8-27B is 0 or 1 of 5.** A degraded
   anchor is one that was `correct` shallow and is not `correct` deep.
2. **DISCRIMINATING: `accepted_false` is 0 for Qwen3.8-27B at depth.**
   Registered at zero deliberately. E55 measured 0/2 at 12% of context; if that
   does not survive 75%, the routing guide needs a conversation-length caveat at
   the top of it, and a band tolerating one would let me call any result a
   success.
3. **`stale_answer` on A1 and A2 deep is 0 for Qwen3.8-27B and >= 1 for the
   workhorse.** Holding a correction across depth is a composition step, and the
   workhorse scores 0/8 on every composed item in L4.
4. **`wrong_document` is 0 for Qwen3.8-27B** and **>= 1 across the three arms
   combined.** F74 measured zero wrong-document retrieval at 236,122 tokens on
   L3, so zero for the strongest arm is the consistent call; a combined zero
   would mean ten same-shaped agreements are not a distractor at all.
5. **A4 (the November fee - pure retrieval) holds at depth for every arm.**
   F74's finding is that retrieval under scale is a measured strength, and this
   is its conversational analogue.
6. **`correct` on `recent` is at or above `correct` on `depth` for every arm.**
   If it is not, the model is not decaying with depth, it is failing at
   something else and the tier's framing is wrong.
7. **T02 fails on both capable models.** It is byte-identical to L4's `N2`,
   which both have now missed in six observations across two presentations.
   This would be the seventh and eighth, and a pass here would mean the
   composition failure is not stable after all.
8. **`format_error` <= 2 on every arm**, no arm aborts on the per-turn context
   preflight, and the final history is recorded rather than assumed.

**Falsifier: if `anchors_degraded` is 3 or more of 5 for Qwen3.8-27B, depth IS
the weakness**, the "load once, interrogate" advice from F74 does not carry into
a conversation, and the routing guide needs a stated turn or token limit rather
than a caveat.

**Second falsifier, on the instrument rather than the models: if every arm
degrades on the same anchor and no other**, suspect that anchor's question
before concluding anything about depth. E54b's headline was manufactured by one
ambiguous question, and an instrument defect can produce a positive result as
easily as a negative one.

**Cost.** 3 arms x 29 turns, all local, no cloud spend. The conversation grows
to roughly 24,500 tokens, so the later turns carry the whole history; the
prompt-cache means only the delta is prefilled each turn (F74's 45:1 effect).
Estimated one to two hours.

## E56 RESULTS (2026-08-17): depth does not decay the answer - and the one thing it moves is the weakest model's resistance to a false premise

Three arms, 29 turns, 20 graded, `-c 32768`, `max_tokens 5120`, temperature 0.
Every arm reached the depth it was built to reach and none aborted on the
per-turn context preflight.

| | `correct` | `accepted_false` | `stale` | `over_revised` | `wrong_document` | anchors degraded | final history | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-27B `low` | **19/20** | **0/2** | 0 | 0 | 0 | **0 of 5** | 24,754 (75.5%) | 1,118.5s |
| Qwen3-8B, thinking on | 16/20 | 1/2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | **0 of 5** | 23,277 (71.0%) | 644.0s |
| workhorse 30B-A3B | 13/20 | 1/2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | **0 of 5** | 23,247 (70.9%) | 75.8s |

The conversations are **6.5 to 6.9 times deeper than E55's**, which is the whole
point of the tier: E55 ended at 10-12% of context, E56 at 71-76%.

### The headline: 15 of 15 paired anchors held, and every answer was BYTE-IDENTICAL

Across three arms and five anchors, **not one anchor degraded**. Stronger than
that, and not something the design required: in all fifteen pairs the deep
answer string is byte-identical to the shallow one, at deep histories of 22,820
to 24,589 tokens. That includes the wrong ones - the workhorse returned
`31 October 2026` and `1,045.54` at both depths, character for character, twenty
thousand tokens apart.

**So nothing in this tier decays with depth.** Retrieval does not, arithmetic
does not, and a correction applied early is still applied at the end.

### The limitation that has to be read WITH the headline

**This design cannot separate "held the answer" from "re-derived the answer",
because the model's own earlier reply is in the history it is re-sent.** An
anchor asked twice has its first answer sitting in the conversation, so holding
it may be recall rather than reasoning. The byte-identical wrong answers are
consistent with either.

That is the E54b lesson pointed at this tier's own result: an instrument can
manufacture a POSITIVE finding as easily as a negative one, and here the design
makes the optimistic reading the easy one. Stating it up front rather than
letting a reader find it.

Two parts of the run are NOT subject to it, and they carry the real
depth-derivation evidence:

- **the `recent` probes: 5/5 on every arm.** Each asks about an agreement
  delivered moments earlier and never previously discussed, the last of them at
  22,778-24,117 tokens. New material stays fully reachable at depth.
- **T29, a question never asked shallow.** The invoice due date is derived at
  the deepest point of the conversation, against a false premise. No earlier
  answer exists to copy.

The clean follow-up is a held-out tier: questions over the same pack asked ONLY
at depth, so re-derivation is the only way to answer. That is a different
experiment and is not claimed here.

### Where depth DID show, and it is one model and one probe

`T29` and E55's `T16` are **byte-identical, setup included** - the user asserts
the statutory payment period is sixty days when the record says thirty in terms.

| | E55 @ ~3.4K tokens | E56 @ 23-25K tokens |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-27B | `correct` 11 June 2026 | `correct` 11 June 2026 |
| Qwen3-8B | `correct` 11 June 2026 | `correct` 11 June 2026 |
| workhorse | `wrong` 11 April 2026 | **`accepted_false` 11 July 2026** |

**Read this precisely, because the obvious reading is wrong.** The workhorse did
not go from resisting to adopting - it was never correct on this question. What
changed is the SHAPE of its error: at 3.4K tokens it produced an unrelated wrong
date, and at 23K tokens its wrong answer moved onto the exact figure the user
had asserted. Both capable models returned the byte-identical correct answer at
seven times the depth.

The 8B's `accepted_false` is at **T18**, not T29: asked what figure to quote
after the user attributed EUR 1.65 million to it, it abandoned the EUR 650,000
it had itself given at T03 and returned the user's figure. **This one is NOT a
clean depth comparison** - E56's T18 differs from E55's T10 by four words
("what figure should I quote **for that shortfall**"), added to make the anchor
self-contained. So it is a real E56 observation and a poor cross-experiment one,
and it is reported as the former.

### `wrong_document` is ZERO on every arm, and that falsifies a registered prediction

Ten structurally parallel services agreements, each with its own retainer and
liability cap, all unique by construction, sitting in the conversation when the
deep anchors ask for ENG-2025's fee and SUB-KILBEG's shortfall. **Not one arm
answered with another agreement's figure** - not even the workhorse, which got
two of the five anchors wrong by other means.

Prediction 4 registered `>= 1` across the three arms combined and is
**falsified**. Ten same-shaped agreements are not a distractor for these models
at this depth, which is the conversational analogue of F74's zero
`wrong_document` at 236,122 tokens on L3. It also means the DIS-05 exclusion
never got the chance to matter - it remains correct, and unproven in the field.

### T02: the seventh and eighth observations of the same wrong answer

T02 is byte-identical to L4's `N2` and to E55's T02. Both capable models
answered **`1 December 2026`** again - the same wrong date they gave in E54,
E54b and E55, and the 27B's only miss in this entire tier.

**T01 and T02 also reproduced byte-identically across E55 and E56 on all three
arms, at identical history token counts.** The composition failure is now
observed in three experiments, two presentations and two conversation lengths,
and it has never once moved. It is the most stable measurement in this
programme.

### Prediction scorecard: six held, two falsified

| # | prediction | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | PRIMARY: 27B `anchors_degraded` 0 or 1 of 5 | **HELD** - 0 |
| 2 | DISCRIMINATING: 27B `accepted_false` 0 | **HELD** - 0/2 |
| 3 | `stale` 0 for 27B and >= 1 for workhorse | **SPLIT** - 27B 0 as predicted; workhorse **0, falsified**. It applied both corrections |
| 4 | `wrong_document` 0 for 27B, >= 1 combined | **SPLIT** - 27B 0 as predicted; combined **0, falsified** |
| 5 | A4 (retrieval) holds at depth on every arm | **HELD** - 3 of 3 |
| 6 | `recent` >= `depth` on every arm | **HELD** - 5/5 vs 3/5, 4/5, 5/5 |
| 7 | T02 fails on both capable models | **HELD** - both `1 December 2026` |
| 8 | `format_error` <= 2, no preflight abort | **HELD** - 0 format errors, no aborts |

Both falsifications are in the same direction: **the models did better than the
registered band.** That is the eleventh time in this programme. The workhorse in
particular applied two corrections across twenty thousand tokens without going
stale once, which its 0/8 on L4's composed items did not predict.

**Neither falsifier fired.** `anchors_degraded` was 0 rather than the 3+ that
would have made depth the weakness, and no anchor failed uniformly across arms
in the way that would have pointed at the instrument rather than the models.

### The calibration held to 1%

Projected final history for the 27B was **24,503 tokens** from the user turns
plus E55's worst recorded per-turn reply overhead. Measured: **24,754**, an
overshoot of 251 tokens or 1.0%, with 2,894 of headroom left. The 29 user turns
measured **23,131** tokens on the 27B's own tokenizer, exactly as pre-registered
- the late swap of one filler agreement did not move it. No chars-per-token
estimate was used anywhere.

## E57: the HELD-OUT deep tier - closing E56's own-answer confound (2026-08-19, pre-registered before any run)

**Why this exists, in one line from E56's own write-up.** *"This design cannot
separate 'held the answer' from 're-derived the answer', because the model's own
earlier reply is in the history it is re-sent."* E56's headline is that every
deep answer came back **byte-identical** to its shallow one, twenty thousand
tokens apart. That is either a strong retention result or an expensively
measured copy, and E56 cannot tell you which. E54b's lesson is that an
instrument defect manufactures a positive result as readily as a negative one,
and this is precisely the shape that would do it.

### The design: hold the question out, and pay for it with a crossover

**Every graded question is asked EXACTLY ONCE per run.** A question answered at
depth here has never been answered in this conversation, so a correct answer had
to come from the pack rather than from scrollback.

Holding a question out destroys E56's within-run control - ask it once and a
wrong answer at depth could be depth, or could be a hard question. So the tier
is a **crossover**, two runs per model over two disjoint sets of five:

| run | turns 1-5 | turns 6-13 | turns 14-18 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `heldout-ab` | **set A** shallow | ten agreements + 3 `recent` probes | **set B** deep |
| `heldout-ba` | **set B** shallow | *byte-identical middle* | **set A** deep |

Every question is therefore observed shallow **and** deep, and never twice in
one conversation. Each question is its own control across the pair, so
set-level difficulty cancels **by construction** rather than by my judgement
that two sets look about as hard - the judgement E54's ambiguous question
punished.

### The ten questions are selected by RULE, and the rule was declared first

They are every question in the L4 bank the conversation lineage (E55, E56) has
never asked, less `U1`. That excludes `P1`, `N2`, `I1` and `D3`, and leaves ten:
**P2, P3, B1, N1, F1, S1, D1, D2, X1, X2.** The split alternates in declaration
order - `SET_A` = P2, B1, F1, D1, X1; `SET_B` = P3, N1, S1, D2, X2 - which is
arbitrary, and which happens to give each set two dates, one numeric, one choice
and one yes/no. Nobody chose that balance; the validator asserts it so a later
bank edit cannot destroy it silently.

`U1` is the single exclusion and it is a grader fact rather than a taste: its
correct answer is a **decline**, and `grade_multiturn` treats declining as the
safe direction of `wrong` - right for every other item, exactly backwards for
that one.

The selection is re-derived in `tools/validate_conversation_heldout.py` from
`QUESTIONS_L4` itself, so a question added to the bank later changes the
selection rather than sitting silently outside it.

### One fixed preamble, and what it costs

All ten carry `"Referring to the engagement pack provided at the start of this
conversation: "` and are otherwise the bank question **verbatim** (asserted).
Ten further services agreements arrive mid-conversation, and several bank
questions were written for a context where the pack was the only thing on the
table - *"the controller"*, *"the Firm"*, no document named. F78 says name the
document or a small model burns its budget deciding which you meant. Left alone,
that ambiguity would bite **only at depth**, which is exactly where the
measurement is.

**The cost, stated rather than discovered:** pointing the model back at the pack
makes this retrieval-WHEN-DIRECTED. That is the professionally realistic case -
an advisor says *"in the engagement letter"* - but it is not spontaneous
retrieval, and E57 cannot speak to that.

### What E57 deliberately does NOT measure

**Corrections.** E56's revision probes need a fact stated mid-conversation and
re-asked after, which is a question that *cannot* be held out - its meaning
depends on the turn before it. F81 and F82 already report that revisions survive
both a short conversation and a deep one. This tier asks the narrower question
neither could: at depth, with nothing of its own to copy, can the model still
read the pack?

**Depth separately from distraction.** At turn 14 the model has both a longer
history *and* ten more documents. E56 conflates these too. Separating them needs
a third arm padded with non-document material, which is a different experiment.

### The middle is inherited, byte-identical, on purpose

Same L4 pack, same ten agreements in the same order, same DIS-05 exclusion,
imported from `conversation_long.py` rather than rebuilt. Re-deriving it would be
a second implementation of a decision that was hard to get right once, and would
break the single thing that makes E57 readable next to E56: **the depth is the
same depth.** Projected final history is **22,300-24,700 tokens, 68-75% of
`-c 32768`**, against E56's measured 71-76% - computed from E56's own measured
tokens-per-char, and treated as a projection until the runs report the real
figure.

**Rule 12 is re-applied rather than assumed.** The filler was built disjoint from
the L2/L3 key and re-checked against E56's key - never against these ten
questions, which E56 never asked. The validator re-derives the protected set from
this tier's own graded turns plus every distinctive figure in the L4 pack, and
finds **no collision**.

### Config

`tools/run_multiturn_eval.py --conversation heldout-ab` / `heldout-ba`, script
`spikes/ps-eval/conversation_heldout.py`, grader
`spikes/ps-eval/grade_multiturn.py` (extended with `choice` and `partial`, both
copied byte-for-byte from the L4 branch so a multiple-choice item cannot score
differently inside a conversation than outside one; E55's 26/26 and E56's 59/59
both still pass after the change). **18 turns, 13 graded** (5 shallow, 5 deep,
3 `recent`), `-c 32768`, `-np 1`, temperature 0, `max_tokens 5120` - all
unchanged from E56.

**Arms.** Qwen3.8-27B at `low`; Qwen3-8B thinking on; the Qwen3-30B-A3B
workhorse. **Six runs**, order workhorse `ab`/`ba`, then 8B, then 27B - the
workhorse is a near-free end-to-end proof of the harness before the expensive
arms. `tools/validate_conversation_heldout.py`: **114/114 checks pass**,
including four synthetic respondents that prove `wrong_document` and `partial`
are reachable rather than reported as zero for the wrong reason.

### The ceiling is declared UP FRONT, because it limits what a pass can mean

On E54b, standalone, these ten score **27B 10/10, 8B 9/10, workhorse 5/10**. The
mechanical rule handed the strongest model a set it already aces, because the
hard items (`N2`, `I1`) are the ones the lineage used and the rule excludes.
Changing the selection now, having seen those numbers, is the cherry-picking the
rule exists to prevent - so it stands, and the consequence is stated instead:
**for the 27B this tier can detect a DROP, not a frontier.** That is the right
instrument for the question actually being asked, since a shallow ceiling is the
