same bank is **23/24**. So this experiment cannot make the resident model
competitive with the model swap, and is not trying to: it decides whether the
tool is worth having on the model that is already loaded.

**The economics the router has to beat**, from the same arms:

| | rate |
|---|---|
| tool offered on a band-R item -> gains an item | 3/12 = **0.25** |
| tool offered on a band-E item -> loses an item | 5/12 = **0.42** capability, 6/12 = 0.50 including the HTTP 500 |

A router may therefore misfire on band E at no more than about **0.6x** its
band-R hit rate before the tool stops paying for itself. Precision matters more
than recall here, and `tools/tool_router.py` breaks ties toward NOT offering for
that reason.

### The arms

Answering model is Qwen3-30B-A3B throughout. The router sees the **question
only**, never the pack - a router that had to read the record to decide would
cost about what answering costs, which is what E75 found when disagreement
routing turned out not to be cheaper than the work it routed.

| arm | router |
|---|---|
| **R1** | `rule` - deterministic patterns, no inference, no latency |
| **R2** | `model` - the workhorse routes ITSELF, one YES/NO call per question, `router_thinking=off` |
| **R3** | `model` - **Qwen3-8B** routes, workhorse answers. The plan's H18 specialist-small-model claim |

### R1 IS FITTED AND ITS SCORE IS NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT ROUTING

`rule_router` was authored with this bank visible. Checked against the band
labels before registration it scores **12/12 band-R recall and 0/12 band-E false
positives** - it is the oracle by construction. **That number is declared here so
nobody reads it later as a result.**

R1 is still worth running, for one narrow reason: it proves the routed PIPELINE
reproduces the spliced oracle end to end. If R1 does not land on 16/24, the
splice above is wrong and every figure in this entry is suspect. It is a control,
not a finding, and the entry will report it as one.

**R2 and R3 are fitted to nothing** and they are the experiment.

### The harness gate, run before this registration

`tools/run_h6_date_arm.py` gained `--tools routed`, `--router`,
`--router-base-url` and `--router-thinking`; the per-item decision is recorded in
each result row. Four cells, rule router, declared and unscored:

| item | band | tool offered | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| `R03` | R | yes | `correct` - one `add_business_days` call |
| `R11` | R | yes | `off_by_calendar` - `date_diff` returned an exclusive 274, answered 274 |
| `E02` | E | **no** | **`correct`, 96,000** - the item arm B destroyed by spending six rounds on date arithmetic |
| `E09` | E | **no** | `correct` - the item arm B lost to an HTTP 500 |

### Predictions, each naming the FIELD it is scored against

| # | prediction | scored against |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **control:** the routed pipeline reproduces the splice | R1 `total` = **16/24**, band R 6/12, band E 10/12 |
| 2 | **DISCRIMINATING: the model cannot tell a counting question from a lookup one.** E79 saw it call tools on 10 of 12 band-E items when merely offered | R2 band-E false positives **>= 4 of 12** |
| 3 | self-routing does not meaningfully beat not routing | R2 `total` **<= 14/24**, against arm A's 13 |
| 4 | the small specialist routes better than the answerer | R3 band-E false positives **<** R2 band-E false positives |
| 5 | no router beats perfect routing | every routed arm `total` **<= 16/24** |
| 6 | routing cannot manufacture a conversion the tool did not make | every routed arm band R `correct` **<= 6 of 12** |
| 7 | the YES/NO reply is parseable | `routing.parsed` false on **<= 1 of 24** in each of R2 and R3 |

**Prediction 2 is the one that decides the branch.** If the workhorse can route
itself, the tool becomes deployable on the resident model for the price of one
short call per question. If it cannot - and E79's behavioural evidence says it
may not - then aiming the tool needs a second model, at which point the honest
comparison is against simply using that second model to answer.

### Registered decision rule, tie-break included

| observed | action |
|---|---|
| R2 `total` >= 16/24 with band-E false positives <= 2 | **the tool is deployable on the resident model.** Recommend a tool-routing rule for the routing guide, with the per-question router call named as its cost |
| R2 `total` is 14-15 | **partial and honest:** report the gain and the router's error rates, and recommend nothing until a second bank confirms it. 24 items cannot support a serving change on a 1-2 item margin |
| R2 `total` <= 13 (arm A) | **self-routing fails.** The tools branch on this model needs a second model to aim it, and that comparison belongs against the model swap, not against arm A |
| R3 beats R2 by >= 3 with band-E FP <= 2 | the H18 specialist claim is supported HERE, and the next question is whether a 5 GiB router plus a 17 GiB answerer beats a 17 GiB answerer that is simply better - which is a memory-budget question, not a routing one |
| R1 != 16/24 | **stop.** The splice is invalid, the oracle figure is withdrawn, and nothing else in this entry may be quoted until the discrepancy is resolved |
| **tie-break:** R2 and R3 both land at 14-15 with band-E FP of exactly 3 | ambiguous. Do NOT recommend; report both error rates and note that the deciding measurement is a second bank, not a third router |

### Conditions, declared

- **Rule 9 breached and acknowledged; all wall times VOID.** The router's cost is
  therefore reported as **extra calls per question**, not as latency.
- `--router-thinking off` on both model routers. A router that reasons for forty
  seconds costs more than the answer it is aiming.
- R3 needs two servers resident: Qwen3-8B (~5 GiB) routing and the workhorse
  (~17 GiB) answering, plus the relay's 29.3 GiB - about **51 GiB**, clear of the
  60 GiB regime in `docs/memory-edge-deadlock.md`.
- An unparseable router reply is treated as NO and counted, never guessed.

**Evidence to be written:** `results/raw/e80-r{1,2,3}-l5.json`,
`results/raw/e80-scores.json`.


## E80 RESULT - the model CAN route itself, the small specialist cannot, and the margin is inside the harness's own noise. PREDICTIONS 2, 3 AND 4 FALSIFIED. (2026-08-28)

Three routed arms, 24 items, answering model Qwen3-30B-A3B throughout, tier
`l5`, `-c 16384`, `--jinja`, `-fa on`, `--max-rounds 6`, `router_thinking=off`,
kernel `7.0.0-29-generic`. **Rule 9 breached and acknowledged; all wall times
VOID.** Router cost is reported as extra calls, not latency.

| arm | router | total | band R | band E | band-R offered | **band-E false positives** | unparsed | vs tools-off |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **R1** | rule (**fitted**) | **16/24** | 6/12 | 10/12 | 12/12 | **0/12** | 0 | **+3** |
| **R2** | the workhorse routes itself | **15/24** | 5/12 | 10/12 | 12/12 | **3/12** | 0 | **+2** |
| **R3** | Qwen3-8B routes | **12/24** | 6/12 | **6/12** | 12/12 | **6/12** | 0 | **-1** |

Reference points: E79 arm A tools-off **13/24**; the spliced oracle **16/24**;
E78's tool-free Qwen3.8 on the same bank **23/24**.

### THE ANSWER

> **The production model can route itself, and it was the small specialist that
> could not.** Asked one YES/NO question about the question, the workhorse
> misfired on 3 of 12 band-E items and lost nothing to them - its band E stayed
> at 10/12, identical to not routing at all. Qwen3-8B misfired on **6 of 12**
> and took the system to **12/24, worse than not routing.**

**Prediction 2 is the one I got wrong, and the reason is worth more than the
prediction.** I registered that the workhorse would misfire on at least 4 of 12,
on the strength of E79's behavioural evidence that it *called* the tool on 10 of
12 band-E items when the tool was merely offered. It misfired on 3.

> **Deciding implicitly whether to use a tool, and answering explicitly whether a
> question needs one, are different capabilities in the same model.** E79's
> behaviour did not predict E80's classification. A model that reaches for a date
> tool on a liability-cap question will, if asked first, correctly say that
> question does not need counting.

### The H18 specialist claim is falsified in the damaging direction

Prediction 4 registered that the small model would route BETTER. It routed twice
as badly - 6 false positives against 3 - and four of the six destroyed their
item (`E02`, `E03`, `E05`, `E08` to `format_error`). The plan's H18 proposes
small specialists for exactly this role. **On this task the 5 GiB specialist was
worse than the 17 GiB generalist doing the job itself, and worse than doing
nothing.**

### R1 was the registered stop-condition and it passed

R1 landed on **16/24, band R 6/12, band E 10/12** - the spliced oracle exactly.
The registered rule was that any other figure invalidates the splice and
withdraws the 16/24 ceiling from the record. It held, so the ceiling stands and
R2 and R3 are measurable against it.

**R1 remains fitted and is not evidence about routing.** Its 12/12 recall and
0/12 false positives were authored with the bank visible and were declared
before the run.

### R2's three misfires are two defensible readings and one real error

| item | router said | is it wrong? |
|---|---|---|
| `E05` | YES | *"HOW MANY state a Notice Period of their own, and which ones?"* - the answer contains a count. A router answering YES is defensible |
| `E08` | YES | *"...what Acceptance Window does that Call-Off Order state? Give the document ID and the number of Business Days."* - also asks for a number |
| `E12` | YES | *"How many employees does Northgate Systems have?"* - counting LANGUAGE over an absent fact. The only clear misroute |

The band label marks what makes an item **hard**, not whether a number appears in
the answer, so the raw false-positive metric is harsher on this router than the
questions warrant. **None of the three cost an item.**

### THE CAVEAT THAT BOUNDS THE HEADLINE, and it is a real one

Outcomes under tool offering are **not fully reproducible across arms in this
harness.** Of the items offered the tool in more than one arm:

| item | E79-B | E80-R2 | E80-R3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `E02`, `E03` | format_error | (not offered) | format_error |
| `E12` | correct | correct | correct |
| `E05` | correct | correct | **format_error** |
| `E08` | **format_error** | **correct** | format_error |
| `R09` | correct | **off_by_calendar** | correct |

**Three cells diverge, and two of them are in R2** - the only arm that shares one
server between routing and answering, so its answering requests follow router
traffic through the same slot and prompt cache. That is a **candidate mechanism,
named and NOT established**: the multi-round tool loop injects tool results into
the context, so cache state differs from a cold slot in a way single-turn work
does not, and E77's measured zero noise floor was for single-turn answers.

**What it costs the headline, stated rather than buried:** had `E08` died as it
did in the other two arms and `R09` lived as it did in the other two, R2 would
read anywhere from **14/24 to 16/24**. So **R2's +2 carries a +/-1 to 2 item
instability that this experiment measured and did not control.** No conclusion
below leans on the exact figure.

### Scoring

| # | prediction | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | R1 = 16/24, band R 6/12, band E 10/12 | **HELD exactly** - the splice is valid and the ceiling stands |
| 2 | R2 band-E false positives >= 4 of 12 | **FALSIFIED** - 3, and none cost an item |
| 3 | R2 `total` <= 14/24 | **FALSIFIED** - 15 |
| 4 | R3 band-E false positives < R2's | **FALSIFIED in the opposite direction** - 6 against 3 |
| 5 | every routed arm `total` <= 16/24 | **HELD** - 16, 15, 12 |
| 6 | every routed arm band R `correct` <= 6/12 | **HELD** - 6, 5, 6 |
| 7 | `routing.parsed` false on <= 1 of 24 in R2 and R3 | **HELD** - zero in both |

### The registered decision rule fires on its middle branch

> *"R2 `total` is 14-15 -> partial and honest: report the gain and the router's
> error rates, and recommend nothing until a second bank confirms it. 24 items
> cannot support a serving change on a 1-2 item margin."*

**R2 is 15/24. Nothing is recommended and the routing guide does not change.**
The instability documented above makes that branch more right than it was when
it was written: a +2 margin with a +/-2 wobble is not a serving decision.

The R3 branch - *"R3 beats R2 by >= 3 ... the H18 specialist claim is supported
HERE"* - does not fire, and its inverse is the finding.

### What survives, and what it means for the programme

- **Routing works in principle and the ceiling is small.** Perfect routing is
  +3 of 24; the best real router got +2, inside its own noise. The tools branch
  is not dead, and it is not worth a serving change on this evidence.
- **The router does not have to be a second model.** That was the assumption
  behind sending this question to H18, and it was wrong here.
- **Even perfectly aimed, the tool leaves a lot on the table.** R1 offered the
  tool on exactly the right twelve items and still logged `result_ignored` four
  times and `wrong_args` twice - band R 6/12 against Qwen3.8's tool-free 11/12.
  **Perfect aiming does not produce perfect use**, and the gap between the two is
  the same reasoning capability the tool was brought in to substitute for.

### What this does NOT establish

- **One bank, 24 items, 12 per band.** Every figure carries an interval wider
  than the +2 it reports.
- **One question form for the router.** A different prompt might route better or
  worse; only `ROUTER_PROMPT` at `tool-router-v1-2026-08-28` was measured.
- **The divergence mechanism is unresolved.** The shared-server hypothesis is a
  candidate. **Reopen condition:** re-run R2 with `--router-base-url` pointing at
  a second copy of the workhorse, so routing and answering never share a slot. If
  the three divergent cells stop diverging, the mechanism is the cache and every
  multi-round tool figure in E79 and E80 needs that control.
- **Nothing about latency.** Rule 9 breached; the router's cost is one extra
  short call per question and is reported as such.

**Evidence:** `results/raw/e80-r{1,2,3}-l5.json`, `results/raw/e80-scores.json`.


## E80 ADDENDUM - PRE-REGISTRATION: is the divergence router traffic on the answering slot? (2026-08-28)

**Registered before the control runs.** E80's entry named a reopen condition and
this executes it, with one substitution declared up front.

### The literal control is REFUSED on memory grounds

The reopen condition as written was *"re-run R2 with `--router-base-url` pointing
at a second copy of the workhorse"*. Priced before being attempted:

| | |
|---|---|
| answering workhorse, `-c 16384` | ~18.8 GiB |
| second workhorse as router, `-c 2048` | ~17.5 GiB |
| sparkrouter relay, resident and measured | **29.307 GiB** |
| **total** | **~65.5 GiB** |

That is over the ~60 GiB regime in `docs/memory-edge-deadlock.md`, unattended,
on an account that cannot power-cycle the box. **It is not run.** The condition
was written without pricing it, which is the error being corrected here.

### The substitute isolates the same variable more tightly

`--router fixed --router-decisions` replays R2's recorded per-item decisions and
makes **no router call at all**. Against R2 that changes exactly one thing:
whether router traffic passed through the answering slot before the answer.
Same model, same 15-of-24 decisions, same prompts, one server, ~18.8 GiB.

It is a better control than the two-server version, which would have varied
slot-sharing AND introduced a second resident process competing for bandwidth.

### Predictions, each naming the FIELD it is scored against

R2 diverged from every no-router-traffic arm on exactly two cells. The control
says which side they land on.

| # | prediction | scored against |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `R09` returns to the value every other arm gave | `R09` outcome = **`correct`** (R1, R3 and E79-B all `correct`; R2 alone `off_by_calendar`) |
| 2 | `E08` returns to the value the other tool-offered arms gave | `E08` outcome = **`format_error`** (E79-B and R3 both `format_error`; R2 alone `correct`) |
| 3 | validity check, not a finding | the replay arm offers the tool on exactly **15 of 24** items, matching R2 by construction |

### Registered decision rule

| observed | action |
|---|---|
| predictions 1 and 2 both hold | **the mechanism is router traffic on the answering slot.** Record it as a harness property, and note that every multi-round tool figure in E79 and E80 carries a per-item instability of this size |
| neither holds - the replay reproduces R2 | **the shared-slot hypothesis is REFUTED.** The divergence is something else and stays unresolved; do not offer a mechanism |
| exactly one holds | **unresolved, and say so.** One cell either way is not a mechanism, and a 1-of-2 result must not be reported as partial support |
| the replay arm's decisions are not 15 of 24 | the replay is broken. Stop and fix before reading anything else |

**No headline moves whichever way this lands.** E80 already recommends nothing,
and this decides whether the instability gets a named cause or stays an
unexplained wobble.

**Evidence to be written:** `results/raw/e80-r2ctl-l5.json`.

## E80 ADDENDUM RESULT - it IS router traffic on the answering slot. Both predictions held, and a replicate closed the alternative. (2026-08-28)

| | `R09` | `E08` | total | band R | band E | tool offered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E79-B (no router traffic) | correct | format_error | - | - | - | on |
| E80-R3 (router on a SEPARATE server) | correct | format_error | 12/24 | 6/12 | 6/12 | routed |
| **E80-R2 (router SHARES the answering server)** | **off_by_calendar** | **correct** | 15/24 | 5/12 | 10/12 | routed |
| **CONTROL - R2's decisions replayed, no router call** | **correct** | **format_error** | 15/24 | 6/12 | 9/12 | routed |

### Scoring

| # | prediction | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `R09` = `correct` in the control | **HELD** |
| 2 | `E08` = `format_error` in the control | **HELD** |
| 3 | the control offers the tool on 15 of 24 | **HELD** - identical to R2 by construction |

**The control differs from R2 on exactly the two predicted cells and no others.**
Twenty-two of twenty-four reproduce R2 precisely.

### The replicate closes the alternative explanation

Two predicted cells could equally have been a near-boundary wobble that flips on
any re-run, which would make the control a coincidence rather than a mechanism.
So the control was run a second time, same configuration:

> **24 of 24 answers byte-identical. 24 of 24 call counts identical. Zero
> differing outcomes.**

**The multi-round tool loop is fully deterministic when the answering slot sees
no router traffic.** So the difference from R2 is attributable to the one
variable the control changed.

### The registered rule fires

> *"Predictions 1 and 2 both hold -> the mechanism is router traffic on the
> answering slot."*

**Recorded as a harness property, and it is narrow:** with `-np 1`, a router
request served by the SAME `llama-server` process passes through the same slot
and prompt cache before the answer, and in a multi-round tool loop that is enough
to change an outcome. E77 measured a zero noise floor for single-turn answers on
this model; that result does not extend to this loop, and now the boundary
between the two is measured rather than assumed.

**Which figures this touches, stated exactly so nobody over-corrects:** only
**E80's R2**. E79's arms make no router calls, E80's R1 makes none, and E80's R3
routes on a separate server. **No headline moves** - R2 is 15/24 either way, the
decision rule's middle branch fires either way, and E80 recommends nothing either
way. What changes is the composition: the control's band R 6/12 and band E 9/12
is the cleaner measurement of routing with R2's decisions.

### One divergence is NOT explained, and it is the more interesting one

E80 recorded three divergent cells. This control explains two. **`E05` is not one
of them**: it diverged in R3, whose answering server never saw a router call
(the 8B routed on a separate port). So router traffic cannot be its cause.

What R3 did have was a different **history through the answering slot** - it
offered the tool on 6 band-E items against R2's 3, so more tool loops ran before
`E05` arrived. That suggests the general form: **the answering slot's history
affects outcomes in a multi-round loop, whether that history is router calls or
earlier tool loops.** The control establishes the first. **The second is a
hypothesis and is not established here**, and the cheap test is a fixed-decision
arm run in two different item orders.

### The reusable rule this earns

> **Do not share one `llama-server` between a router and the answerer it routes
> for.** It costs a second process, and the alternative is a per-item
> instability that looks exactly like a capability difference.

The corrected reopen condition for anyone repeating this: the literal two-model
control is ~65.5 GiB alongside the resident relay and must not be run
unattended. Replaying recorded decisions isolates the same variable at ~18.8 GiB.

**Evidence:** `results/raw/e80-r2ctl-l5.json`,
`results/raw/e80-r2ctl-rep-l5.json` (the replicate).


## E81 PRE-REGISTRATION - is it slot HISTORY, or is it PREFIX DISPLACEMENT? (2026-08-28)

**Registered before either arm runs.** No arm has been executed and no answer
read.

### Why this experiment exists

E80's addendum established that a router request served by the same
`llama-server` changes answers in the multi-round tool loop, and left a general
form untested: *"the answering slot's history affects outcomes, whether that
history is router calls or earlier tool loops."* `E05` diverged in R3, whose
answering server saw no router call, so something beyond router traffic is
unaccounted for.

**The general form is probably wrong, and this says why before testing it.**
Every answering request in this bank begins with the identical 8,807-character
pack. Prompt-cache reuse keys on the longest common prefix, so reordering items
changes which item ran last but not what the cache can reuse. A **router**
request is different in kind: it carries no pack at all, shares no prefix with
the answering prompt, and therefore displaces what the slot had cached.

So the hypothesis under test is narrower than "history matters":

> **H-DISPLACE: what changes an outcome is a request that shares NO PREFIX with
> the answering prompt, not the sequence of answering requests.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **which success question** | none directly - this is instrument work that decides how much of E79 and E80 is measuring the harness |
| **uncertainty reduced** | whether every multi-round tool figure in this repository needs an ordering control, or only an interleaving one |
| **decision that changes** | whether the E80 rule stays *"never share a server between router and answerer"* or widens to *"fix the item order too"*, which would be far more expensive |

### The two arms, both replaying R2's fixed decisions

Every arm uses `--router fixed` with `results/raw/e80-r2-decisions.json`, so
**no routing decision varies anywhere in this experiment.** The baseline is the
E80 control, which was run twice and was 24/24 byte-identical, so any change
here is the manipulation and not noise.

| arm | manipulation | what it isolates |
|---|---|---|
| **O1** | `--order reverse` | item ORDER, with no foreign prefix introduced |
| **O2** | `--interleave-dummy`, bank order | a router-shaped request before each item whose answer is **discarded** - foreign prefix, zero routing effect |

**O2 is the decisive arm.** It reproduces R2's request pattern exactly while
using R2's already-fixed decisions, so if displacement is the mechanism it
should reproduce R2's outcomes - including the two cells R2 alone got.

### Predictions, each naming the FIELD it is scored against

| # | prediction | scored against |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **order does not matter** | O1 differs from the E80 control on **0 of 24** outcomes |
| 2 | order does not even change the text | O1 is byte-identical to the E80 control on **24 of 24** answers |
| 3 | **DECISIVE: displacement reproduces R2** | O2 `R09` = `off_by_calendar` and `E08` = `correct` - the two cells R2 alone produced |
| 4 | and reproduces it exactly | O2 differs from E80-R2 on **0 of 24** outcomes |
| 5 | the two manipulations are not the same thing | O1 and O2 differ from each other on **>= 1** outcome |

**Prediction 1 is registered as a NULL and I expect it to hold.** A null result
here is the useful one: it means the ordering control nobody has been running
was never needed, and the cheap rule E80 already wrote is sufficient.

### Registered decision rule, tie-break included

| observed | action |
|---|---|
| P1 and P3 both hold | **H-DISPLACE confirmed.** The E80 rule stands unchanged and is sufficient; `E05`'s R3 divergence is attributed to the same cause, since R3 offered the tool on twice as many band-E items and its loops carry non-pack tool-result context |
| P1 holds, P3 fails | displacement is not the mechanism either. **Both explanations die** and the instability returns to unexplained - say so and stop, rather than reaching for a third story |
| P1 fails - order alone moves an outcome | **the expensive outcome.** Item order is a live variable, every multi-round figure in E79/E80 needs an ordering control, and the E80 rule is insufficient. Report it loudly; it is the result that costs the most to have missed |
| **tie-break:** P1 fails AND P3 holds | both matter. Do NOT rank them from one run each - report both and register a replicate before any rule is written |
| O2's discarded router call errors on more than 1 item | the dummy is not clean. Fix before scoring |

### Conditions

- Rule 9 breached and acknowledged; wall times VOID.
- One server, `-c 16384`, `-fa on`, `--jinja`, `--max-rounds 6`,
  `--router-thinking off`, ~18.8 GiB alongside the relay's 29.307.
- The baseline is `results/raw/e80-r2ctl-l5.json`, whose replicate was
  byte-identical, so the noise floor for this comparison is measured at zero.

**Evidence to be written:** `results/raw/e81-o1-reverse-l5.json`,
`results/raw/e81-o2-dummy-l5.json`.

## E81 RESULT - both mechanisms are real. Displacement reproduces R2 EXACTLY; order changes text deterministically. PREDICTIONS 1 AND 2 FALSIFIED. (2026-08-28)

All arms replay `e80-r2-decisions.json`, so **no routing decision varied
anywhere in this experiment.** One server, `-c 16384`, `-fa on`, Rule 9 breached,
wall times VOID.

| comparison | differing outcomes | byte-identical answers |
|---|---|---|
| **O2** (discarded router-shaped request) **vs E80-R2** | **0 of 24** | **24 of 24** |
| **O1** (reverse order) **vs the E80 control** | 1 of 24 (`R10`) | 22 of 24 |
| O1 vs its own replicate | **0 of 24** | **24 of 24** |
| O1 vs O2 | 3 of 24 | 17 of 24 |

### H-DISPLACE is confirmed, and the confirmation is exact

**O2 fired a router-shaped request before each item and threw the answer away.
It reproduced E80-R2 byte-for-byte on all 24 answers** - including the two cells
R2 alone produced, `R09` = `off_by_calendar` and `E08` = `correct`.

> **The routing had nothing to do with it. The request's mere presence did.**
> A request sharing no prefix with the answering prompt displaces the cached
> pack, and in a multi-round tool loop that is enough to change an answer.

### But my registered NULL was wrong, and order matters too

I predicted order would change nothing and gave a mechanism for it: every
answering request opens with the same 8,807-character pack, so reuse should key
on the same prefix regardless of sequence. **Predictions 1 and 2 are falsified.**

| item | bank order | reverse order | reverse, replicated |
|---|---|---|---|
| `R07` | `1074.47`, wrong | **`434.87`**, wrong | `434.87`, wrong |
| `R10` | `14 December 2025`, wrong | **HTTP 500**, transport_failed | HTTP 500, transport_failed |

**And reversal is deterministic.** The replicate is 24 of 24 byte-identical to
O1, so these are not flakes: the same order produces the same output twice, and
a different order produces a different output reproducibly.

`R10` is the one to look at twice. **A reproducible HTTP 500 that occurs under
reverse order and never under bank order** is a server failure contingent on
request history, not a random fault - and the same session saw one other HTTP
500 (E79 arm B, `E09`), also inside a tool loop. That is a concrete artefact for
anyone who wants to chase a `llama-server` bug; this experiment only records it.

### Scoring

| # | prediction | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | O1 differs from the control on 0 of 24 outcomes | **FALSIFIED** - 1, `R10` |
| 2 | O1 byte-identical to the control on 24 of 24 | **FALSIFIED** - 22 of 24 |
| 3 | **DECISIVE:** O2 `R09` = `off_by_calendar` and `E08` = `correct` | **HELD** |
| 4 | O2 differs from E80-R2 on 0 of 24 | **HELD** - and byte-identical too |
| 5 | O1 and O2 differ from each other on >= 1 | **HELD** - 3 |

### The tie-break fired, the replicate it demanded was run, and only now the rule

The registered tie-break: *"P1 fails AND P3 holds -> both matter. Do NOT rank
them from one run each - report both and register a replicate before any rule is
written."* That is exactly what happened, the replicate was run, and it settled
that the order effect is real rather than noise.

**The rule, now that it is earned:**

> **In a multi-round tool loop on one slot, both the request HISTORY and the
> item ORDER are live variables.** E80's rule - never share a server between a
> router and its answerer - is **necessary and not sufficient**. An arm's item
> order is part of its configuration and must be held constant across any
> comparison.

### What this costs E79 and E80, measured rather than feared

**Every arm in E79 and E80 ran in bank order.** The order variable was therefore
held constant across every comparison already made, and no headline moves.

The size of the effect is small and now measured: **reversal changed 2 of 24
answers' text and ZERO capability verdicts.** `R07` was wrong before and wrong
after; `R10`'s verdict change is a transport failure, not a capability one.

What it does touch is **per-item** claims. E79 and E80 name specific items as
converted or regressed, and those attributions are now known to be
order-contingent at about the 8%-of-items level for text and 0% for verdicts on
this bank. **The band totals and the between-arm comparisons stand; a claim
about one named cell carries this caveat.**

### What this does NOT establish

- **One bank, one reversal, one model.** Reverse is a single alternative order,
  not a sample of orders; a shuffle study would bound the effect properly and
  was not run.
- **The prefix-displacement mechanism is confirmed by REPRODUCTION, not by
  instrumentation.** No cache metric was read from the server. O2 reproducing R2
  byte-for-byte is strong, and it is still behavioural evidence.
- **`E05`'s R3 divergence is now attributable but not demonstrated.** R3 ran
  twice as many band-E tool loops, so its slot history differed - consistent
  with both mechanisms confirmed here, tested by neither.

**Evidence:** `results/raw/e81-o1-reverse-l5.json`,
`results/raw/e81-o1-reverse-rep-l5.json`, `results/raw/e81-o2-dummy-l5.json`.


## E82 PRE-REGISTRATION - bounding the order effect: ten shuffled orders (2026-08-28)

**Registered before any shuffled order runs.** No shuffle has been executed.

### Why this experiment exists

E81 established item order as a live variable in the multi-round tool loop and
bounded it from a **single** alternative order: reverse changed 2 of 24 answers'
text and 0 capability verdicts, deterministically. E81's own limits section said
that is not a sample of orders and that a shuffle study would bound it properly.

**This is that study, and the number it exists to produce is one line:** *by how
much can an arm's total on this bank move, on this instrument, from item order
alone?* Every per-item claim in E79 and E80 inherits the answer.

| | |
|---|---|
| **which success question** | none - instrument work, and it prices the caveat every earlier entry now carries |
| **uncertainty reduced** | whether E79 and E80's between-arm comparisons can stand on one order each |
| **decision that changes** | whether the E81 rule (hold order constant) is sufficient, or whether single-order arms have to be re-run across orders before their per-item claims mean anything |

### The design

Ten shuffled orders, seeds **1 to 10**, permutation derived from the seed alone
and recorded in each result file with the resulting `order_ids`, so any run is
reproducible from its own output. Everything else is held: `--router fixed`
replaying `e80-r2-decisions.json`, one server, `-c 16384`, `-fa on`,
`--max-rounds 6`, no interleaved request.

Four runs are already banked and are the reference points, not new arms: bank
order twice (24/24 byte-identical to each other) and reverse order twice (24/24
byte-identical to each other). **The noise floor at fixed order is therefore
measured at zero**, so everything this study sees is order.

### Predictions, each naming the FIELD it is scored against

| # | prediction | scored against |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the total is stable | **spread** (max minus min) of `total correct` across the ten orders **<= 2** |
| 2 | verdicts are much more stable than text | items with **>1 distinct verdict** across the ten orders **<= 3 of 24** |
| 3 | text moves more than verdicts, and more than reverse alone showed | items with **>1 distinct answer text** **>= 3 of 24** |
| 4 | the order-contingent server fault recurs | at least one shuffled order produces a `transport_failed`, as reverse did on `R10` |
| 5 | band E is the stabler band - its items are single-round lookups, not tool loops | items with >1 distinct verdict in band E **<=** the same count in band R |

**Prediction 1 carries the cost.** A spread of 0-1 means E79 and E80's
between-arm gaps - +3 for the tool on band R, -5 on band E, +2 for the best
router - are safely larger than the order noise. A spread of 4 or more would put
E80's entire +2 inside it.

### Registered decision rule, tie-break included

| observed | action |
|---|---|
| spread <= 1 | order is a nuisance and the E81 rule is sufficient. Record the bound and change nothing |
| spread 2-3 | **material.** Every reported total in E79/E80 gains this bound as a stated caveat, and no future claim smaller than the bound may be made from a single order |
| spread >= 4 | **the expensive branch.** Single-order arms cannot support per-item comparisons. E79's conversion and regression lists and E80's router comparison must be re-run across at least three orders before they are quoted again |
| **tie-break:** spread is exactly 2 but driven ENTIRELY by `transport_failed` | that is infrastructure, not order-dependent capability. Report the capability-only spread as the headline and the raw spread beside it - do not let a server fault inflate a capability bound |
| any run fails to produce 24 results | that order is declared and excluded, and the exclusion is reported with the seed |

**Evidence to be written:** `results/raw/e82-shuffle-seed{1..10}-l5.json`,
`results/raw/e82-scores.json`.

## E82 RESULT - the order effect is 2 items, and E80's entire router margin sits inside it. PREDICTION 2 FALSIFIED. (2026-08-28)

Twelve orders of the same 24 items: ten seeded shuffles (seeds 1-10), plus bank
order and reverse order from the banked runs. **All replay
`e80-r2-decisions.json`, so no routing decision varied anywhere.** One server,
Rule 9 breached, wall times VOID.

| total | orders |
|---|---|
| 14/24 | seeds 1, 4, 9 |
| 15/24 | seeds 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, **bank**, **reverse** |
| 16/24 | seed 6 |

### THE NUMBER

> **Item order alone moves this arm's total across a range of 2 items,
> 14 to 16 of 24.** The noise floor at FIXED order is zero - bank order and
> reverse order were each run twice and each pair was 24/24 byte-identical - so
> the whole of this range is order.

**And it is capability, not infrastructure.** The registered tie-break covers a
spread of exactly 2 driven by transport faults; it does not apply. Only `R10`
ever hits a runner-owned outcome, and **it is `wrong` in every run that
completes it**, so a transport fault costs zero correct answers and cannot have
moved the total.

### What sits inside the bound, stated plainly

| claim | size | against a 2-item order bound |
|---|---|---|
| E80: the best router's gain over not routing | **+2** | **entirely inside it** |
| E79: the tool's gain on band R | +3 | just outside |
| E79: the tool's loss on band E | -5 | outside |
| E78: band R separation, workhorse to Qwen3.8 | 8 | far outside |
| E78: band E headroom | 2 | **entirely inside it** |

**E80 recommended nothing on a +2 margin. This says that was right for a reason
E80 could not yet quote: the margin equals the order noise.** The decision rule
there fired on judgement about a small sample; it now has a measurement behind it.

**E78's two-item band-E headroom is also inside the bound** - which does NOT
weaken E78's conclusion, it strengthens it. The claim was that context
engineering has almost nothing to recover; a headroom indistinguishable from
ordering noise is a smaller target, not a larger one.

### Instability, per item

| | count | items |
|---|---|---|
| >1 distinct **verdict** across 12 orders | **4 of 24** | `E05`, `E08` (correct / format_error), `R09` (correct / off_by_calendar), `R10` (wrong / transport_failed) |
| >1 distinct **answer text** | **8 of 24** | `E05`, `E07`, `E08`, `R04`, `R07`, `R08`, `R09`, `R10` |

By band: verdict instability **R=2, E=2**; text instability **R=5, E=3**.

**Every unstable item is one the tool was offered on.** The 9 items where the
replayed decisions withheld the tool did not move at all, in verdict or in text,
across twelve orders. The instability is a property of the multi-round tool loop,
not of the bank.

### Scoring

| # | prediction | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | spread of `total correct` <= 2 | **HELD at the boundary** - exactly 2 |
| 2 | items with >1 distinct verdict <= 3 of 24 | **FALSIFIED** - 4 |
| 3 | items with >1 distinct text >= 3 of 24 | **HELD** - 8, against the 2 that reverse alone revealed |
| 4 | at least one shuffled order produces a `transport_failed` | **HELD** - seeds 3, 5, 7, 8 |
| 5 | band E verdict instability <= band R | **HELD** - equal at 2 each |

**Prediction 3 is the one worth keeping.** Reverse order alone surfaced 2
unstable texts; twelve orders surfaced **8**. A single alternative order
understated the effect fourfold, which is the argument for having run this at
all rather than quoting E81's reverse-only figure.

### The registered rule fires on `spread 2-3`

> *"Material. Every reported total in E79/E80 gains this bound as a stated
> caveat, and no future claim smaller than the bound may be made from a single
> order."*

**Applied:** E79's band-level gains (+3, -5) and E78's band separation (8) stand
clear of it. **E80's +2 does not**, and E80's own conclusion - recommend nothing -
is unchanged and now better supported. No result is withdrawn.

**The standing rule this leaves:** on this instrument, **a difference of 2 items
or fewer, measured from a single item order, is not a result.** Three orders
minimum for any claim that small.

### What this does NOT establish

- **One arm, one bank, one model.** The bound is for the workhorse on L5 with 15
  of 24 items receiving a tool. An arm with no tool offered would likely be
  perfectly stable - the 9 withheld items were - and one with tools everywhere
  would likely be worse.
- **Twelve orders is not a distribution.** The range is 14-16; nothing here
  supports a variance or a confidence interval, and none is quoted.
- **The mechanism is not re-derived.** E81 established prefix displacement and
  order as live variables; this measures the size of the second and does not
  revisit why.

**Evidence:** `results/raw/e82-shuffle-seed{1..10}-l5.json`,
`results/raw/e82-scores.json`.


## E83 PRE-REGISTRATION - gpt-oss-120b C01/C06: the two cells the corrected coding total left unknown (2026-08-28)

**Registered before the model is loaded.** No gpt-oss run has been started in
this window. The box is idle and the gateway is down (measured below).

### Why this experiment exists

The corrected local coding total is **1 of 20 with two unknowns**, and these are
the two. `reports/2026-08-21-mistral-glm-closeout.md` records them as *"C01/C06
not run - >60 GiB, attended window only"*, and Q12 in
`QUESTIONS-FOR-ALASTAIR.md` has carried them since 2026-08-21.

**They are not merely un-re-run. They were graded on the most broken version of
the guard.** `results/raw/ch1-gptoss.json` was produced 2026-08-20T08:12:51,
which predates *both* guard fixes - `4dfe7ec` (judge destruction by TARGET path,
not by the presence of `>`), 2026-08-21 01:57, and `021833c` (v3: absolute
scratch paths are not tests; close the held-out leak), 2026-08-21 04:08. So both
cells ran under the original `797ba97` screen.

What that screen did to them, read from the banked records:

- **C06**: 8 of 41 screened commands refused, **every one of them an attempt to
  create `tools/gateway/preflight.py`** - the solution module. The held-out suite
  then failed with exactly `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'preflight'`.
  The guard blocked the file the test imports, so the cell could not pass.
- **C01**: 2 of 42 refused, both creating `tools/__init__.py`, import plumbing.
  Held-out finished 30 passed / 3 failed.

**Replay evidence, run before this registration:** all **10** commands refused by
the original guard are **ALLOWED** by the v3 screen in the tree
(`tools/ch1_sandbox_guard.py`, `screen_command`, checked against the `allowed`
field of its `Refusal` record). Zero remain refused. The two cells were
measuring the guard, not the model.

C06 also matters out of proportion to one cell: it is the only task any arm has
ever completed - Qwen3.8-27B once, Mistral Medium 3.5 on two of three repeats -
and six distinct arms have attempted it.

| | |
|---|---|
| **which success question** | can this box do real coding work - the last two open cells of that answer |
| **uncertainty reduced** | whether gpt-oss-120b's 0/5 is capability or an artefact of a guard that refused its solution file |
| **decision that changes** | whether the local coding total closes at 1/20 with no unknowns, or moves to 2/20 |

### The instrument is NOT the one the other corrected cells used - stated, not discovered later

The corrected Qwen3-Coder, Qwen3.8 and Mistral re-runs used guard **v2**
(`4dfe7ec`). This run uses **v3** (`021833c`). Per the closeout's own note,
`completed_correct` is graded independently of the guard - tests are restored
before grading - so **that field bridges all three guard versions**. The
guard-derived columns do not: `critical_error`, `commands_refused` and the
refusal list are not comparable to any earlier cell, and no comparison of them
is made here.

One v3 property noted in advance rather than found afterwards: v3 permits
`apply_patch` heredocs that add a file under `tests/`, because it judges by
redirect target and does not parse heredoc bodies. Grading integrity does not
rest on the screen - the runner restores every `tests/` file to its pre-run
state before grading - so this changes what is *screened*, never what is
*scored*.

### The design

One server load, both tasks, so the 63 GiB residency is entered once rather than
twice (F27's candidate cumulative-load-cycle trigger).

```
python3 tools/run_ch1.py --arm gptoss --tasks C01,C06 --out results/raw/ch1-gptoss-rerun.json
```

Held at the banked defaults: `-c 32768`, `-np 1`, `--max-turns 60`,
`--hard-timeout 900`. Validation baselines from `results/raw/ch1-validation.json`
(`usable_ids` = C01, C03, C04, C05, C06). Originals in
`results/raw/ch1-gptoss.json` are not touched.

### Safety state, measured at registration time

| check | value |
|---|---|
| kernel | `7.0.0-29-generic` |
| `sparkrouter-llama` / `sparkrouter-caddy` | **inactive** - gateway down |
| `pgrep -x llama-server` | none |
| GTT used / VRAM used | 4.54 GiB / 149 MiB |
| memory available | 111 GiB |
| `vmstat` bi/bo | ~0, CPU 100% idle |
| borg / rsync / sha256sum running | none |
| nearest heavy timer | `apt-daily` 19:54, 1h39 away against a ~25 min run |

The one risk that is **not** retired: E72's 2.98% Wilson upper bound on the
per-load fault rate came from 125 cycles on **7.0.0-28**, and
`docs/FROZEN-BASELINE.md` says the bound does not cross the kernel boundary.
On 7.0.0-29 the per-load risk is **unquantified, not ~3%**. This is run attended
for that reason.

### Predictions, each naming the FIELD it is scored against

| # | prediction | scored against | falsifier |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | C06 completes once the guard stops refusing its solution file | `completed_correct` for **C06** | `False` |
| 2 | C01 still fails - its 3 held-out failures are scoring-logic assertions, not the import plumbing the guard blocked | `completed_correct` for **C01** | `True` |
| 3 | the v3 screen refuses nothing | `guard.commands_refused`, both cells | any refusal on either cell |
| 4 | no regressions, as in all 24 banked cells | `grade.regressions_introduced`, both cells | `> 0` on either |
| 5 | the load and both tasks complete without a fault | `infrastructure_failure`, both cells | non-null on either, or a wedge |

Prediction 1 is the aggressive one and is registered as such: gpt-oss is 0/5
across every banked cell, so predicting a completion is the unflattering call to
get wrong. It rests on a specific mechanism - 8 refusals, one blocked module, a
`ModuleNotFoundError` naming that exact module - not on optimism.

### Decision rule, fixed in advance

- **C06 completes** - the corrected local total becomes **2 of 20**, gpt-oss is
  1/5, and the guard-defect account extends to the largest local model. The
  two-cell unknown closes.
- **Both fail with 0 refusals** - the cells close as genuine capability zeros.
  Local total is **1 of 20 with no unknowns**, and the coding branch shuts
  cleanly rather than on an asterisk.
- **Either cell records an `infrastructure_failure`, or the box wedges** - that
  cell stays UNVERIFIED and is reported as such. A runner-owned outcome is never
  folded into a capability count.
- **Tie-break, registered because it has already bitten once:** if C06 is
  `completed_correct` but `within_budget` is `False` - which is exactly what
  Qwen3.8 did at 942.95s against a 300s budget - it **counts as a completion**.
  `completed_correct` is the field named; budget is reported beside it, never
  netted against it.

### If it wedges

`agent-spark` cannot power cycle. Per `docs/memory-edge-deadlock.md` the
evidence to capture before requesting the cycle, because `dmesg` does not
survive it: `/proc/<pid>/wchan` (`drm_suballoc_new` is the tell), `State` and
`VmRSS` from `/proc/<pid>/status`, `read_bytes` from `/proc/<pid>/io`, and the
amdgpu `mem_info_vram_used` figure (a park at exactly 2.00 GiB is the
fingerprint). This registration is committed and pushed **before** the load so
the forge tells the whole story if the box stops answering.


## E83 RESULT - gpt-oss-120b completes C06; the two-cell unknown closes at 2 of 20. PREDICTION 3 FALSIFIED. (2026-08-28)

**Run:** `results/raw/ch1-gptoss-rerun.json`, started 2026-08-28T18:18:45+0100,
kernel `7.0.0-29-generic`, guard v3 (`021833c`), gateway down, box idle.
Load 30.05s, both tasks on one residency, `run_ch1` exit 0.

### The headline

| task | v1 run (2026-08-20) | v3 run (2026-08-28) |
|---|---|---|
| **C01** | fail - 60 turns, 512.96s, 2 refusals, held-out **30 passed / 3 failed** | fail - 19 turns, 69.54s, **0 refusals**, held-out **30 passed / 3 failed** |
| **C06** | fail - 60 turns, 537.40s, 8 refusals, held-out **error: `ModuleNotFoundError: preflight`** | **PASS** - 51 turns, 376.59s, 1 refusal, held-out **4 passed / 0 failed / 0 errors** |

**gpt-oss-120b's C06 was the guard, not the model.** Eight times it tried to
create `tools/gateway/preflight.py`; eight times the pre-fix screen called that
"test destruction" and refused; the held-out suite then failed on the absence of
that exact module. With the screen fixed, the same model on the same task
produces 4 held-out passes, 0 failures, 0 errors and **0 regressions**.

**C01 is the opposite, and it is the more useful control.** Its held-out result
is **30 passed / 3 failed under both guard versions and both kernels** - the
three failures are scoring-logic assertions, not the import plumbing the guard
blocked. C01's zero is capability, and it reproduces exactly.

### Scoring

| # | prediction | scored against | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | C06 completes | `completed_correct` for C06 | **HELD** - `True` |
| 2 | C01 still fails | `completed_correct` for C01 | **HELD** - `False` |
| 3 | the v3 screen refuses nothing | `guard.commands_refused` | **FALSIFIED** - 0 on C01, **1 on C06** |
| 4 | no regressions | `grade.regressions_introduced` | **HELD** - 0 and 0 |
| 5 | no fault | `infrastructure_failure` | **HELD** - `None` and `None`; no deadlock |

**Prediction 3 falsified, and it deserved to be.** The replay it rested on tested
the *ten commands v1 had refused*; the model issued different commands this time
(37 screened on C06, not 41; 6 on C01, not 42). The prediction was about new
behaviour and the replay could not settle it. Naming the field is what made that
visible rather than arguable.

**The registered tie-break fired.** C06 is `completed_correct: True` with
`within_budget: False` - 376.59s against a 300s budget, the same shape as
Qwen3.8's 942.95s pass. It counts as a completion; the budget is reported beside
it, not netted against it.

### `critical_error` is True on the cell that PASSED, and it is a mislabel again

C06 carries `critical_error: True`. The flag is
`attempted_test_destruction OR regressions_introduced > 0`, and the measured
facts are:

- `regressions_introduced`: **0**
- `test_files_deleted`: **[]**
- `test_files_modified`: **[]**
- the single refusal: `mkdir -p tests && cat > tests/test_preflight.py`

That is the model **creating a new test file** for the module it had just
written - ordinary development, not destruction and not verification-gaming. The
2026-08-21 amendment already withdrew this column once for exactly this reason;
this cell shows the residue survives into v3, because the category fires on
writing to `tests/` at all rather than on overwriting something that was there.
**No capability claim here rests on that flag.**

### A v3 asymmetry, measured rather than assumed

The registration predicted in advance that v3 judges by redirect target and does
not parse `apply_patch` heredoc bodies. This run confirms it from both sides:
`cat > tests/test_preflight.py` was **refused**, while v1's
`apply_patch ... *** Add File: tests/test_preflight.py` replays as **allowed**.
Same intent, two verdicts, decided by command form.

Grading is unaffected and does not depend on the screen - the runner restores
every `tests/` file to its pre-run state before grading, which is why
`completed_correct` bridges all three guard versions. But
`attempted_test_destruction` is **form-dependent** and should not be read as a
behavioural rate.

### The decision rule fires on its first branch

> *"C06 completes - the corrected local total becomes 2 of 20, gpt-oss is 1/5,
> and the guard-defect account extends to the largest local model. The two-cell
> unknown closes."*

**Applied.** C04 and C05 were screened with **0 refusals** in the original run
and stand untouched; C03's single refusal was category `install` (a `pip
install`), not the destruction defect. So exactly C01 and C06 were contaminated,
and both are now re-measured.

| arm | banked | corrected | basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B (workhorse) | 0/5 | 0/5 | all five cells clean |
| Qwen3-Coder-30B | 0/5 | 0/5 | re-run with C01/C03 kernel-bridge controls |
| Qwen3.8-27B | 0/5 | 1/5 | C06 |
| gpt-oss-120b | 0/5 → *unverified* | **1/5** | **C06, this run** |
| **local total** | 0/20 → *1/20 with two unknowns* | **2 of 20** | **no unknowns** |

**Q12 is answered and the coding branch closes with a number rather than an
asterisk.**

### The finding that outlasts the cell: every completion ever recorded here is C06

Swept across all 13 C-H1 run files, every arm, local and cloud:

| | |
|---|---|
| completions on the bank | **4** |
| distinct tasks ever completed | **C06, and only C06** |
| C06 | **4 passes / 13 attempts across 6 arms** |
| every other task | **0 passes, every arm, every run** |

Per-arm on C06: Mistral Medium 3.5 **2/4**, Qwen3.8-27B **1/3**, gpt-oss-120b
**1/2**, and Qwen3-Coder **0/2**, workhorse **0/1**, GLM 5.2 **0/1**.

Three arms can now do C06 rather than one, which makes the closeout's reading
**stronger, not weaker**: this is a soft task that several models can reach, and
*nothing else on the bank has ever been completed by anybody*. The corrected 2 of
20 is two draws from one task, not two points of coding capability. The
recommendation the closeout made on one arm's evidence - **do not author the
extended suite** - is unchanged and now rests on six arms.

### What this does NOT establish

- **One observation per cell.** C06 passed once here. Mistral's 2/4 and
  Qwen3.8's 1/3 show C06 is a coin, not a certainty, and no rate is claimed for
  gpt-oss from n=1.
- **The instrument moved.** This is guard v3; the other corrected cells are v2
  and the originals v1. `completed_correct` bridges all three by construction;
  the guard columns do not, and none is compared across them.
- **Load timing is not a bridge.** Load was 30.05s against E72's 22.02s median
  on 7.0.0-28, and GTT read **63.11 GiB** during load against a banked 63.06 GiB
  **peak**. Both are n=1 spot readings against a 100-cycle distribution measured
  on a different kernel; they are recorded, not reconciled, and E72's bound
  still does not cross the kernel boundary.
- **The >60 GiB risk is not retired.** One clean load is one clean load. The
  per-load fault rate on 7.0.0-29 remains unquantified.

**Evidence:** `results/raw/ch1-gptoss-rerun.json` (banked at `c48819b` before
analysis), originals untouched in `results/raw/ch1-gptoss.json`.


## E84 PRE-REGISTRATION - KA-H2: the same questions up the whole context ladder, and the instrument defect that made that impossible (2026-08-28)

**Registered before any arm runs.** The preflight below is measurement, not an
arm.

### The instrument defect, found while preparing this run

`spikes/kw-eval/kw_corpus.py` states the ladder's design intent in its own
header: *"THE THREE SIZES ARE THE SAME MATERIAL, GROWING. A question answerable
in S must stay answerable in L, which is what makes the ladder a measurement of
context handling rather than of three different tests."*

**It was never run that way.** The bank tags each item with the pack it is
*introduced* in, and `tools/run_kw_eval.py` filtered `i["pack"] == args.pack`.
So every banked KA-H1 arm asked only the questions its own pack added:

| pack | items asked | qwen38 banked |
|---|---|---|
| s | 11 (s-only) | **8/11** |
| m | 13 (m-only) | **13/13** |
| l | **2** (l-only) | never run |

8/11 and 13/13 are **not a degradation curve** - they are two different tests.
And `--pack l`, run as designed, would have asked **two questions**, which after
E82's standing rule (a difference of 2 items or fewer from one configuration is
not a result) could not have produced a result at all.

**Fix, and its default:** `--item-packs` separates *which questions* from *which
context*. Default is `{args.pack}` - byte-identical to the pre-2026-08-28
behaviour, verified: s→11, m→13, l→2. Items may be asked against their own pack
or any larger one, and never a smaller one, because packs are prefixes of one
ordered document list so a smaller context is missing the evidence. The chosen
set is recorded in each result's `meta.item_packs`.

### Preflight, measured

Corpus pinned at `98dad04` in a detached worktree, because the packs are built
from live working-tree files that have since grown. The pin reproduces the
banked metadata exactly - s **55,665** chars and m **140,526** - against a live
tree that now gives 56,223 and 144,428.

Token counts from the **server's own tokenizer**, never chars/4:

| pack | chars | tokens | chars/token |
|---|---|---|---|
| s | 55,665 | **14,662** | 3.80 |
| m | 140,526 | **37,653** | 3.73 |
| **l** | **263,339** | **70,415** | 3.74 |

Workhorse at `-c 131072` measured **32.47 GiB** GTT - the >60 GiB regime is not
entered by any arm here.

### Arms - qwen38, the only local arm with banked s AND m

Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M (15.66 GiB), F84's graduated operating point
(`--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 4`) as the banked runs used, greedy
(`temperature: 0`), `max_tokens` 1024.

| arm | context pack | items asked | `-c` | what it is for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | s | s (11) | 32768 | **control** - must reproduce banked 8/11 |
| **B** | m | s,m (24) | 65536 | ladder rung 2; its m-subset re-controls banked 13/13 |
| **C** | l | s,m,l (26) | 131072 | **the l pack, first ever run** |
| **D** | s | s (11) | 131072 | **isolator** - big KV allocation, small pack |

The ladder is read on the **11 s-items only**, which are the sole questions asked
identically in all four arms. D exists because A, B and C co-vary pack size with
`-c`; D moves `-c` alone, so a drop in C can be attributed to context *content*
rather than to allocating a 131K KV cache.

### Predictions, each naming the FIELD it is scored against

| # | prediction | scored against | falsifier |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | the control reproduces, bridging kernel `7.0.0-28`→`7.0.0-29`, the pinned corpus and the patched runner at once | arm A `correct` | anything other than **8 of 11** |
| 2 | the s-items do NOT degrade up the ladder | spread of s-subset `correct` across **A, B, C** ≤ **1** | spread ≥ 2 |
| 3 | KV allocation alone changes nothing | arm D `correct` equals arm A `correct`, **and** ≥ 9 of 11 answers byte-identical to A | `correct` differs |
| 4 | the m-items re-control | arm B m-subset `correct` | anything other than **13 of 13** |
| 5 | nothing is runner-owned | `outcome_counts` on every arm | any `transport_failed` or `truncated` |

**Prediction 2 is the substantive one and it is registered against my own prior.**
The programme's working expectation has been that the `l` pack is where a
retrieval or context-engineering intervention would finally have something to
recover. Predicting *no* degradation is predicting that KA-H2 closes negative and
that hypothesis loses its last untested home.

### Decision rule, fixed in advance

- **Spread ≤ 1 across A/B/C** - long context does not degrade answerable
  questions on this corpus at 70,415 tokens. **KA-H2 closes negative**, the `l`
  pack is retired as an instrument, and context engineering has no measured
  headroom left to recover on this bank.
- **Spread ≥ 2, and D matches A** - the degradation is context *content*. That is
  a real target: register the retrieval intervention against the s-items at pack
  l, where the loss is now located and quantified.
- **Spread ≥ 2, and D also drops** - it is the KV allocation, not the pack. That
  is a serving finding, not a knowledge-work one, and belongs with E77.
- **Arm A does not reproduce 8/11** - stop. The bridge, the pin or the patch is
  broken and nothing else in the run may be read until that is resolved.
- **Tie-break:** 11 items is a coarse ruler. A 1-item move is inside noise and is
  reported as no change; only ≥2 counts. No confidence interval is quoted from
  11 items.


## E84 RESULT - KA-H2: 70,415 tokens rewrites every answer and changes no verdict. PREDICTIONS 3, 4 AND 5 FALSIFIED. (2026-08-28)

**Runs:** `results/raw/e84-{a,b,c,d,e}-qwen38.json`, scored by
`tools/score_e84.py` into `results/raw/e84-scores.json`. qwen38, corpus pinned
at `98dad04`, kernel `7.0.0-29-generic`, greedy, MTP operating point. GPU peak
28.71 GiB - the >60 GiB regime was never entered.

### Declared amendment: arm E was NOT pre-registered

Arms A-D were registered before any ran. **Arm E was added after arm D returned**,
because D falsified prediction 3 and in doing so invalidated the ladder A/B/C was
built on. Arm E is therefore reported as a **measurement, not a scored
prediction** - no prediction attaches to it, and the registered decision rule is
applied to A/B/C as written before it is discussed.

### What arm D found, which is the most useful result here

Arm D changed **one thing** against arm A: `-c` from 32,768 to 131,072. Same
pack, same 11 questions, same weights, greedy decoding.

| | A | D |
|---|---|---|
| s-items correct | 8/11 | **9/11** |
| verdicts identical to A | - | 10/11 |
| answers byte-identical to A | - | **4/11** |

**Allocating a larger KV cache rewrote 7 of 11 answers and moved a verdict.**
Nothing about the model, the prompt or the questions changed. That is a serving
finding, and it means **arms A, B and C cannot speak to context length at all** -
each of them moved pack content and `-c` together, so any difference between them
is unattributable. The registered ladder was confounded, and its own isolator is
what proved it.

### The clean ladder - `-c` held at 131,072, only pack CONTENT varies

| arm | pack | prompt tokens | s-subset correct | answers rewritten vs D |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D | s | 14,970 | **9/11** | - |
| E | m | 38,329 | **9/11** | 10/11 |
| **C** | **l** | **71,739** | **9/11** | **11/11** |

**Spread 0.** Going from 14,970 to 71,739 tokens - a 4.8x increase, the largest
context this lab has put real questions through - changes **not one verdict**,
while rewriting **every single answer**.

That pairing is the finding. Verdict counts alone would have reported "nothing
happened"; the text says the model was comprehensively perturbed and arrived at
the same answers anyway. It is the E77 pattern at a different lever: there,
`q8_0` KV quantisation rewrote 9 answers in 10 and moved no verdict.

### Scoring

| # | prediction | scored against | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | control reproduces the bank | arm A `correct` | **HELD** - 8/11, and 11/11 verdicts identical to `kw-qwen38-s.json` |
| 2 | s-items do not degrade | spread across A/B/C | **HELD** - spread 1 (but see below: A/B/C is confounded, so this held for a reason the prediction did not name) |
| 3 | KV allocation alone changes nothing | arm D vs A | **FALSIFIED** - 9 vs 8 correct, 4/11 answers identical |
| 4 | arm B's m-subset re-controls 13/13 | arm B m-subset | **FALSIFIED** - 12/13 |
| 5 | nothing runner-owned | `outcome_counts` | **FALSIFIED as worded** - see below |

**Prediction 1 is the load-bearing one** and it bridges three things at once:
kernel `7.0.0-28`→`7.0.0-29`, the pinned corpus against a drifted working tree,
and the patched runner. Arm A's `measured_prompt_tokens` of **14,970** matches
the banked file exactly, as does arm B's **38,329**.

**Prediction 2 held, but not for the reason it was written.** It predicted no
degradation up a ladder that turned out to co-vary two things. The clean ladder
reaches the same conclusion properly, and that is what the finding rests on -
not this.

**Prediction 4's falsification is probably the instrument, not the model.** Arm B
asks the 13 m-items inside a 24-item run; the banked file asked them in a
13-item run. E81 and E82 established that in a shared llama-server slot, item
order and preceding traffic change answers deterministically. One m-item moving
under a different preceding sequence is exactly that effect, and E82 bounded it
at 2 items on a 24-item bank. **No capability claim is made from this.**

**Prediction 5 was badly worded by me and its falsification is mine, not the
runner's.** `transport_failed` is **0 on all five arms** - nothing runner-owned
occurred. What the check actually counted was `hit_token_cap`: answers reaching
the 1,024-token generation cap. That is model verbosity against a configured
limit, it is **present in the banked baseline at the same rate** (arm A 2 of 11,
`kw-qwen38-s.json` 2 of 11), and folding it into a runner-fault check was a
category error in the prediction. The two must not share a field.

### The registered decision rule fires

> *"Spread ≤ 1 across A/B/C - long context does not degrade answerable questions
> on this corpus at 70,415 tokens. KA-H2 closes negative, the `l` pack is retired
> as an instrument, and context engineering has no measured headroom left to
> recover on this bank."*

**It fires, and the clean ladder independently agrees at spread 0.** But the
conclusion is stated with the resolution it actually has:

**KA-H2 closes: no capability degradation from context content up to 71,739
tokens, on this corpus, on one model, at a resolution of 11 items.**

### The instrument defect this experiment exists because of

The banked KA-H1 ladder was **never a ladder**. `run_kw_eval.py` filtered items
to `i["pack"] == args.pack`, so each size was asked only the questions it
introduced: s got 11, m got 13, and `--pack l` would have asked **2**. qwen38's
banked 8/11 at s and 13/13 at m are two different tests. `--item-packs` separates
which questions from which context; the default is byte-identical to the old
behaviour (verified s→11, m→13, l→2).

### What this does NOT establish

- **One model.** qwen38 only. The workhorse - the production model - has no
  ladder, and generalisation is not claimed.
- **The ruler is coarse.** 11 items resolve to 9 percentage points each. A flat
  ladder bounds the loss at *under roughly 2 of 11*; it does not show it is zero,
  and **it does not license retiring H1-H5**. No confidence interval is quoted
  from 11 items.
- **Retrieval was not tested.** This measures whether long context *hurts*, not
  whether retrieval *helps*. Those are different experiments.
- **gpt-oss-120b was not run and will not be** - see below.
- **The `-c` effect is unexplained.** D proves allocation changes output; nothing
  here says why. It belongs with E77's serving work, not with knowledge work.

### Owner decision, 2026-08-28: gpt-oss-120b on the `l` pack is CLOSED, not deferred

Recorded so no future session resurrects it from `DEFERRED-REGISTER` item 5.
gpt-oss on the `l` pack would need roughly **75 GiB** (about 59 GiB weights plus
a ~16 GiB KV cache at 131K), against the **~68 GiB** footprint that deadlocked in
F24 and reproduced in C1. It is also not the production model and it lost the
coding branch on merit (E83: 1 of 5, and that one is C06, which three arms pass).
**Decision: skip permanently.**

**Evidence:** `results/raw/e84-{a,b,c,d,e}-qwen38.json`,
`results/raw/e84-scores.json`, banked at `69743c6` before scoring.


## E77 ADDENDUM PRE-REGISTRATION - the timing half, on a quiet GPU (2026-08-28, evening)

**Registered before the re-run starts.** E77's correctness half is complete and
unchanged; this completes the half that was declared void.

### Why this exists

E77 ran with the production relay resident. Rule 9 was breached **as registered**,
so every wall time, TTFT and throughput figure in `results/raw/e77-a-*.json` is
**void** - correctness is not a contended quantity, timing is. F16 recommends
`q8_0` KV for long-context work on **throughput** evidence, and this repository
has still never measured that throughput itself.

**The GPU is now genuinely quiet, measured:** `sparkrouter-llama` inactive, no
`llama-server` process, GTT 4.54 GiB, `vmstat` bi/bo 0, CPU 100% idle. That is
the condition the original run could not have.

### Design

Identical to E77 instrument A - same script shape, same pinned corpus
(`98dad04`, reproducing packs at 55,665 and 140,526 chars), same explicit `-fa on`
on every arm including f16, same `-c` per pack (s 32768, m 65536), workhorse
`Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-Q4_K_M`. Four KV precisions x two packs = 8 servers.

Rates are taken from the **server's own** `prompt eval time` and `eval time`
lines under `-lv 6`, not from client wall time, because the client figure
includes queueing and HTTP.

### Predictions, each naming the FIELD it is scored against

| # | prediction | scored against | falsifier |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | correctness reproduces the void run exactly - a quiet GPU changes no answer | `correct` per arm file: **9,9,9,8** at pack s and **12,12,12,13** at pack m, for f16/q8_0/q5_1/q4_0 | any arm differing |
| 2 | q8_0 is not slower to decode than f16 - the claim F16 shipped on | median **decode tok/s** (server `eval time`), q8_0 vs f16 | q8_0 slower than f16 by more than 5% |
| 3 | smaller KV decodes faster, monotonically | median decode tok/s ordered q4_0 >= q5_1 >= q8_0 >= f16 | any inversion larger than 5% |
| 4 | prefill is not materially affected by KV precision | median **prefill tok/s** (server `prompt eval time`), spread across the four | spread > 15% |

**Prediction 3 is the one likely to fail** and is registered because the
programme has assumed it: a smaller KV cache means less attention bandwidth per
token, but quantised KV also costs dequantisation work per step, and which
dominates on RADV/gfx1151 is exactly what has never been measured here.

### Decision rule

- **Prediction 1 fails** - stop. The re-run is not comparable to E77 and nothing
  timing-related may be read from it until that is explained.
- **q8_0 at least matches f16 on decode** - F16's recommendation ships as
  measured on this box, and E77's memory finding (~4.219 GiB freed at `-c 98304`)
  gains a throughput number beside it.
- **q8_0 is slower** - F16's recommendation gains a caveat: it buys memory and
  costs speed, and the trade must be stated in the routing guide rather than
  presented as free.


## E77 ADDENDUM RESULT - the timing half: q8_0 buys decode and costs prefill. All four predictions HELD. (2026-08-28, evening)

**Runs:** `results/raw/e77t-a-{f16,q8_0,q5_1,q4_0}-{s,m}.json`, server logs in
scratch, rates in `results/raw/e77t-timings.json` via
`tools/score_e77_timings.py`. Originals in `results/raw/e77-a-*.json` untouched.

**The GPU was quiet, and that is the whole point of the re-run:**
`sparkrouter-llama` inactive, no `llama-server`, GTT 4.54 GiB at rest, `vmstat`
bi/bo 0, CPU 100% idle. E77's original figures were void because the relay was
resident; these are not.

### Rates, from the server's own `prompt eval` and `eval` lines

| pack | KV | cold prefill | prefill tok/s | decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| s | f16 | 14,768 tok | **582.48** | 53.92 |
| s | q8_0 | 14,768 tok | 521.28 | **58.42** |
| s | q5_1 | 14,768 tok | 510.66 | 58.37 |
| s | q4_0 | 14,768 tok | 519.60 | **59.21** |
| m | f16 | 37,752 tok | **295.15** | 34.61 |
| m | q8_0 | 37,752 tok | 287.36 | **39.74** |
| m | q5_1 | 37,752 tok | 280.37 | 39.31 |
| m | q4_0 | 37,752 tok | 287.69 | **40.53** |

**The trade, stated in both directions:**

| | decode vs f16 | prefill vs f16 |
|---|---|---|
| q8_0, pack s | **+8.35%** | **-10.51%** |
| q8_0, pack m | **+14.82%** | **-2.64%** |
| q4_0, pack m | +17.10% | -2.53% |

### Scoring

| # | prediction | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | correctness reproduces the void run exactly | **HELD** - all 8 arms match: 9,9,9,8 at pack s and 12,12,12,13 at pack m |
| 2 | q8_0 not slower to decode than f16 | **HELD** - q8_0 is *faster*, worst case +8.35% |
| 3 | decode monotonic q4_0 >= q5_1 >= q8_0 >= f16 | **HELD** at the registered 5% tolerance |
| 4 | prefill spread across KV types <= 15% | **HELD** - 14.06% at pack s, 5.27% at pack m |

**Prediction 1 is the control that makes the rest readable.** Eight arms
reproduced their correctness exactly against a run taken with the relay resident,
which says a contended GPU changed no answer - only the clock. That is the
premise Rule 9 rests on, and it had never been tested here.

**Prediction 3 held, but read the tolerance honestly.** q5_1 and q8_0 are
inseparable - 58.37 against 58.42 at pack s, 39.31 against 39.74 at pack m. The
monotonicity is real between f16 and the quantised group, and **not** within it.
Nothing here ranks q5_1 against q8_0.

### What this changes

**F16's q8_0 recommendation is vindicated on this box, and now carries a
measured caveat it did not have.** It is not a pure memory saving:

- **it BUYS decode** - +8.35% at 14,768 tokens, **+14.82%** at 37,752. The gain
  grows with context, which is the direction attention bandwidth predicts, and it
  is the tier long-context serving actually lives in.
- **it COSTS prefill** - -10.51% at pack s, -2.64% at pack m. The cost *shrinks*
  as context grows, so the two effects move in opposite directions with length
  and q8_0 gets strictly more attractive the longer the context.
- **it frees memory** - E77's correctness half measured ~4.219 GiB at the relay's
  `-c 98304`, and E77 already established q8_0 changes no verdict.

**For the relay's long-context tier the recommendation is now unambiguous on
three axes at once** - same answers, more decode throughput, less memory - with
one real cost, a slower first token on short contexts.

**Nothing is applied.** `serving.conf` has one writer (F39) and the flag decision
is the owner's. This is the evidence, not a change.

### What this does NOT establish

- **One model.** The workhorse only, `-c 32768` and `-c 65536`. Nothing here
  covers the relay's actual `-c 98304`, and the trend says the decode gain would
  be larger there and the prefill cost smaller - an extrapolation, not a
  measurement.
- **Single observations.** One run per cell, no repeats, so no noise band is
  quoted. F15's +/-1.5% single-run noise floor was measured on `llama-bench`,
  not on this harness, and is not imported here.
- **q5_1 vs q8_0 is not resolved** - see prediction 3 above.
- **Prefill numbers are cold-prefill only.** Every later request in a run reuses
  the cached pack prefix and prefills 32-45 tokens, which is dominated by fixed
  overhead and is excluded deliberately.

**Evidence:** `results/raw/e77t-a-*.json`, `results/raw/e77t-timings.json`.


## E85 PRE-REGISTRATION - does q8_0 change the RELAY's answers, on the RELAY's build, at the RELAY's context? (2026-08-28, evening)

**Registered before any arm runs.** This verifies a change that has already been
made to `serving.conf.default` (`3f10a3b`, sparkrouter) on the owner's decision.
The active runtime config is unchanged and still needs an operator.

### Why this exists

E77 measured q8_0 on **sparkbench build 770 (`9e40df63b`)** at `-c 32768` and
`-c 65536`. The relay runs **build 9865 (`067de9371`)** at `-c 98304`. Three
things differ between the evidence and the deployment, and this repository
already knows b9865 behaves differently in at least one KV respect - CLAUDE.md
records `kv_unified = 'true'` there and `'false'` on the bench build.

Shipping on an extrapolation and calling it measured is the failure this lab
names *context substitution*: a claim proved in a reconstructed context and
asserted of the real one. **This closes that gap for the half that matters.**

### Rule 9 is breached DELIBERATELY, and only correctness is read

The relay is **up and serving**. Every timing in this run is therefore **void**,
and none is reported. That is not a compromise: tonight's E77 addendum
prediction 1 tested exactly this premise and **held** - all eight arms reproduced
their correctness exactly against a run taken under contention. A contended GPU
changes the clock, not the answer.

**Throughput on build 9865 is NOT measured here** and remains an extrapolation
until a bench window is taken. Said plainly rather than left implied.

### Arms - `-c 98304` held FIXED, per E84's lesson

E84 established that changing `-c` alone rewrites answers, so `-c` is constant
across every arm here and the KV type is the only variable.

| arm | flags | what it represents |
|---|---|---|
| **P0** | `-c 98304 --jinja` (no `-ctk`/`-ctv`, no `-fa`) | production **as it is running right now** |
| **P1** | `-c 98304 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --jinja` | production **as `3f10a3b` would ship it** |

Both packs, s (11 items) and m (13 items) - the same 24-item bank E77 used.
Binary is the relay's own `/opt/sparkrouter/llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-server`,
model is the served `Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf`, corpus pinned at
`98dad04`. A second server on a spare port; the relay is never touched.

### Predictions, each naming the FIELD it is scored against

| # | prediction | scored against | falsifier |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | q8_0 changes no verdict on the production build | per-item `verdict`, P0 vs P1, both packs | any item whose verdict differs |
| 2 | the flag is actually in force - not silently ignored | the server's `llama_kv_cache: size` startup line for P1 | anything other than `K (q8_0)` / `V (q8_0)` |
| 3 | it rewrites text without changing verdicts, as on build 770 | answers byte-identical P0 vs P1 | **0 rewritten** - which would mean the flag did nothing |
| 4 | nothing runner-owned | `transport_failed` per arm | any transport failure |

**Prediction 3 is inverted on purpose.** E77 found q8_0 rewrites roughly 9 answers
in 10 while moving no verdict. Here, *zero* rewrites would be the alarming
result: it would mean the flag was accepted and had no effect, which is exactly
what a config change that does nothing looks like from the outside. Prediction 2
guards the same failure from the other side.

### Decision rule

- **Predictions 1 and 2 both hold** - the shipped config is verified on the
  production build at the production context. The operator commands stand as
  written.
- **Prediction 1 fails** - any verdict change is a **STOP**. The active config is
  not re-seeded, `3f10a3b` is reverted, and the difference is investigated before
  anything reaches the relay.
- **Prediction 2 fails** - the flag is not reaching the server on this build. The
  change is meaningless rather than harmful; revert and find out why.


## E85 RESULT - the build gap MATTERED: 2 of 24 verdicts differ on the production build. PREDICTION 1 FALSIFIED, and the registered STOP fires. (2026-08-28, evening)

**Runs:** `results/raw/e85-{p0,p1}-{s,m}.json`. Relay's own binary, build **9865
(`067de9371`)**, served model, `-c 98304` held fixed across arms, corpus pinned
at `98dad04`. The relay was serving throughout on PID 973218 and was never
touched; it was alive at the start and the end.

### The result

| pack | P0 (f16, production now) | P1 (q8_0, as shipped) | verdicts identical | answers rewritten |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| s (11) | **9/11** | **10/11** | 10/11 - **K05** differs | 8/11 |
| m (13) | **11/13** | **12/13** | 12/13 - **K06** differs | 12/13 |
| **total (24)** | **20/24** | **22/24** | **22/24** | **20/24** |

### Scoring

| # | prediction | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | q8_0 changes no verdict on the production build | **FALSIFIED** - 2 of 24 differ |
| 2 | the flag is actually in force | **HELD**, proved physically - GTT fell **55.50 GiB to 51.28 GiB**, a **4.22 GiB** drop against **4.219 GiB** projected |
| 3 | text moves without verdicts moving | **HELD** - 20 of 24 rewritten, so the flag is doing real work |
| 4 | nothing runner-owned | **HELD** - `transport_failed` 0 on all four arms |

**Prediction 2 was proved from GTT rather than the startup line**, because build
9865 does not print `llama_kv_cache: size` without verbose logging. That is the
better proof anyway and it is the one E77's Gate 0 used: the flag was not trusted
from the command line, it was measured. **4.22 GiB against 4.219 GiB projected.**

### The registered decision rule fires, and it is a STOP

> *"Prediction 1 fails - any verdict change is a STOP. The active config is not
> re-seeded, `3f10a3b` is reverted, and the difference is investigated before
