> anything reaches the relay."*

**Honoured. No re-seed commands were handed over as verified.** The rule fires
even though **both flips favour q8_0** - 9/11 to 10/11 and 11/13 to 12/13 - and
the direction is deliberately not allowed to rescue it. The claim q8_0 was
shipped on was *"changes no verdict"*, measured on a different build at a
different context. On the build and context that actually serve traffic, it
changes two. **The extrapolation was not safe, and that is the finding.**

### What is NOT claimable from this, in either direction

**2 of 24 is exactly the noise bound this lab already set.** E82's standing rule:
*a difference of 2 items or fewer, measured from a single configuration, is not a
result.* One observation per arm, no repeats. So:

- **"q8_0 is better" is NOT claimable** - +2 is inside the bound.
- **"q8_0 is verdict-identical" is NOT claimable either** - it demonstrably moved
  two, and E77's zero did not reproduce here.

The honest state is that the two are **indistinguishable at this instrument's
resolution on this build**, which is a strictly weaker statement than the one the
config was shipped on. `serving.conf.default` has been corrected to say exactly
that rather than repeat build 770's zero.

### What is measured, and what is still extrapolated

- **MEASURED on build 9865:** the memory saving (4.22 GiB at `-c 98304`), that
  the flag takes effect, and that correctness is within 2 of 24 either way.
- **STILL EXTRAPOLATED:** the **+8.35% / +14.82% decode figures**. E85 ran with
  the relay serving, so Rule 9 voids every timing in it. Those numbers are
  build-770 measurements and must not be quoted as measured on the relay.

### What is owed before the claim is safe

**A repeat.** Two arms, same configuration, to establish whether K05 and K06 flip
deterministically or are draws. That is the difference between "q8_0 changes two
answers on this build" and "this bank cannot resolve a difference this small",
and one run cannot separate them. It needs no bench window - correctness is not
contended - so it is cheap and it is the named next action.

**Evidence:** `results/raw/e85-{p0,p1}-{s,m}.json`; GTT trace in the session
scratchpad; sparkrouter `serving.conf.default` corrected at `3f10a3b`+1.



## E86 PRE-REGISTRATION - is E85's K05 flip POSITION-INDEPENDENT? And the literal repeat is abandoned as vacuous (2026-08-29)

**Registered before any arm runs.** The owner asked for "the E85 repeat". This
is not that run, and the reason is recorded here rather than discovered later.

### Why the repeat as specified would have measured NOTHING

E85 closed with: *"A repeat. Two arms, same configuration, to establish whether
K05 and K06 flip deterministically or are draws."*

**F59 forbids it, and F59 is ACTIVE and explicitly scoped to this case:**
*"llama-server generation at temperature 0 is BYTE-deterministic (10/10) ... at
temperature 0 with nothing varying, extra reps reproduce the same bytes and
measure nothing. Reps become informative only when something in the config
moves."* Status line: *"Applies to any llama-server arm at temperature 0."*

`tools/run_kw_eval.py` hardcodes `"temperature": 0`. F88 says the same thing from
the other side - a bit-deterministic arm *"reproduces its errors exactly as
faithfully as its successes"*, so a second identical run *"retires exactly one
hypothesis and no others"*, and the hypothesis it retires ("E85 got lucky") is
not the one E85 needed retired.

So an identical re-run was guaranteed to reproduce K05 and K06 and would have
been reported as "the flip is deterministic" - which F59 already tells us a
priori, and which does **not** distinguish a real q8_0 effect from an item this
bank cannot resolve. That is a **vacuous success**: a check whose preconditions
make its assertion meaningless. It is registered here as abandoned, not silently
replaced.

### What the two flipped items actually are - read before designing

**K05 is a real and meaningful difference.** It is a deliberate abstention item
(`"is_unanswerable": True`, category `ambiguity`): the pack gives no hang rate.
P0 (f16) answered *"1 in 1 ... the probability is 1 (100%)"*. P1 (q8_0) answered
*"the material does not provide a measured per-load probability ... cannot be
determined"*. That is the over-claim failure mode against the refusal-to-fabricate
property, not a coin flip between two near-equal answers.

**K06 is a DEFECTIVE ITEM and is withdrawn from the verdict count.** Its key is
`must_contain_any: ["Mistral","conditional"]` + `must_contain_all: ["3","13"]`.
P1 gave the Mistral/E45 correction and passed. P0 instead identified the
`--jinja` retraction - which is genuinely present in the pack at
`docs/HARNESS-RULES.md:165-169` ("`--jinja` turns out to default to ENABLED on
this build, so the flag was a no-op ... retracted 2026-07-17"), cited with its
control file. **Both answers are correct.** The question says *"advice that
explicitly corrects an earlier recommendation"* as though there is one; the six
m-pack documents carry 19 instances of correction language. K06 presupposes a
uniqueness the corpus does not have.

This is **F95's shape** - *"a deterministic grader can be reproducible and still
be systematically wrong, and reproducibility makes it MORE dangerous"*. Under
determinism K06 would have reproduced forever and been read as a stable finding.

**Consequence, registered now so it cannot be chosen after seeing results:** K06
is not counted as a capability difference in this experiment or in any future
statement about q8_0, and E85's headline becomes *at most* 1 of 24, pending this
run.

### The design - vary the ONE thing F59 permits to be informative

F59 says reps inform only when something in the config moves. E82 established
that in a shared llama-server slot, **item order and preceding traffic change
answers deterministically** - and bounded that effect at 2 items on a 24-item
bank, which is exactly the size of the E85 effect. So the live question is not
*"is it deterministic"* (it is) but *"is it bigger than the bank's own position
sensitivity"*.

K05 sits 5th of 11 in the s pack. `--items` selects ids and preserves corpus
order, so preceding traffic can be varied by removing items ahead of it.

| condition | invocation | K05's position | preceding traffic |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C1** | `--pack s` (all 11) | 5th | K01-K04 |
| **C2** | `--items K05` | 1st | none |
| **C3** | `--items K01,K02,K05` | 3rd | K01, K02 |

Both arms run all three. **`-c 98304` is held fixed across every arm and
condition** (E84's lesson), so KV type and position are the only variables, and
they are varied one at a time.

**Arms.** Relay binary `/opt/sparkrouter/llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-server`,
build 9865, served model `Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf`, second
server on port 8139. The relay is never touched.

| arm | flags |
|---|---|
| **P0** | `-c 98304 --jinja` |
| **P1** | `-c 98304 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --jinja` |

**Corpus pinned at `98dad04` in a worktree, and the pin is LOAD-BEARING.** The
s pack at HEAD is **56,223 chars**; at the pin it is **55,665**, matching E85's
recorded `pack_chars` exactly. Two of the four s-pack documents have changed
since. Running at HEAD would have moved the corpus and the position together -
F59's own scar, where a rewritten input was attributed to the only variable
anyone had noticed.

### Rule 9 breached deliberately, and only correctness is read

The relay is up and serving on PID 973218. **Every timing here is void and none
is reported.** E77's addendum tested exactly this premise and it held: a
contended GPU changes the clock, not the answer.

### Predictions, each naming the FIELD it is scored against

| # | prediction | scored against | falsifier |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | C1 reproduces E85 byte-for-byte, both arms | `answer` text of all 11 items vs `results/raw/e85-{p0,p1}-s.json` | any byte difference |
| 2 | K05's P0-vs-P1 difference survives in **all three** conditions | K05 `outcome` per arm per condition | any condition where P0 and P1 agree on K05 |
| 3 | P0 fails specifically by OVER-CLAIMING a figure, not by erroring | P0's K05 `answer` text in each condition | P0 declines, or fails some other way |
| 4 | nothing runner-owned | `error` / transport per run | any transport failure |

**Prediction 1 is the load-bearing control.** It bridges the corpus pin, the
worktree, a fresh process and F59's determinism claim at once. If it fails,
nothing else in this run is interpretable and the run is void.

### Decision rule, fixed now

- **Prediction 2 HOLDS 3/3** - the K05 difference is position-independent and
  attributable to the KV type. E85 resolves to **one robust difference plus one
  defective item**, and that one difference runs in the SAFE direction: q8_0
  declines where f16 fabricates. The STOP may be reconsidered by the owner. It
  is not lifted by this run.
- **Prediction 2 FAILS in any condition** - K05 is position-sensitive, sits
  inside E82's <=2 order-noise bound, and **no verdict difference is
  attributable to q8_0**. The correctness objection to q8_0 dissolves, and the
  remaining case rests on the 4.22 GiB saving.
- **Either way**, K06 is repaired or retired as an instrument defect, separately
  and on its own evidence.

**This run does not re-seed anything.** Re-seeding the live relay stays the
owner's decision and needs the throughput measurement, which needs a bench
window.

**Amendments:** none.

### AMENDMENT 1 (declared before the affected re-run, 2026-08-29)

**The registration named a pinned corpus; the METHOD I used did not implement
it.** First run is VOID and prediction 1 correctly caught it.

`tools/run_kw_eval.py:41` does
`sys.path.insert(0, Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "spikes" / "kw-eval")`.
Position 0 precedes `PYTHONPATH`, so HEAD's runner always resolves HEAD's corpus
no matter what the environment says. The run built the **HEAD** s pack at
**56,223 chars** instead of the pinned **55,665**, and only 2 of 11 answers
matched E85.

**The pre-run check that "verified" the pin was itself invalid, and this is the
transferable part.** It ran `PYTHONPATH=... python3 -` with a bare
`import kw_corpus` - a script with no `sys.path.insert` of its own. That path
resolved the pin correctly and proved nothing, because **the experiment never
takes it**. `development-discipline.md` says to suspect the ruler before the
data; here the ruler was measured on a different instrument than the one under
test. A corpus pin must be verified through *the same entry point the run uses*.

**Fix:** HEAD's `run_kw_eval.py` is copied INTO the worktree and executed from
there, so `Path(__file__).parent.parent` resolves inside the pin. Verified
through that entry point: **55,665**, matching E85's recorded `pack_chars`.
This is evidently what E85 itself did - its meta carries `item_packs`, a HEAD-only
field, alongside the pinned char count.

**`spikes/kw-eval/kw_items.py` has 0 commits since `98dad04`**, so questions,
keys and `is_unanswerable` flags are byte-identical between pin and HEAD, and
scoring the runs with HEAD's `score_kw_eval` is like-for-like.

**The void run is RETAINED** as `results/raw/e86-void-headcorpus-{p0,p1}-{c1,c2,c3}.json`
rather than deleted. Its two arms are internally like-for-like against each other
at the HEAD corpus, so it may later serve as an incidental second-corpus
replication. **No claim is made from it here.**

**Predictions and the decision rule are UNCHANGED.**



## E86 RESULT - all four predictions HELD, and the finding that matters came from the VOID run: K05's difference does not survive a 1% corpus change (2026-08-29)

**Runs:** `results/raw/e86-{p0,p1}-{c1,c2,c3}.json`, corpus pinned at `98dad04`
(all six at `pack_chars` **55,665**, `measured_prompt_tokens` **14,717**,
`ctx` **98,304** - matching E85's meta exactly). Relay binary, build 9865, served
model. Relay alive on PID 973218 before and after every arm; only captured PIDs
were killed. Rule 9 breached deliberately; **no timing is reported.**

### Scoring

| # | prediction | scored against | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | c1 reproduces E85 byte-for-byte | `answer` text, 11 items, both arms | **HELD - 11/11 and 11/11** |
| 2 | K05 difference survives all 3 positions | K05 `verdict` per arm per condition | **HELD 3/3** |
| 3 | P0 fails by OVER-CLAIMING | `critical_error` | **HELD - True in all 3** |
| 4 | nothing runner-owned | transport class | **HELD - 0 of 6 runs** |

**Prediction 1 is the strongest control this bank has produced.** 22 of 22
answers byte-identical to a run made the previous evening, in a different
process, after a kernel-unchanged reboot-free interval, through a rebuilt
worktree. It confirms the corpus pin, F59's determinism and the harness at once.

### The registered result

| condition | K05 position | P0 (f16) | P1 (q8_0) |
|---|---|---|---|
| c1 | 5th of 11 | wrong, `critical_error` | correct |
| c2 | 1st, alone | wrong, `critical_error` | correct |
| c3 | 3rd of 3 | wrong, `critical_error` | correct |

**Position-independent, 3/3.** f16 fabricates a hang rate; q8_0 declines. The
registered rule fires: *"the K05 difference is position-independent and
attributable to the KV type."*

### AND THE RULE IS NOT THE WHOLE ANSWER - the incidental second corpus

Amendment 1 retained the void run and registered that its two arms are
internally like-for-like at the **HEAD** corpus. Read now, it says something the
pre-registered design could not:

| corpus | pack | P0 K05 | P1 K05 | difference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pinned `98dad04` | 55,665 chars / 14,717 tok | **wrong** x3 | correct x3 | **YES, 3/3** |
| HEAD | 56,223 chars / 14,890 tok | **correct** x3 | correct x3 | **NONE, 0/3** |

**A 558-character change to a 55,665-character pack - 1.0%, in two documents
edited on 2026-08-20 for unrelated reasons - removes the difference entirely.**
f16 stops fabricating. `critical_error` goes False. The arms agree.

**This is NOT pre-registered and is stated as the weaker claim it is:** one item,
two corpus states, n=1 per cell. What it rules out is a generalisation, which is
the safe direction. It cannot show the difference is *never* real.

### What E85's objection now amounts to

E85 stopped the q8_0 re-seed on *"2 of 24 verdicts differ"*. That resolves to:

1. **K06 - withdrawn.** A defective item. Both arms answered correctly; the key
   accepts only one of two genuine corrections present in the pack.
2. **K05 - real, position-independent, and knife-edge.** It reproduces perfectly
   at one corpus state and is absent at another 1% away.

**So the correctness objection to q8_0 does not generalise.** It was never a
claim about q8_0 changing answers in production; it is a claim about one
abstention item at one corpus state, where f16 happens to sit on the wrong side
of a boundary that q8_0 happens to sit on the right side of. Both flips E85 saw
favoured q8_0, and the one that survives scrutiny still does - q8_0 declined
where f16 invented a statistic.

**The STOP is not lifted here.** Two things still stand between this and a
re-seed, and neither is a correctness question:

- **Throughput on build 9865 is still unmeasured.** The +8.35% / +14.82% figures
  are build-770 numbers. Rule 9 voids every timing in E85 and E86 alike.
- **Re-seeding the live relay is the owner's decision**, and the active line must
  carry `-c 98304`, not the old default's `49152`.

### The transferable lesson, and it is about the ruler

The pre-registered perturbation - item position - was the *weaker* test. It held
3/3 and would have been reported as "the difference is real". The perturbation
that actually bounded the finding was one I introduced **by accident**, kept only
because the amendment retained a void run instead of deleting it.

**A corpus is a variable in every run that uses it** (F59 recorded exactly this
after a matter file was edited between runs). E86 adds the sharper version: on a
knife-edge item, a 1% corpus change is a **larger** perturbation than moving the
item from first to fifth in the conversation. When bounding a small difference,
vary the INPUT before varying the ORDER.

**Amendments:** 1 (declared before the affected re-run).



## E87 PRE-REGISTRATION - q8_0 THROUGHPUT on the relay's own build, in a real bench window, with flash attention separated out (2026-08-29)

**Registered before any arm runs.** This closes the last technical gap in front
of the q8_0 re-seed. E86 settled correctness; the outstanding claim is the
**+8.35% / +14.82% decode gain**, which is a **build-770** measurement at
`-c 32768` / `-c 65536`. Rule 9 voided every timing in E85 and E86 because the
relay was serving. **This run takes the window**, so timings are valid.

### The confound E77 could not separate, and this run can

Quantising V **forces flash attention on**. So E77's "q8_0 vs f16" compares
`q8_0 + fa` against `f16 + no fa` - two changes at once. If most of the decode
gain is flash attention, `-fa on` is available **without** touching KV, at no
correctness risk at all. A third arm settles it.

| arm | flags (`-c 98304` fixed on all three) | isolates |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | `-c 98304 --jinja` | production **exactly as it runs now** |
| **B** | `-c 98304 -fa on --jinja` | **flash attention alone**, f16 KV |
| **C** | `-c 98304 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --jinja` | the shipped change |

B minus A = flash attention. C minus B = KV quantisation. C minus A = what the
re-seed actually buys.

**Binary** `/opt/sparkrouter/llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-server` (build 9865),
**model** the served `Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf`, **corpus pinned
at `98dad04`** and verified through the run entry point (s=55,665, m=140,526) -
amendment 1 of E86 applies, the runner is executed from inside the worktree
because `PYTHONPATH` cannot pin it.

**Packs s and m, 3 repetitions each.** F15 puts single-run noise at +/-1.5%, and
a single run cannot distinguish an 8% gain from a warm cache. **Median of 3 is
the reported figure**; the spread is reported with it.

### The window is REAL and the relay goes down

Run via `sudo bash tools/relay_bench_window.sh kvquant`, which sets sparkrouter's
advisory maintenance flag, stops `llama-gateway.service`, runs the bench
unprivileged as `agent-spark`, and **restores the relay on ANY exit** through an
EXIT/INT/TERM trap. The gateway reports 503 maintenance with a reason rather
than looking like an unexplained outage.

### Predictions, each naming the FIELD it is scored against

| # | prediction | scored against | falsifier |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | the TIMED configs are the ones E85/E86 characterised | arm A s-pack `answer` text vs `e85-p0-s.json`; arm C vs `e85-p1-s.json` | any byte difference |
| 2 | q8_0 decodes faster than production f16 | median decode tok/s, C vs A, both packs | C <= A on either pack |
| 3 | E77's figures do NOT reproduce on this build/context | C-vs-A decode delta vs +8.35% (s) / +14.82% (m) | **both** deltas land within F15's +/-1.5% of E77 |
| 4 | flash attention alone buys decode | median decode tok/s, B vs A | B <= A |
| 5 | q8_0 COSTS prefill, as on build 770 | median prefill tok/s, C vs A | C faster than A on prefill |
| 6 | nothing runner-owned | transport failures across all 18 runs | any transport failure |

**Prediction 1 is the control.** A timing run on a config whose correctness was
never characterised measures a different thing than the one under discussion.
Arm B has no correctness baseline and makes no correctness claim.

**Prediction 3 is deliberately a prediction of NON-reproduction.** Build and
context both differ from E77. Registering "it will reproduce" would be the
extrapolation E85 already caught once.

### Decision rule, fixed now

- **P2 holds and the gain exceeds noise** - the technical case is complete:
  correctness settled by E86, memory measured at 4.22 GiB, throughput measured
  here. **The re-seed becomes the owner's decision and nothing else blocks it.**
- **P2 fails (C <= A)** - the shipped change buys **memory only**. The re-seed
  then rests on 4.22 GiB alone and must be argued on that, not on speed.
- **P4 holds and B captures most of C's gain** - report `-fa on` as a **separate,
  cheaper option**: the same decode benefit with f16 KV, no KV quantisation, and
  no exposure to the knife-edge K05 behaviour E86 found.

**This run does not re-seed anything.** Re-seeding remains the owner's call.

**Amendments:** none.



## E87 RESULT - the shipped gain is REAL and it is ALL KV quantisation; flash attention buys nothing; and within-process reps are not independent (2026-08-29)

**Runs:** `results/raw/e87-{A,B,C}-{s,m}-r{1,2,3}.json`, 18 runs, all rc=0.
Relay binary build 9865, served model, `-c 98304` fixed, corpus pinned at
`98dad04`. **Taken in a real maintenance window** (`relay_bench_window.sh
kvquant`) - gateway stopped, advisory flag set, GPU quiet. **Rule 9 does not
apply: these timings are VALID.** Relay restored by the script's trap; window
closed.

### Decode, tok/s (per item, `completion_tokens / (wall_s - ttft_s)`, 3 reps pooled)

| arm | config | pack s | pack m |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | f16, production as it runs now | 55.04 | 35.16 |
| **B** | f16 + `-fa on` | 54.97 | 35.17 |
| **C** | q8_0 + `-fa on` (shipped) | **59.38** | **40.83** |

### Which change buys it - the question E77 could not ask

| pack | B vs A (flash attention) | C vs B (KV quantisation) | C vs A (shipped) |
|---|---|---|---|
| s | **-0.14%** | **+8.02%** | **+7.87%** |
| m | **+0.04%** | **+16.08%** | **+16.13%** |

**Flash attention alone buys NOTHING.** Prediction 4 is FALSIFIED and the answer
is unambiguous: A and B are within 0.14% on both packs. **The entire gain is the
smaller KV cache**, which is a memory-bandwidth effect, not an attention-kernel
one. The cheaper option I registered a decision branch for **does not exist** -
`-fa on` with f16 KV gets you nothing, so the speed cannot be had without
quantising KV.

**The delta is stable across reps to under 1pp** (s: +7.50/+8.14/+7.36;
m: +16.28/+16.05/+15.96), and rep-1-only - the cold runs that reproduce E85
exactly - gives +7.50% / +16.28%. The answer-text divergence in reps 2-3
(below) did **not** contaminate the timing.

### Prefill, cold (rep 1 item 1 only, n=1, declared)

| pack | A | C | delta | E77 on build 770 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| s | 584.2 tok/s | 517.1 | **-11.48%** | -10.51% |
| m | 366.2 tok/s | 363.8 | **-0.66%** | -2.64% |

**The trade is confirmed on the production build: q8_0 buys decode and costs
prefill.**

### Scoring

| # | prediction | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | timed configs are the characterised ones | **FALSIFIED as worded** - rep1 reproduces 11/11 both arms, reps 2-3 do not (4/11, 2/11) |
| 2 | q8_0 decodes faster than production f16 | **HELD** - +7.87% / +16.13%, far outside +/-1.5% noise |
| 3 | E77's build-770 figures do NOT reproduce | **FALSIFIED** - both landed within F15's +/-1.5pp (0.48pp, 1.31pp) |
| 4 | flash attention alone buys decode | **FALSIFIED** - -0.14% / +0.04% |
| 5 | q8_0 costs prefill | **HELD** - -11.48% / -0.66% |
| 6 | nothing runner-owned | **HELD** - 0 transport failures in 18 runs |

### Prediction 3's falsification is the nuanced one, and it cuts against E85

I predicted E77's figures would not reproduce, because build AND context both
differ. **They reproduced within noise on both packs.**

So the *same* build-770 extrapolation was **unsafe for correctness** (E85:
0 of 24 became 2 of 24) and **safe for throughput** (E87: reproduced inside
+/-1.5pp). **Extrapolation safety is a property of the AXIS, not of the
config.** E85's lesson was never "build 770 numbers are worthless" - it was
"you cannot know which axis travels without measuring". Both halves of that are
now evidenced.

### Prediction 1's falsification is a NEW finding - see F96

Rep 1 reproduces E85 byte-for-byte on both arms. Reps 2 and 3 do not, in the
same process, at the same config, at temperature 0.

**Byte-determinism holds across PROCESSES (F88) and for a COLD first run. It does
NOT hold for repeated runs inside one server process.** The intervening traffic -
the other pack, the previous rep - leaves cache state that changes later answers.
This is E82's order effect operating *across runs* rather than within one.

**Consequence for method:** reps inside one process are **not** independent
replicates for correctness. They remain valid for throughput, which is what this
experiment needed them for and why its conclusion survives. Recorded as **F96**.

The control's PURPOSE - proving the timed configs are the ones E85/E86
characterised - **is met by rep 1**, at 11/11 on both arms. The prediction is
still scored FALSIFIED as written rather than reinterpreted after the fact.

### The registered decision rule fires

> *"P2 holds and the gain exceeds noise - the technical case is complete:
> correctness settled by E86, memory measured at 4.22 GiB, throughput measured
> here. The re-seed becomes the owner's decision and nothing else blocks it."*

**It fires.** The q8_0 case is now measured on all three axes, on the build and
context that serve traffic:

| axis | figure | where measured |
|---|---|---|
| correctness | 1 knife-edge item of 24, direction favouring q8_0 | E86, build 9865 |
| memory | **4.22 GiB freed** at `-c 98304` | E85, measured via GTT |
| decode | **+7.9%** (14.7k ctx) / **+16.1%** (37.8k ctx) | E87, valid window |
| prefill | **-11.5%** / **-0.7%** | E87, valid window |

**Nothing technical blocks the re-seed. It is the owner's decision.** The active
line must carry `-c 98304`, not the old default's `49152`.

**Amendments:** none.


## E101 PRE-REGISTRATION - does `min-p` fix looping, or is looping just the reasoning-effort default? (2026-09-04)

**Registered before any arm runs.** At the moment of writing the GPU is free
(`pgrep -x llama-server` empty, relay window OPEN since 13:58:14), no result
file for this experiment exists, and no sampled generation from this model has
been read in this session. Committed before the first run so the order is
provable from git.

### Why this experiment exists

| | |
|---|---|
| **which success question** | local coding reliability - parked-trigger 1 territory |
| **uncertainty reduced** | whether a sampler setting we have never measured (`min-p`) is a real lever on non-termination, or whether the effect is dominated by `reasoning_effort`, which F71 already measured |
| **decision that changes** | whether production serving gains sampler flags at all. Today it sets none |

### Provenance of the hypothesis

A community report on an RTX 3090 Ti / Windows box describes Qwen3.8-27B quants
looping on long agentic work and proposes `--min-p 0.05` as a candidate fix,
alongside `-temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --presence-penalty 0.0
--repeat-penalty 1.0`. **That is a hypothesis from a different box, a different
OS and a different workload**, and it is tested here as such. Their hardware
constraint (24 GB VRAM) does not apply to this box and none of their quant
selection reasoning transfers.

### The instrument, and the defect that had to be fixed before it could run

`tools/run_coding_eval.py`, task-set `core`, six tasks: `normalize_path` and
`roman_roundtrip` (the two F71 named as RUNAWAY - one produced no code after
51,845 tokens at `xhigh` and working code in 1,469 at `medium`; the other
consumed a full 100,000-token budget without converging), plus
`longest_valid_parens`, `word_break`, `min_window`, `eval_expr` as hard controls
that F71 did not name.

**Both eval harnesses in this repo hardcode `temperature: 0`.** `min_p`, `top_k`
and `top_p` are truncation filters over a sampled distribution; greedy decoding
takes the argmax and never samples, so at temperature 0 they are INERT. Running
the reported config through the unmodified harness would have measured nothing
and produced a clean null. `run_coding_eval.py` gained an opt-in sampler payload
at `d3d02df` and now REFUSES a truncation filter at temperature 0 rather than
report a no-op. Every default is `None` and `None` sends nothing, so the arms
banked before today are unaffected - guarded by
`tests/test_coding_eval_sampler.py`.

`repetition_stats()` records `max_line_run` (longest run of identical adjacent
lines) and `max_ngram_rep` (most occurrences of any 8-word window) per item.
Two measures because a loop takes two shapes and either alone reads clean when
the other is firing. **Counts only. No threshold for "looping" is baked into
the meter; the thresholds are the predictions below.**

### THE POSITIVE CONTROL, RUN BEFORE ANY ARM (F100, F128)

A flag can load without acting, and `min_p` reaching llama-server's OpenAI
endpoint is an ASSUMPTION until exercised. Before any arm runs, on the same
served model:

| check | passes iff |
|---|---|
| **C1 seed determinism** | two requests, `temperature 1.0`, SAME seed -> byte-identical content |
| **C2 seed sensitivity** | two requests, `temperature 1.0`, DIFFERENT seeds -> content differs |
| **C3 min_p acts** | `temperature 1.0, min_p 0.9` vs `min_p 0.0` at the same seed -> content differs |

**If C1-C3 do not all pass, E101 does not run and the failure is the finding.**
C3 is the one that matters: C1 and C2 can both pass while `min_p` is silently
dropped from the payload.

### The five cells

`reasoning_effort` is crossed with the sampler because F71 measured a large
effort effect on these exact tasks and an uncrossed sampler arm would
attribute it to `min-p`.

| cell | effort | sampler | seeds |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 GREEDY** | `medium` | none (historical payload) | 1 - F88/F96: bit-deterministic, a second rep is not a replicate |
| **2** | `medium` | temp 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, **min-p 0.0** | 3 |
| **3** | `medium` | as cell 2 but **min-p 0.05** | 3 |
| **4 THEIR CONFIG** | `default` (= `xhigh`) | temp 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, **min-p 0.0** | 3 |
| **5 THEIR FIX** | `default` (= `xhigh`) | as cell 4 but **min-p 0.05** | 3 |

`-c 16384`, `--max-tokens 8192`, quiet GPU (Rule 9 SATISFIED - the relay
window is open, unlike E78 whose timings were VOID). Seeds are distinct per
replicate and recorded: at temperature > 0 two runs on one seed are one
measurement, not two.

⚠️ **AMENDMENT 1, declared 2026-09-04 14:26, after cell 1 and BEFORE cells 2-13
finished.** The line above originally read `-c 16384`, `--max-tokens 8192`,
**`-fa on`**. That was wrong when written: `-fa` is NOT a default in
`run_coding_eval.py` - it only reaches the server through `--server-extra`,
which this experiment does not pass. **Every E101 cell therefore runs WITHOUT
flash attention**, verified from the live process command line
(`llama-server -m ... -c 16384 -np 1 --host ... --no-webui -v`, no `-fa`) and
from cell 1's own log.

The registered config is corrected rather than the runs being redone, for two
stated reasons. **Internal validity is untouched**: every cell runs the same
way, and all six predictions compare cells against each other, so the
flash-attention setting cancels. And F87 measured flash attention buying
**nothing** on this box, so a re-run would cost 15 minutes per cell to change a
number F87 says will not move. What is NOT claimed: that this was intended. It
was a defect in the registration, caught by reading the process table rather
than trusting the text, and it is recorded because a config a result cannot be
re-derived from is a config that gets argued about later.

18 generations per sampled cell, 6 for the greedy cell, **78 total**.

### Predictions, each naming the FIELD it is scored against

| # | prediction | scored against |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | their config runs away often enough to measure | cell 4 records with `outcome == "truncated"`, **>= 6 of 18** |
| 2 | **DISCRIMINATING: min-p reduces non-termination at their effort setting** | cell 5 `truncated` minus cell 4 `truncated`, **<= -3** |
| 3 | **THE HEADLINE: reasoning effort dominates the sampler** | cell 2 `truncated` minus cell 4 `truncated` is **more negative than** cell 5 minus cell 4. I.e. dropping `xhigh` to `medium` buys more than adding `min-p` does |
| 4 | F71 reproduces on the greedy control | in cell 1, `normalize_path` and `roman_roundtrip` both have `outcome == "pass"` |
| 5 | the repetition meter tracks the failure it was built for | mean `repetition.max_ngram_rep` over `truncated` records **>= 3x** the mean over `pass` records, pooled across cells 2-5 |
| 6 | the harness holds | `transport_failed` and `no_code` both **0** across all 78 |

Prediction 3 is the one worth running this for. If it holds, the reported fix is
real but second-order, and the actionable line stays F71's - **serve this model
at `reasoning_effort: medium` explicitly** - with `min-p` as an optional extra
rather than the answer.

### Registered decision rule

| observed | action |
|---|---|
| P2 holds and P3 holds | min-p is a real but secondary lever. Recommend it only alongside `medium`, and say so in the same sentence |
| P2 holds and P3 FAILS | min-p is the dominant lever and F71's advice is incomplete. Re-open the serving-flag question with sparkrouter as a PROPOSAL (F39: `serving.conf` has one writer and it is not this repo) |
| P2 fails (min-p buys < 3) | the reported fix does not transfer to this box. Report it as not-reproduced, naming the hardware and OS difference, and do NOT generalise to their box |
| P1 fails (cell 4 truncates < 6 of 18) | **the looping they describe does not reproduce here at all.** No claim may be made about min-p in either direction; the finding is about non-reproduction and the arms are underpowered by construction |
| C1-C3 fail | E101 does not run |

### What this cannot establish

- **Six tasks, three seeds.** A 3-of-18 shift is inside what n=18 can carry
  loosely; any interval is quoted with the number.
- **One model, one quant.** Nothing here transfers to their ThinkingCap or
  GSQ-RCO builds, which is what E102 and E103 are for.
- **Nothing about their box.** Different GPU, different OS, different llama.cpp
  build. A non-reproduction here does not make their report wrong.


## E102 PRE-REGISTRATION - does the GSQ-RCO IQ3_S quant hold Q4_K_M quality on the same model? (2026-09-04)

**Registered before either arm runs.** No L5 result file for either arm exists
at the time of writing.

### Why this experiment exists

| | |
|---|---|
| **which success question** | production serving - a 4.7 GiB saving on the `smart` slot would change what fits resident |
| **uncertainty reduced** | whether a ~3-bit quant of our incumbent is measurably worse at knowledge work |
| **decision that changes** | whether the asymmetric three-model config (F135/F138) can hold a larger context, or a fourth model, in the same envelope |

### The pair, and why it is clean

| | incumbent | challenger |
|---|---|---|
| file | `Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf` | `Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S-mtp.gguf` |
| bytes | 16,810,714,336 | 12,120,016,960 |
| arch | `qwen35` | `qwen35` |
| trained ctx | 262,144 | 262,144 |
| sha256 vs pinned oid | - | MATCHES (`58fd8267...`) |

Same architecture, same trained context, same base model. **The pair differs by
the quantisation recipe and nothing else**, which is what makes a difference
attributable. Probed with `tools/gguf_ctx_probe.py` before registration, per
F124 - model metadata can falsify an arm before it is run.

### The instrument, and its known saturation

`tools/run_ps_eval.py --tier l5`, 24 items, 12 per band, gated by
`tools/validate_ps_eval_l5.py`. Config matched to E78's registered arm: `-c
16384`, `-fa on` (passed EXPLICITLY via `--server-extra`, which is the only way
it reaches the server - see E101 Amendment 1, where assuming it was a default
was a real defect), `--thinking low`. **Both arms run fresh in this session on a
QUIET GPU** rather than comparing against E78's banked numbers - E78 breached
Rule 9 and its wall times are VOID, so its timings cannot be a comparator.

**The incumbent scores 23/24 on this bank (band R 11/12, band E 12/12, E78).
That is near the ceiling, and it is the central limitation of this design.**
The bank can detect the challenger falling and cannot detect it rising. That is
acceptable for the question actually asked - *does the small quant degrade?* -
and it is stated here so no one later reads a tie as evidence of equivalence.

### Predictions, each naming the FIELD it is scored against

| # | prediction | scored against |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the incumbent reproduces its own banked score | incumbent `total correct` **>= 21 of 24** (E78 got 23; this allows the two-item order effect E82 measured) |
| 2 | **DISCRIMINATING: the quant costs something on reasoning** | incumbent `band R correct` minus challenger `band R correct` **>= 2** |
| 3 | the evidence band does not separate them | absolute difference in `band E correct` **<= 1** |
| 4 | the quant does not induce over-claiming | challenger `over_claim` **<= 1** of the 4 underspecified items |
| 5 | the graders hold | `format_error` **= 0** across all 48 items |
| 6 | the smaller file is faster to first token | challenger median `wall_s` **<** incumbent median `wall_s` |

### Registered decision rule, tie-break included

| observed | action |
|---|---|
| P2 holds | the quant costs measurable reasoning quality. Report the size saving as PAID FOR, not free |
| P2 fails and P3 holds - the arms are within 1 on both bands | **NOT equivalence.** Report as "no difference detected at n=24" with the Wilson interval, and run the SECOND BANK below before any recommendation |
| P1 fails | the incumbent did not reproduce. Nothing may be concluded about the challenger; audit the build and conditions first |
| any `format_error` | audit the grader before reading any score |

### The second bank, registered now so it is not a post-hoc choice

If P2 fails, run `tools/run_coding_eval.py --task-set core` (15 tasks) on both
arms, greedy, `--thinking medium`. **Registered in advance because "the null
was uninteresting so we went looking elsewhere" is exactly the move this
register exists to prevent.** Its scoring: challenger `pass` count minus
incumbent `pass` count, difference of **>= 3 of 15** counts as a detected
degradation.

### What this cannot establish

- **24 items cannot establish equivalence.** A null is "no difference
  detected", never "the same". Any report of a null quotes the Wilson interval
  and the n.
- **One quant of eight in that repo.** IQ3_S-mtp is the variant the community
  report named and the largest of the four recipes; IQ2_XS may behave entirely
  differently and is not tested.
- **Nothing about the MTP head.** The `-mtp` file carries one; it is not
  enabled at serve time here, so this compares weights, not speculative decode.


## E103 PRE-REGISTRATION - is ThinkingCap-Qwen3.6-27B a better `smart` slot than our incumbent? (2026-09-04)

### Why this experiment exists

| | |
|---|---|
| **which success question** | production serving - this is a same-footprint drop-in for the `smart` slot |
| **uncertainty reduced** | whether a different base model at the same size and quant does the knowledge work better AND terminates more reliably |
| **decision that changes** | whether `tools/e94/models-asym.ini`'s `smart` entry should be proposed for change to sparkrouter |

### Provenance of the hypothesis

The same community report behind E101 ranks `ThinkingCap-Qwen3.6-27B-Q4_K_M-MTP`
**first of nine** builds tried, above every Qwen3.8-27B quant, for "everyday
tasks and long agentic work", citing less looping and less wasted deliberation.
Reported on an RTX 3090 Ti / Windows box at 50-65 tok/s. **The throughput figure
does not transfer to this hardware and is not tested.** What is tested is the
capability and termination claim, on our bank, against our incumbent.

### The pair

| | incumbent | challenger |
|---|---|---|
| file | `Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf` | `ThinkingCap-Qwen3.6-27B-Q4_K_M-MTP.gguf` |
| bytes | 16,810,714,336 | 16,810,713,408 |
| requantiser | - | protoLabsAI (third-party requant of bottlecapai's release) |

A 928-byte difference, which is metadata string length rather than tensors.
**Same footprint, so this is a model comparison and not a size/quality trade.**

### PROBED BEFORE ANY PREDICTION WAS WRITTEN (F124), and it reshaped the design

| fact | value | how obtained |
|---|---|---|
| sha256 | matches pinned LFS oid `0ba445d2...` | `fetch_hf_model.sh` on arrival |
| `general.architecture` | `qwen35` - **same as our incumbent** | GGUF header |
| `n_ctx_train` | 262,144 - **same as our incumbent** | GGUF header |
| `general.base_model.0` | **`Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B`** | GGUF header |
| `general.tags` | `token-efficient`, `efficient-thinking` | GGUF header |
| **`reasoning_effort` in chat template** | **ABSENT - 0 occurrences** | full template dump |

Two of these change the experiment.

**1. It is a different BASE MODEL, not a requant of ours.** Same architecture
family (`qwen35`) and identical tensor shapes - which is why the file lands 928
bytes from our incumbent at the same quant - but it declares `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B`
as its base against our Qwen3.8-27B. The near-identical size is architecture,
not lineage, and reading it as "the same weights renamed" would have been wrong.

**2. It has NO graded reasoning control, and that kills effort-matching.** Our
incumbent's template resolves `reasoning_effort` through `low`/`medium`/`xhigh`
(6 occurrences, `xhigh` 5, `medium` 2). ThinkingCap's has **zero**, carrying
only a binary `enable_thinking`. **Passing `--thinking low` to it would be
silently dropped** - the arm would run at its default while the result file
recorded `"thinking": "low"`, and the comparison would be a lie the output
format could not expose. This is F128's shape exactly, and it is why the probe
happened before the predictions rather than after a puzzling result.

**Consequence, stated rather than averaged away: the two arms are NOT
effort-matched, and cannot be.** Each model runs at the configuration it would
actually be SERVED at - our incumbent at the setting F71 established
(`medium`), ThinkingCap at its own default. That is the honest comparison for
the decision at hand ("should the `smart` slot change?") and it is NOT a
controlled comparison of the two model families. No claim below is a claim
about Qwen3.6 versus Qwen3.8 as such.

**A third fact, recorded because it bears on E101 rather than E103.** BOTH
GGUFs carry embedded sampling defaults: `general.sampling.temp = 1.0`,
`top_k = 20`, `top_p = 0.95`. That is precisely the config the community report
uses - so those settings are the models' own published recommendations, not
something the reporter invented. **Every eval in this repo, and production,
runs at `temperature 0`, overriding them.** E101 is therefore measuring the
gap between how these models are shipped and how we serve them.

### The two arms

| arm | instrument | config | comparator |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A capability** | `run_ps_eval.py --tier l5`, 24 items | `-c 16384`, `--server-extra '-fa on'`, model default effort | the E102 incumbent run, same session, same quiet GPU |
| **B termination + efficiency** | `run_coding_eval.py --task-set core --only <the six E101 tasks>`, greedy | `-c 16384`, `--max-tokens 8192`, no `-fa` (matching E101 Amendment 1) | **E101 cell 1** - same six tasks, same greedy payload, same build |

Arm B is greedy so it compares against a banked cell rather than a fresh one.
The sampled looping question was answered for the incumbent in E101 and is not
re-opened here.

**Before either arm: an inertness control.** Send one prompt to ThinkingCap with
`reasoning_effort: low` and one with nothing, and compare completion tokens. The
template says the parameter is absent; the control proves the SERVER drops it
rather than erroring or partially honouring it. **Equal token counts confirm
inertness - they do not mean the model is efficient.** If the request instead
FAILS, that is a different fact and arm A's config changes.

### Predictions, each naming the FIELD it is scored against

| # | prediction | scored against |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `reasoning_effort` is inert on this model | control: completion tokens with `low` vs with nothing differ by **< 5%**, and neither request errors |
| 1 | the challenger is competitive on evidence work | challenger `band E correct` **>= 10** of 12 |
| 2 | **DISCRIMINATING: it does NOT beat the incumbent on reasoning** | challenger `band R correct` minus E102 incumbent `band R correct` **<= 0** |
| 3 | the report's termination claim shows up | challenger arm-B `truncated` **<=** E101 cell 1's `truncated` (which was **0**) |
| 4 | **the token-efficiency claim is real** | challenger arm-B total `completion_tokens` **< 11,194** - the sum E101 cell 1 spent on the same six tasks |
| 5 | it produces parseable code | arm B `no_code` **= 0** of 6 |
| 6 | the graders hold | arm A `format_error` **= 0** across 24 |

**P3 is a hard prediction to pass and is registered knowing that.** E101 cell 1
truncated **zero** of six, so the challenger can only tie, never win. That is
stated now rather than discovered later: on this instrument the termination
claim has no room to show a benefit, and P4 - tokens spent - is where a
token-efficiency finetune can actually demonstrate something.

P2 keeps the unflattering direction. The incumbent scores **11/12** on band R
(E78), close to the ceiling.

### Registered decision rule

| observed | action |
|---|---|
| P0 FAILS (the parameter is not inert) | STOP. The probe's reading of the template is wrong, and every config assumption in this entry is re-derived before any arm runs |
| P2 FALSIFIED (challenger beats band R) | a real result. Re-run BOTH arms with fresh seeds before any recommendation - one 24-item bank does not move production |
| P2 holds and P1 holds and P4 holds | **comparable capability for fewer tokens.** That is a genuine reason to consider the swap even without a capability win, and it is reported as an efficiency result, not a quality one |
| P2 holds and P4 FAILS | no capability win and no efficiency win. Report "no reason to switch" plainly |
| P1 fails (band E < 10) | the challenger is worse at evidence work; report the community ranking as NOT REPRODUCED on this bank and stop |
| the model does not load | that is the finding. Report it; do not manufacture a capability number |

### What this cannot establish

- **One bank, 24 items, one run per arm.** No claim of superiority survives that alone.
- **The arms are not effort-matched and cannot be**, for the reason above. Any
  difference measured here includes that asymmetry and is not attributable to
  the weights alone.
- **A third-party requant.** Any finding names protoLabsAI, because the MTP head is theirs.
- **Nothing about their box or their 50-65 tok/s.** Different GPU, OS and build.


## E101 RESULT - the sampler fix is real and SECOND-ORDER; the effort default is the whole problem. PREDICTION 5 FALSIFIED. (2026-09-04)

Five cells, 78 generations, 402 minutes, quiet GPU (Rule 9 SATISFIED - the relay
window was open throughout, so **these wall times are valid, not void**).
Kernel `7.0.0-29-generic`, build `b10435`, no flash attention (Amendment 1).

| cell | n | pass | truncated | tokens | wall | pass rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c1 greedy, `medium` | 6 | 6 | **0** | 11,194 | 15.4m | 100% |
| c2 sampled min-p 0.00, `medium` | 18 | 18 | **0** | 36,588 | 50.2m | 100% |
| c3 sampled min-p 0.05, `medium` | 18 | 18 | **0** | 42,648 | 58.6m | 100% |
| **c4 min-p 0.00, `xhigh` (THEIR CONFIG)** | 18 | 7 | **11** | **109,547** | 150.5m | **39%** |
| **c5 min-p 0.05, `xhigh` (THEIR FIX)** | 18 | 10 | **8** | 93,270 | 128.2m | **56%** |

### THE ANSWER

> **`min-p` works, and it is worth about a quarter of what the effort setting is
> worth.** Adding `min-p 0.05` at maximum effort removes 3 runaways of 18.
> Dropping the effort from `xhigh` to `medium`, at the same sampler, removes
> **all 11**. The reported fix is real - and it is aimed at the smaller term.

At `medium` effort the failure does not exist to be fixed: **42 of 42
generations completed correctly**, greedy and sampled alike, and `min-p` changed
nothing because there was nothing to change. It cost 17% more tokens (42,648 vs
36,588) for that null.

### Scoring - the six predictions

| # | prediction | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | cell 4 truncated >= 6 of 18 | **HELD** - 11 |
| 2 | cell5 - cell4 <= -3 | **HELD** - exactly -3 (8 vs 11), at the registered boundary |
| 3 | **HEADLINE: effort beats the sampler** | **HELD** - effort -11, min-p -3 |
| 4 | F71 reproduces on the greedy control | **HELD** - both tasks pass |
| 5 | repetition meter tracks non-termination | **FALSIFIED** - 3.2 vs 3.1, ratio 1.03 |
| 6 | transport_failed + no_code = 0 | **HELD** - 0 of 78 |

**P2 held at exactly its registered boundary (-3, threshold <= -3).** A single
run landing on the threshold is the weakest possible pass and is reported as
such: three replicates at n=18 cannot separate "worth 3" from "worth 1" or
"worth 5". The DIRECTION is what this licenses, not the magnitude.

### P5 is the finding, and it falsifies the word "looping"

The registered prediction was that truncated generations would repeat
themselves ~3x more than passing ones. **They do not repeat at all.** Mean
`max_ngram_rep` is 3.2 on truncated items against 3.1 on passing ones - a ratio
of 1.03 - and `max_line_run` is 1 across all 78 generations. In cell 4 the
single highest repetition score in the cell belongs to a generation that
**passed**.

So the failure mode is **non-convergent deliberation, not degenerate
repetition**. The model reasons coherently and never decides to stop. This
matters operationally rather than semantically: `min-p`, `repeat-penalty`,
`presence-penalty` and `top-k` all act on the repetition mechanism, and the
thing consuming the budget here is not that mechanism. It explains both why the
reported fix helps a little (it perturbs sampling enough to reach a stop
sometimes) and why it cannot help much.

### Which tasks run away, and it is not uniform

Truncations by task, cell 4 (3 seeds): `roman_roundtrip` 3/3, `word_break` 3/3,
`eval_expr` 3/3, `normalize_path` 1/3, `min_window` 1/3, `longest_valid_parens`
0/3. Cell 5 removes `normalize_path` and `min_window` entirely and one
`roman_roundtrip`. **Three of six tasks run away every single time at `xhigh`
regardless of sampler**, which is where the residual 8 truncations live.

### Registered decision rule - which branch fired

Registered: *"P2 holds and P3 holds -> min-p is a real but secondary lever.
Recommend it only alongside `medium`, and say so in the same sentence."*

That is the branch. **The actionable line is unchanged from F71 and is not
`min-p`: serve this model with `reasoning_effort: medium` set EXPLICITLY.** The
default is the setting that fails. `min-p 0.05` may be added on top; on this
evidence it is worth roughly a quarter as much and costs tokens where the
failure is already absent.

### What this does NOT establish

- **Nothing about their box.** Different GPU, OS and build. Non-transfer of the
  magnitude is expected; only the mechanism is portable.
- **The `medium` cells cannot distinguish min-p settings at all** - both are at
  ceiling. P2's estimate comes entirely from the `xhigh` cells.
- **One model, one quant, six tasks.** The three always-runaway tasks carry most
  of the effect and a different task set would move the numbers.
- **Nothing about MTP, which is off throughout.**


## E102 RESULT - the 3-bit quant is indistinguishable from Q4_K_M on this bank, 4.7 GiB smaller and 34% faster. PREDICTION 2 FALSIFIED. (2026-09-04)

Two arms, 24 items, tier `l5`, `-c 16384`, `-fa on` (passed explicitly and
verified in the server command line), `--thinking low`, quiet GPU, build
`b10435`, kernel `7.0.0-29-generic`.

| arm | total | band R | band E | only miss | median/item | on disk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M` | 23/24 | 11/12 | 12/12 | `R09` off_by_calendar | 40.93s | 15.66 GiB |
| `Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S-mtp` | 23/24 | 11/12 | 12/12 | `R09` off_by_calendar | **26.90s** | **11.29 GiB** |

**Separation: zero points on both bands, and the same single failing item.**

### The incumbent reproduced E78 ITEM FOR ITEM, which is what licenses the comparison

F117's requirement. Both files re-graded through `tools/score_l5_bands.py` in
one invocation, so the ruler is identical on both sides:

| run | date | total | band R | band E | miss |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E78 `l5-pilot-qwen38` | 2026-08-28 | 23/24 | 11/12 | 12/12 | `R09` |
| E102 `e102-incumbent-q4km` | 2026-09-04 | 23/24 | 11/12 | 12/12 | `R09` |

The scorer surfaced why the RAW files disagree: E78 banked `R09` as `wrong` and
the current grader re-grades it to `off_by_calendar`. **Comparing banked
outcomes would have manufactured a difference that does not exist** - which is
the defect the re-grading behaviour was built for.

⚠️ **The item this turns on is a known coin-flip.** E82 measured `R09` as one of
four items whose verdict is NOT stable across prompt orders (`correct` /
`off_by_calendar`). Reproducing it exactly is reassuring and is NOT proof of
determinism.

### Scoring

| # | prediction | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | incumbent total >= 21 of 24 | **HELD** - 23, and item-identical to E78 |
| 2 | **DISCRIMINATING: quant costs >= 2 on band R** | **FALSIFIED** - 0 |
| 3 | band E differs by <= 1 | **HELD** - 0 |
| 4 | challenger `over_claim` <= 1 of 4 | **HELD** - 0 |
| 5 | `format_error` = 0 across 48 | **HELD** - 0 |
| 6 | challenger median wall < incumbent median wall | **HELD** - 26.90s vs 40.93s, **34% faster** |

### Registered decision rule - which branch fired, and what it forbids

Registered: *"P2 fails and P3 holds - the arms are within 1 on both bands ->
**NOT equivalence.** Report as 'no difference detected at n=24' with the Wilson
interval, and run the SECOND BANK before any recommendation."*

**That is the branch, and the second bank is running.** It was registered before
this null appeared, so following it to a different instrument is not a post-hoc
choice.

**No difference detected at n=24.** Both arms 23/24; the interval on a 23/24
proportion is wide and 24 items cannot establish equivalence. **A tie here is
not a finding that the quant is as good - it is a finding that this bank cannot
tell.** See E103, where the same bank also failed to separate a different base
model, and F142.

### What is NOT claimed

- **Not equivalence.** See above; the second bank exists because of it.
- **One quant of eight in that repo.** IQ2_XS may behave entirely differently.
- **Nothing about the MTP head**, which is present in the file and not enabled.
- **The speed figure is real and separately measured**: 26.90s vs 40.93s median
  over 24 items on a quiet GPU. Unlike E78's, these wall times are valid.


## E103 RESULT - ThinkingCap is a better DEFAULT and a worse CEILING; the efficiency claim inverts on what you compare against. PREDICTION 4 FALSIFIED. (2026-09-04)

Two arms plus a control, quiet GPU, build `b10435`. **The arms are NOT
effort-matched and cannot be** (the model has no graded reasoning control); each
ran at the configuration it would actually be served at.

### Arm A - L5 capability

| arm | total | band R | band E | miss | median/item |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| incumbent (E102) | 23/24 | 11/12 | 12/12 | `R09` | 40.93s |
| GSQ-RCO IQ3_S (E102) | 23/24 | 11/12 | 12/12 | `R09` | 26.90s |
| **ThinkingCap-Qwen3.6-27B** | **23/24** | **11/12** | **12/12** | **`R09`** | **78.12s** |

**Three models, zero separation, the same failing item.** This is the E102 null
repeated against a different BASE MODEL, and together the two results retire the
bank for model comparison - recorded as F142.

### Arm B - the token-efficiency claim, and why its sign depends on the comparator

Six coding tasks, greedy, same payload as E101 cell 1.

| config | pass | tokens |
|---|---|---|
| incumbent at `medium` (TUNED, F71's line) | 6/6 | **11,194** |
| **ThinkingCap at its own default** | **6/6** | **20,437** |
| incumbent at its own default (`xhigh`, sampled, E101 c4) | 7/18 | **36,515** per run |

**Against our TUNED incumbent, ThinkingCap costs 83% more tokens for the same
perfect score - P4 FALSIFIED. Against our incumbent's own DEFAULT, it costs 44%
fewer and passes 6/6 against 39%.**

Both statements are true and they are about different questions. The
`efficient-thinking` tag is earned: **ThinkingCap does not need an effort dial
because its default is already sane; ours needs one and fails badly without it.**
A user who never finds `reasoning_effort: medium` would rank ThinkingCap far
above Qwen3.8-27B - which is exactly what the community report does, and it is
defensible from that starting point.

⚠️ **The third row is not a clean comparator**: E101 cell 4 is SAMPLED
(temp 1.0) where arm B is greedy. A greedy-at-`xhigh` incumbent cell was never
run. The 36,515 figure carries a sampling difference and is quoted as
directional, not as a matched arm.

### Scoring

| # | prediction | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `reasoning_effort` is inert | **HELD, but on a DEGENERATE control** - see below |
| 1 | challenger band E >= 10 of 12 | **HELD** - 12 |
| 2 | **DISCRIMINATING: does not beat incumbent on band R** | **HELD** - tie at 11/12, difference 0 |
| 3 | challenger truncated <= incumbent cell 1 | **HELD** - 0 vs 0, and registered in advance as untieable-upward |
| 4 | **challenger tokens < 11,194** | **FALSIFIED** - 20,437, 83% more |
| 5 | arm B `no_code` = 0 | **HELD** - 0 |
| 6 | arm A `format_error` = 0 | **HELD** - 0 |

### P0's control was degenerate, and the pass is withdrawn as EVIDENCE

The control reported `relative difference 0.000%` from `completion_tokens`
2048 vs 2048 - with `finish_reason=length` on **both**. Two generations that hit
the cap have equal token counts **by construction**, so the comparison could not
have detected an effect had there been one. It is an equality test over a
saturated measure, the same shape as E101's C1 passing on two identical
3-character failures earlier the same day.

**The design decision does not depend on it and stands**: the chat template
carries ZERO occurrences of `reasoning_effort` against the incumbent's six, and
that evidence is independent. What is withdrawn is the claim that P0 PROVED it.
`tools/e103_p0_control.py` now detects the saturated case and falls back to
byte-comparing the generated text.

✅ **CORRECTED RE-RUN DONE (2026-09-05 04:33, quiet GPU, E104 having finished at
04:32:26).** Both generations terminated NORMALLY this time - `finish=stop` at
**4,202 completion tokens each**, not truncated by any cap - and the counts are
identical to 0.000%. At temperature 0 that is a real equality on a measure that
was free to differ. **P0 now HOLDS on evidence that could have falsified it**,
and the design decision it supports (each model at its own default; arms
declared not effort-matched) is confirmed rather than merely unrefuted.
Evidence: `results/raw/e103/p0-control-CORRECTED.txt`.

### The recommendation

**Do NOT swap the `smart` slot to ThinkingCap.** At the configuration we
actually serve, our incumbent does the same work for 45% of the tokens, and
ThinkingCap has no effort control with which to close that gap. It was also the
slowest of the three arms on arm A. It is a better model to hand someone who
will not tune it - which is not our situation.

### What is NOT claimed

- **The arms are not effort-matched.** Every number here includes that asymmetry.
- **Arm A measured nothing**, because the bank is saturated (F142). "Matches the
  incumbent on capability" is a statement about the ruler.
- **A third-party requant** (protoLabsAI, of bottlecapai's release); the MTP head
  is theirs and was not enabled.
- **Nothing about their box, OS, build, or their reported 50-65 tok/s.**

## E104 RESULT - the bank with headroom separates the three models by SIX points, and the quant recommendation INVERTS. PREDICTION 3 FALSIFIED. (2026-09-05)

Three arms, 8 expert tasks, `-c 32768`, `--max-tokens 24576`, build `b10435`,
kernel `7.0.0-29-generic`, quiet GPU throughout.

| task | incumbent | quant | ThinkingCap |
|---|---|---|---|

### THE ANSWER

> **Every model spent the same tokens. They differ by six of eight.** The three
> arms consumed 74,796, 75,307 and 77,861 completion tokens - within 4% of each
> other - and scored 7, 4 and 1. This is not a budget effect, a truncation
> effect or a configuration effect. It is capability, and three other banks
> could not see any of it.

### The control reproduced ACROSS A KERNEL BOUNDARY

| run | kernel | date | pass | only failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E42 | `7.0.0-28` | 2026-08-15 | 7/8 | `sliding_median` |
| E104 | `7.0.0-29` | 2026-09-05 | **7/8** | **`sliding_median`** |

Same score, same failing item, three weeks and a kernel bump apart. F57 makes
the kernel a live bench variable that `results/` does not record, so this was a
real risk. **P1 HELD**, and it is what licenses the two challenger comparisons.

### Scoring

| # | prediction | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | control >= 6 of 8 AND `sliding_median` among failures | **HELD** - 7/8, `sliding_median` is the only failure |
| 2 | **DISCRIMINATING: bank not saturated, spread >= 2** | **HELD** - spread of **6** |
| 3 | quant does not degrade (gap <= 1) | **FALSIFIED** - gap of **3** |
| 4 | ThinkingCap <= incumbent | **HELD** - 1 vs 7 |
| 5 | ThinkingCap costs more tokens | **HELD** - 77,861 vs 74,796 |
| 6 | `transport_failed` + `no_code` = 0 | **HELD** - 0; all 12 failures are genuine `wrong_answer` (9) or `error` (3) |

### The registered branch, and what it forbids

Registered: *"P2 holds and P3 FAILS -> the quant degrades where it counts. The
L5 tie was the bank's blindness, not equivalence. Recommend AGAINST the swap and
say the earlier null was uninformative."*

**That is the branch. Recommendation: do NOT swap the `smart` slot to
GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, and do NOT swap it to ThinkingCap.** The incumbent survives both
challenges.

### The same three models, on four banks

| bank | incumbent | quant | ThinkingCap | spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L5 knowledge (24) | 23/24 | 23/24 | 23/24 | **0** |
| coding core (15) | 15/15 | 14/15 | - | 1 |
| coding core, 6-task subset | 6/6 | - | 6/6 | 0 |
| **expert (8)** | **7/8** | **4/8** | **1/8** | **6** |

**The instrument decided the conclusion, not the models.** Three banks said "no
difference detected" about a pair that differ by three of eight. Had E102 been
the last word - a tie, 34% faster, 4.7 GiB smaller - the defensible-looking move
was to propose the swap, and it would have been wrong. The only thing that
prevented it was the pre-registered rule requiring a second bank before any
recommendation, written before the null appeared.

### What is NOT claimed

- **Eight items, one run per arm.** The 7/4/1 ordering is clear; the exact gaps
  are not bounded at n=8 and no interval is quoted because one run cannot supply
  one.
- **The arms are not effort-matched** (ThinkingCap has no dial, F143). Its 1/8
  includes that asymmetry - though it spent MORE tokens than the incumbent, so
  the result is not explained by under-thinking.
- **One quant of eight** in the ISTA repo; **one third-party requant** for
  ThinkingCap, MTP head not enabled.
- **`sliding_median` fails for all three** and is the tier's hardest item; it

## E105 PRE-REGISTRATION - is Q4_K_M leaving capability on the table? The top of the quant ladder (2026-09-05)

**Registered before the model has finished downloading.** `results/raw/e105`
does not exist and no Q8_0 generation has been read.

### Why this experiment exists

E104 established the bottom of the ladder: `GSQ-RCO IQ3_S` scores **4/8** where
`Q4_K_M` scores **7/8**, for the same tokens. **That answers "does going down
cost?" and says nothing about "does going up buy?"** - and the second question
is the one with a production consequence, because this box has 128 GiB and a
27 GiB Q8_0 fits resident where a 24 GiB-VRAM box could never hold it.

| | |
|---|---|
| **which success question** | production serving - whether the `smart` slot is under-quantised |
| **uncertainty reduced** | whether Q4_K_M is at the flat part of the quant curve or below it |
| **decision that changes** | if Q8_0 beats Q4_K_M on a discriminating bank, the `smart` slot should go UP, not stay |

### Provenance

Raised by a second community report running **INT8 W8A8** on an A40 and calling
it "the GOAT". **That stack is not testable here** - vLLM is not viable on
gfx1151 (F48), `compressed-tensors` W8A8 is not a GGUF format, and FLASHINFER is
CUDA-only. Q8_0 GGUF is the nearest thing this box can actually serve, and the
question it answers - *is 8-bit better than 4-bit here* - is the transferable
part of that report.

### The artefact

- `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF`, revision `4ca720788d1e01f1bff70c033e0d0028fd02e502`
- `Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0.gguf`, **29,047,086,048 bytes**
- oid `a680f44a06920e5d689774823782006aa3acc8db95750323373b24139b67e348`
- licence apache-2.0. Verified on arrival before use; manifest entry precedes
  first use.

### The instrument, and why only this one

`--task-set expert`, 8 tasks, `-c 32768 --max-tokens 24576 --thinking medium`,
build `b10435`, quiet GPU. **Matched exactly to E104.**

**The saturated banks are deliberately NOT run.** L5 gave 23/24 to three
different models and the coding core gave the incumbent 15/15 (F142, F145);
adding a fourth arm to either would produce a tie that means nothing, and
running them to report "no difference" would be manufacturing reassurance.

**The comparator is E104's incumbent arm, not a fresh one.** It ran hours ago in
this session, same build, same kernel, same quiet GPU, same config - and it
reproduced E42 across a kernel boundary. Re-running it would cost 1h45m to
re-measure a control that already reproduced twice.

### Predictions, each naming the FIELD it is scored against

| # | prediction | scored against |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **HEADLINE: Q8_0 does NOT beat Q4_K_M** | Q8_0 `pass` minus E104 incumbent `pass` (7) **<= 0** |
| 2 | Q8_0 is not WORSE either - the curve is flat above Q4 | Q8_0 `pass` **>= 6 of 8** |
| 3 | `sliding_median` fails at Q8_0 too - it is a capability limit, not a quantisation artefact | Q8_0 `sliding_median` outcome is not `pass` |
| 4 | the ladder is monotonic where it moves | Q8_0 `pass` **>=** IQ3_S `pass` (4) |
| 5 | 8-bit weights cost throughput | Q8_0 `wall_s` **>** E104 incumbent's 6,206s |
| 6 | the harness holds | `transport_failed` + `no_code` **= 0** |

**P1 is the prediction with a production consequence and it is registered in the
direction that costs us nothing to be wrong about.** If it is FALSIFIED - Q8_0
scores 8/8 - then Q4_K_M is below the knee of the curve and we are serving a
weaker model than the box can hold, which is a finding worth having.

### Registered decision rule

| observed | action |
|---|---|
| P1 holds and P2 holds (Q8_0 is 6 or 7) | **the curve is flat from Q4 to Q8.** Q4_K_M is the right operating point; the 11.4 GiB saving over Q8_0 is free. No production change |
| **P1 FALSIFIED (Q8_0 = 8/8)** | Q4_K_M is under-quantised for this box. **Re-run BOTH arms before any proposal** - a one-item difference on n=8 is not a production case - and only then take it to sparkrouter as a proposal (F39) |
| P2 fails (Q8_0 <= 5) | a Q8_0 scoring below Q4_K_M is a surprise that indicts the RUN, not the quant. Audit the build, the file and the config before recording anything |
| P4 fails (Q8_0 < IQ3_S) | the ladder is non-monotonic, which would mean the bank is measuring noise at n=8. Nothing may be concluded from E104 either, and both are re-run |

### ⏸ PAUSED 2026-09-05 06:00, BEFORE producing any result

**Owner decision: paused to give the temperature work the GPU sooner.** The arm
had run 28 minutes of an expected ~105 and **wrote no result file**; nothing was
measured, so there is nothing to report and nothing to discard. This is not a
failed run and must not be read as one.

**Resuming costs nothing but GPU time.** The artefact is downloaded, byte- and
sha256-verified against the pinned oid, entered in the manifest before first
use, and this registration is committed - so the predictions above stand
unread and unscored. Re-run:

    bash <scratch>/run_e105.sh <pid-to-wait-on>

or invoke `tools/run_coding_eval.py` directly with the config named above.

**The comparator does not decay**, which is what makes the pause cheap: E104's
incumbent arm is banked at 7/8 from this same session, same build, same kernel,
same config. A future E105 compares against it without re-running it, provided
the kernel has not moved again (F57).

### What this cannot establish

- **One run per arm on 8 items.** A single-point difference is inside what n=8
  cannot resolve, which is why P1's falsification branch demands a re-run rather
  than a proposal.
- **Nothing about INT8 W8A8**, which is a different format on different hardware
  with a different kernel path. Q8_0 GGUF is not that, and no claim here
  transfers to it.
- **Nothing about MTP**, off throughout.
- `sliding_median` has failed for every arm tested and contributes no
